dialogs.content: Mr. Joshua... As you saw in the mirage, I wasn't at the record store with him.
Nor was I at the theater for more practice as I had said.
I came here instead, standing in the spot where I am now.
With this piano score in my hands.
Joshua would often stay next to large areas of water whenever he composed piano pieces.
He would close his eyes, with a very peaceful smile on his face. He said he listens to the symphony of winds and water.
I volunteered to be his assistant at the time.
I became famous at a young age, so famous to a point where everyone praised that I was a musical genius which only appears once every hundred years.
I cherished my title of a genius, but I didn't let go of my efforts, so inevitably I became successful.
But I knew that no matter how talented I am, or how hard I practiced, there will always be a behemoth looking down at me, and a plethora of leading musicians that I cannot surpass at the time.
So I volunteered to become Joshua's assistant. I hope to stand next to his side and learn from him at every moment. Thinking that one day I'll be able to surpass him.
Ha. You're quite perceptive for your age aren't you?
That's right, the more impatient I am, the more I feel inferior to him.
How does he keep his composure all the time?
Why the casual attitude?
Why does he always tell me to be calm and relax?
Why can he just listen to the sound of water and winds, and have expressions of so much enjoyment? And can't I?
After glossing over the piano score in my hands, looking at the dotted notes in his handwritings.
A sudden urge of emotions that I couldn't even define flowed into my head.
And I flung the score into the air with all my strength, turned my back and headed towards to the theater.
I made up my mind that after the performance, I would request a formal resignation to my mentor.
But then, halfway there, I heard a soul-shaking blare.
The eerie howls... ground-shaking boomings of the theater collapsing... and the screams of people running for their lives...
I was caught between the fleeing crowds, petrified as rescue workers dragged and pulled me away...
After I was taken to a safety area, I desperately searched for my mentor among the survivors...
So many years have passed, I know more than anyone that there was no chance Joshua could've survived.
Since then, I can no long play again, so I became a composer.
But when I saw that news, there's no doubt in my mind that his soul had made a return.
He was calling out to me.
Oh... Forgive me, it's just me getting old. Every time I think of the past, I always end up rattling on.
I apologize for dragging you along in this woeful story of mine.
I have to go back to the theater, with this music score, and finish the performance that was meant to be.

I didn't know at the time that the person who gave me the record at the record store was the maestro Joshua that my mother had admired so much.

How the student was sharp and more talented than even himself, and everyone will fall in love with him and his performance.
Then, out of nowhere, I heard strange noises above my head.
Mr. Joshua and I were the first to notice the noises. We looked up at the ceiling almost at the same time.
Before we knew... the sky came down on top of us.
Yes, it was... it was that monster.
It was still a time where knowledge of the TD's habits were limited, and the guidelines and restrictions placed on outdoor theater performances were not as strict as they are now.

dialogs.content: You look like you're interested in our training. I’m training a footwork unique to Liondance—the backflip!
Oh, I forgot to introduce myself. I am Xiuyi, a Liondancer at Liondance Troupe! I'm a peer of Lingyang.
Liondance is a dance style derived from martial arts. The postures and footworks often take root in traditional Huanglong martial arts, in which the backflip is an essential move.

Most of the time we practice it on Plum Blossom Poles at Central Plains. While I was in Jinzhou and the space was limited, I set up a temporary platform for the practice. It attracted a great audience to my surprise.
It has gradually become a major street recreation here, so I decided to open it to the public. Everyone can try to do the backflip, and I hope this boosts the popularity of Liondance.
Imagine the platform before you is a Plum Blossom Pole, and underneath it is a rushing, freezing stream.

Another lion confronts you, attempting to take your territory. Now, you have to drive it away, yet the space doesn't allow you to perform martial arts, so you have to depend on the footwork. After all, you don't want to soak your fur in the freezing water.

What you do is you <color=yellow>leap high</color> and Dash without a direction while you're airborne to perform an excellent backflip, which will not only blow away your opponent, but land you steadily on the Pole in one fell swoop.
To win my challenge, you have to successfully perform a number of backflips in a <color=yellow>limited time</color>. No "soaking", no help from any other items.
You wanna give it a try?
Perfect for beginners. Great introductory practice for every Liondancer. Get some warm-up and we'll start right away.
Looks like you've grasped something about the backflip. Brace yourself for a good challenge!

title: 剧情_支线_今州一日奇谈_1_2

dialogs.content: After arriving near Panhua's Restaurant, you message Chixia and wait for a moment...
Hey there, Rover! Finally found you! Hope I didn’t keep you waiting!
Ah, my bad! Let’s not dilly-dally any longer. Trust me, once we munch, you won’t wanna stop!
Aw, you’re too kind, but eating always comes first! Let’s dive straight into ordering and kick-start this feast!
Ah, well, look who’s here! Our little Xiaofang has brought a friend along today. How delightful!
No, no, no, Auntie Panhua, just forget that name! I’m begging you!
Yeah, exactly! Meet Rover, my awesome new friend! Today’s treat’s on me, so I brought {Male=him;Female=her} here to experience your culinary magic.
Oh dear, then I must show {Male=him;Female=her} something!
Any preferences or dislikes? Sweet, salty, sour, spicy, just let me know what you like. There’s always a Jinzhou cuisine for every taste!
Alright, something light... Find yourselves a spot inside. The dishes will be ready soon.
Before long, Panhua served up the dishes. The delicious pairing of sweet Candied Caltrops and slow-cooked Jinzhou Stew made you hungry.
Alright, something spicy... Find yourselves a spot inside. The dishes will be ready soon.
Before long, Panhua serves the dishes. The saucy Poached Chicken, complemented by the spicy and numbing Mapo Tofu, whets your appetite.

Hmm... The Candied Caltrops is fresh with just the right sweetness; the Poached Chicken sauce is Auntie Panhua’s original, unmatched anywhere else. Oh, and the Jinzhou Stew! It’s something you can only find here. I bet you’ve never tasted anything like it! Trust me, you don’t wanna miss out on this!
I’ve decided. Let’s get all of them.
We Patrollers don’t get paid a lot, but I love treating my friend to a feast once in a while. It’s just one meal, I won’t go broke!
To cater to all appetites, Auntie Panhua’s rolled out a small portion menu. Same fantastic flavors, just less food waste. So, no need to fret about over-ordering!
Alright, find yourselves a spot inside. The dishes will be ready soon.
Before long, Panhua served up the dishes. The delicious mix of Candied Caltrops, Poached Chicken in sauce, and Jinzhou Stew made your mouth water.
Rover, you enjoying the meal?
You got it! Next time, we’ll bring Yangyang and Baizhi along. Food’s always better with more pals, right? But what should we get then?
If you come next time, I’ll have to treat you to a taste of my famous Essence Medley Soup.
That’s all? Seriously? Not even Auntie Panhua’s culinary magic can shake you?
Looks like I’ll have to introduce you to the wonders of the Essence Medley Soup.
Something special? Hmm, give me some time to think.
In that case, I’ll have to introduce you to the wonders of the Essence Medley Soup.
Essence Medley Soup? What’s that?
It's brewed from the finest Jinzhou ingredients. Every essence is simmered and distilled into a single bowl. Some gourmets claim it's the epitome of Jinzhou's flavor, captured in a nutshell.
Even though I just polished off my plate, there’s always room for soup in my second stomach. Rover, fancy trying it out? Auntie Panhua, can you whip it up for us?
Whoa, did you hear that? Brewed from the finest Jinzhou ingredients! My taste buds are tingling already... Rover, fancy trying it out? Auntie Panhua, can you whip it up for us?

It's not that I'm unwilling to make it right now... In fact, it's an old wartime dish, a recipe lost to the ages. We keep it alive through word of mouth, preserving its memory. Now, about its taste, people have a lot of fun debates about it, but one thing's certain: it's like a warm, fresh hug, absolutely delightful and unforgettable.

However, while searching through old books, I stumbled upon its recipe. Though, calling it a recipe might be a stretch. See, back then, they used names for ingredients that are like riddles to us now. “Red beads,” “sweet roots,” “Monkvyrid,” “golden handle spoon”... I have no idea what they are.
Speaking of peculiar ingredients, it does remind me of someone...
Stop beating around the bush. Just tell me. I won’t take offense.
Well… it’s Uncle Mahe!
Hmph, he’s always bragging about how he can get any ingredient, but if he’s clueless about these, he’s just wasting his time in this business.
Just so we’re clear, I won’t go to him for answers, but if you want to give him a shot with this recipe, it’s your call.
Auntie Panhua! You’ve got the sweetest heart. I always knew it!
Alright, I’ll copy the recipe for you.
Don’t worry! I won’t let you do it for nothing! Auntie here will make sure you eat your fill!

I work for a magazine called Wutherium Geographic as a journalist with the Pioneer Association.
Our job is to take pictures and share the beauty of the world with people who can't travel.

dialogs.content: I've tried every way, but I can't persuade him. What should I do... Rover, you came at the right time. Help me think of a solution.
It's about my junior, Zhuyi. He recently joined the Pioneer Association and is now working as an intern photographer.
According to the regulations, new members are required to participate in the regular "Fireside Chats" to share and learn the history and culture of the Pioneer Association.

The recent adventure story was about the Icebreakers, who ventured into places far and between, like the distant polar oceans, the revived volcanoes, and the Great Rift Valley after the Lament occurred.
They reported about nature's warning signs that they spot around the world and became the first witnesses of countless powerful Tacet Discord.
After hearing these stories, Zhuyi suddenly became restless and applied to the Association to join the next expedition to the unchartered danger zones.
I'm worried that he's moving too fast and might make the mistakes I made before.
To be honest, when I was young, I was just as hotheaded as him. Always at the forefront of the team.
Later, in one of the missions, I rushed forward without properly surveying the terrain and accidentally fell into a cave.
As a result, I injured my thigh, and since then had to gradually retire from the field. Now I'm starting to think about transferring to support.
What if he makes my mistake again?
Rover, if you have a solution, you must tell me.

What brought you here? Picking up medicine for someone else, or feeling under the weather? Any injuries? Have you seen a doctor? Need any prescriptions?
Oh no, it’s just a habit I’ve picked up from running this pharmacy. Sometimes people struggle to describe their symptoms, so I ask a lot of questions to get a clearer picture.
Yeah... Hold up! Rover, what’s that supposed to mean? Obviously, I...
Obviously, just like this {Male=gentleman;Female=lady} said, once you get carried away, you forget your own safety!
Ms. Chixia, you’re the reigning champ on our pharmacy’s medication leaderboard. While I wholeheartedly appreciate your support, topping the charts won’t result in any discounts here.
Seriously, don’t you have work to do? Who keeps tabs on this stuff anyway!
Alright, let’s cut to the chase. {PlayerName} and I are here to get you to check out this recipe Auntie Panhua handed us.
Essence Medley Soup? I felt like I heard it from my grandmother or someone of her generation.
Really? C’mon, wrack your brain for it! Uncle Mahe thinks it’s more of a medicinal cuisine than a regular dish.

Let's see... Caltrops, Kudzu, Honeysuckles, a handful of Gemberries, and some pulled poultry breast. Simmer with water from the Monkvyrid. Once it's boiled, give it a stir with a golden-handled spoon... Water from the Monkvyrid? Isn't that the medicinal soup made from Coriolus, Perilla, and Lemongrass?

Who knew the medicinal soup could serve as a base... In a way, it leans towards medicinal cuisine. But with so many ingredients, wouldn’t it dilute the medicinal effect? There’s always something new to learn in dietary therapy.
No need to go through all that trouble. Remember where you are? A pharmacy! I’ve got some pre-made medicinal soup right here.
Good medicine often tastes bitter, so I've been thinking of ways to make it more palatable.
By making it into medicinal cuisine, we preserve its healing qualities while getting rid of the bitterness, so it’s enjoyable for everyone.
This recipe seems ancient. The Monkvyrid water is an old term from pharmacies, referring to that medicinal soup. Hold on, I’ve got the pre-made stuff for you.
Oh, and here are some new recovery and synthesis potions. Consider them a bonus.
But even with potions to treat your injuries, stay safe out there, alright? Always keep your guard up when exploring.
Don’t be like Chixia, just barging in and scaring everyone.
Are you for real right now? My reputation as the Jinzhou Speedster is...
I-I had no other choice! How can I remember all those safety rules when there are bad guys coming at me? They’d only slow me down... Okay, okay, next time, I’ll watch out!
So, are you two heading back to help Auntie Panhua with this Essence Medley Soup? If so, count me in on learning that recipe too!
Just let Auntie Panhua know. It should be cool for you to join in!
But there's still one last piece of the puzzle to crack: the golden-handled spoon. If we whip up the soup without figuring out what that is about, the flavor might not hit the mark, right?
Wait, isn’t the golden handle spoon that big pyrite spoon from Uncle Wei’s shop? I thought you both knew.
Seriously? No way! Who’d have guessed that!
Oops, looks like I gotta step down from my role as the Jinzhou encyclopedia. I’ve never even heard of that pyrite spoon!
Haha, no worries. I spotted that spoon the last time I dropped off medicine at Uncle Wei’s and asked out of curiosity.
Why does the best weapon maker in Jinzhou have a big pyrite spoon tucked away? Well, I’m counting on you to solve that mystery, along with the last step of the recipe.

Everything you see, from the shield over our heads to the high-precision instruments deployed on every street, are the work of the people who came before us.
I wonder when I will be able to catch up with them, especially Senior Taoqi!

I am wondering if Taoqi's "slow response" is deliberate.

Maybe there is some truth to it. My brain usually comes alive only after the sun sets.
Sometimes a complete new idea defense setup would just come to me after dark.
It's difficult to set up a defense that's watertight all around. I'm constantly put in a dilemma where I put heavy forces in one place and expose ourselves in another place.
But if I leave a deliberate opening in the setup to guide the enemy's attack in another direction, you'd be more targeted and prepared in your defense.
Hehe, my idea is not bad, right? This theory is not only limited to Jinzhou. It can also be extended to other places.

Brother Bai, I'm back again. I have a new idea about the Tacetite weapons. You must hear me out this time.
You mentioned before that the Resonators can activate the energy in the Tacetite and convert it into a new form they can control.
That's why the Tacetite weapons are so compatible with the Resonators, even though all current Tacetite weapons use only a small chunk of Tacetite in the core module.
So, if we could process the Tacetite into raw materials for other components, the "Tacetite content" of the entire weapon would increase dramatically!
They say that a quantitative change can lead to a qualitative change. Maybe a weapon like this can deliver a fatal blow to the Tacet Discord.

As long as it's a day-to-day thing found around the house, I can always fix them when you come to me.

He has been watching me repair these things since he was a child, and perhaps he has memorized the steps just by watching.
Sometimes, I have to read an instruction manual for some of the more complex items customers bring in, but he'd be able to understand and start dismantling the structure in a few minutes.
Once I caught him completely disassembling an item to its last gear. I panicked so hard as I thought there had been no way to restore it. But he put it back together in moments like it was brand new.
He also fixed those things. So, I let him do his things from then on. Later, he became increasingly more sophisticated with it.
Maybe one day he can become a great inventor. And I'll be known as the father of a great inventor.

Let's cut to the chase, “Madam Magistrate.” I'm getting bored already.
Very well. You will answer only our questions from now on.
Sure, why not. What do you want to know?
A <ano=Oracle Engine>Sentinel</ano> such as Jué can predict and "correct" future events. It gets in our way of achieving our sublime vision.
We merely wanted to topple the set future built on lies, and take control of our own destiny.
The Threnodians... They hold the key to our ideal.
Together they will bring us the promised "true Lament," and we will embrace the new world that is bound to come.
What is the Lament? Disaster? Curse? Some kind of punishment? Ha! People only see the surface...
The Lament brings death, destruction, and countless Reverberations.
Reverberations that will be reflected, overlapped, and interwoven during the Lament... They will be our salvation, the only path to a new lifeform and a new civilization.
Our goal has always been the same... We want you. Want you to join us.
Forces battle over you, causing all this strife, and yet you remain unaware of your own worth... Are you really that naive, or are you just dense?
Whatever. Our interest in you is not affected by such trivial matters.
Too bad. We will then be forced to kill you, by any means necessary...
But I'm sure you'll willingly come to us... When the time arrives.
You kidnapped Jué and revived the Threnodian, accelerating the next Lament... This is proof enough that you are the enemy of Jinzhou, and all humanity.

Yes, Madam Magistrate.
I will be going on a temporary leave. During my absence, please help me handle my responsibilities in Jinzhou.

No need. Both Changli and I will be away, and there'll be more than enough paperwork for you to handle.
Is Lady Changli leaving for the capital?
Please pardon my intrusion, but {Male=he;Female=she} just faced an ambush in the Central Plains. What if...
Regarding that incident... We tried to warn {Male=him;Female=her} about the Fractsidus, but they were more cunning than we thought.
If {Male=he;Female=she} runs into another powerful enemy like Scar, {Male=he;Female=she}'ll eventually have to confront them on {Male=his;Female=her} own.
Sanhua, you can place more trust in Rover and me.
Understood. I will.
My lady... No matter what happens, my sword is always yours.
Both the interrogation and my appointed meeting with Rover have already finished.
Scar only needed the two of you as his audience. We already knew what he wanted, and we let him have as much.
{Male=He;Female=She} decrypted every message we intended to convey. It's only proper you meet {Male=him;Female=her} in person, as the one who crafted those puzzles.
Such intricate puzzles... I guess only Rover has the patience to solve them all.
No detail is too small. I'm sure {Male=he;Female=she} understands. Besides... Not seeing the opponent heightens the thrill of the game.
If everything goes according to the prophecies of Jué, I will meet {Male=him;Female=her} in person eventually.
So... What did our captive from the Fractsidus tell you about Jué?
...That Jué had predicted I will have to fight it one day. A fight that will shape Jinzhou's future.
Well, that is... unexpected. But you don't seem all that surprised, do you?
Can't say I am. I had suspected as much from our previous conversations, and the message it left me... His words only confirmed it.
Where was it when you last sensed its presence?
It was... In Mt. Firmament. Unlike Jinzhou city, that mountain is still resting in "stillness."
The place where the first people of Jinzhou lived, and where Jué first manifested before us humans... I see.
I'll find Jué and bring it back as soon as possible.
Our enemies could have planned it as a trap. We have a bigger goal to focus on, remember?
I understand. I will not let anything or anyone disrupt the peace in Jinzhou.
Would you let what you heard from Scar sway your determination?

dialogs.content: How to resolve the disputes?
Yes, the dispute about the deployment of the new technology has been escalating recently, and I'm worried that the workplace party next week will turn into a chaos.
New technologies always meet resistance at the start. Because it's not only about technology, but also about people behind it.
The old miners represent experience and skills from the old times, and the young miners are the promoters of new technology.
As more and more young miners join in, these dynamics are thrown off balance. So the conflict was set off.
As for me... I'm not one of the miners, but a Patroller who carries out the duties as required.
The concerns or reasons for disagreements aren't as many as they appear to be. I think it's natural for things to iterate and evolve, isn't it?
Just like the law of physics we all learn in textbooks: the entropy of a system is bound to increase over time. And the systems of the world aren't isolated.
So as they recombined, they'd return to a low entropy state before the entropy rises again.
Isn't this the law of the world?

dialogs.content: Little lambs cowered and huddled in their village, terrified of the relentless wolf packs.
Until a shepherd arrived, bearing the gift of wishes and providing shelter and sustenance.
Slowly, the shepherd gained control over the flock, and the lambs lived contented lives... but this is not the end of our story.
The shepherd found the solitary black lamb in his flock, and offered to grant any wish it desired. In exchange, he wanted one of its companions as a sacrifice.
The black lamb refused, and it was shunned by its flock, left without shelter or sustenance.
After the black lamb's exile, more lambs continued to vanish...
The shepherd then blamed that black lamb for breaking the rules, and withheld his wish-granting power as punishment.
From the very beginning, the lambs knew the risk of making wishes—they too could become sacrifices for those of others.
But they always believed it wouldn't be them.
Meanwhile, some lambs reasoned that since they had already risked being sacrificed for someone else's wish...
It was then only fair to pass on that risk for a chance at fulfilling their own desires. And so, they continued to play the game.
They all knew the consequences, but chose to remain silent.
Fearful yet greedy, they followed the shepherd's orders and made wishes again and again...
Until one day a brave black lamb spoke up, shattering their façade of a peaceful and happy life.
The black lamb got in their way and the shepherd's greedy pursuit, sparking hatred in their hearts.
Suddenly, they could no longer ignore the blood and ashes of past sacrifices littering the ground.
Little lambs cowered and huddled in their village, terrified of the relentless wolf packs.

After the black lamb's exile, more lambs continued to vanish...
The shepherd then blamed that black lamb for breaking the rules, and withheld his wish-granting power as punishment.
From the very beginning, the lambs knew the risk of making wishes—they too could become sacrifices for those of others.

Behind the twists and turns of the gloomy plots is a pursuit of romantic ideals.
I have always suspected that there are real horror stories around me, just between you and me.
To think of something ominous might lurk in the darkness under the cold industrial surface of this jungle of steel and bolts... Phew... I've got goose bumps.

I see busy couriers rushing on the road, Pioneer Association members going on expeditions, and workers returning to Jinzhou to visit their families...
At moments like this, I'd see how our efforts have maintained the peace and order of this city.
It makes me feel cool.

Pistols are compact firearms that use Resonance Energy to create powerful bullet projectiles.

Additionally, Rectifiers can scan and interfere with the unique frequencies of Tacet Discords. As a type of Tacetite Weapon, Rectifiers test the user's skills.
Swords are a staple weapon for Resonators like you, with their balanced and agile design.

Allow me to introduce Konglin, leader of the ranged units team.
And this is Yuehui. He's in charge of the infantry team.
This is a topographic map of the Norfall Barrens.
The Ovathrax's power limits our reach. Outrider scouts can't go beyond the Norfall Barrens and Valley junction.
The deepest we ventured was three years ago, when we discovered the Suspended Ruins in its hinterland.

On the other hand, our enemies must take the same route if they want to attack us.
With the Ovathrax reorganizing their frequencies and bringing them back, we will face endless waves of attacks.
Every time we cut down an enemy, it gains more power.
Time is of the essence. We cannot afford a prolonged battle.
We must swiftly and safely get our strongest units in the heart of the battlefield, reach that statue, and take down Ovathrax in time.
Rover, let's plan carefully and use each team's strengths to our advantage.
First, our ranged units. Armed with long-range weapons, they can strike from a distance.
But we need to strategize based on the terrain, topography, and enemy forces.
If we manipulate the terrain to our advantage, their strikes will be more effective and cover a larger range.
Where should we deploy the ranged units?
Deploying our ranged units high above the valleys in advance...
(Our main battlefield will be at the valley's bottom, where space and vision are limited.)
(Placing ranged units behind infantry can slow their aim, making it counterproductive... This may not be the best strategy.)
(Mixing ranged and infantry units may seem versatile, but it wastes the advantage of ranged units... This may not be the best strategy.)
This way, they'll provide cover for our close-combat forces while staying safe themselves. We'll use their range advantage to the fullest. It's a smart move.
Next, the infantry. They have been trained and equipped for close combat.
The heart of Norfall Valley is our main battleground, where we'll fight our enemies head-on. We need to plan our attack wisely.
How should the infantry engage enemy targets?
Now that the narrow terrain has dictated an inevitable confrontation...
(We could divert some forces to flank the enemy, disrupting their formation and gaining an edge...)
(However, a successful outflank requires a wide battlefield, but the small passage of Norfall Barrens limits our options for movement.)
(And we can't predict everything that will happen on the battlefield… Our diversion could leave our frontline vulnerable. It may not be the best strategy.)
(To infiltrate enemy lines, a small group of our forces will enter through gaps in their formation and attack from the rear.)
(This maneuver takes time and requires caution to avoid detection, particularly in a valley where evasion is difficult.)
(Small infiltration forces may stay hidden but risk being overwhelmed by enemy attacks. Alternatively, diverting forces could lead to losing on the main front.
(We have little knowledge of what's happening behind enemy lines... Better not act rashly. This may not be the best strategy.)
The infantry will attack head-on, breaking their line. Then our task force can strike where they're vulnerable... A reasonable choice.
Lastly, the special task force, all Resonators with powerful abilities. They have superior mobility and combat skills.
If the chance arises, they will be responsible for taking down the Ovathrax.
What should the special task force do?
We'll join our effort to break through their defenses and crush their source of power. This is the only way to completely rout the enemies.
It's a risky but necessary move under our current circumstances.
(Hmm... flank tactics aim to avoid direct confrontation and exploit enemy weaknesses to take them down slowly.)
(However, our combat power could be drained by the endless enemy assaults if we don't eliminate the Ovathrax in time.)
We can't afford to prolong engagement… There may be more effective tactics available.)
(We could split into two groups to cover each other during our mission. It could increase safety and efficiency.)
(But if we further split up our small team of four, we risk getting outmatched in extreme situations.)
(Also, finding cover for everyone may prove difficult during an intense fight.
(Perhaps we should consider other options... There may be more effective tactics available.)
Thank you, Rover. The battle plan is clear.
I will now recap our plan:
Konglin, your team will take the cliffs for fire support.
Yuehui, your team will charge enemy lines to pave way for the special task force.

Rover, do you see that iridescent veil?
That's the Groundwave Barrier. Ovathrax set it up to absorb weapon frequencies in the Norfall Barrens without interruption.
One of our top priorities now is to protect the Disruptor from Tacet Discord attacks.
It's a powerful anti-Threnodian weapon from when Jinzhou was founded. We need it to break through this barrier.
I'll leave it to the professional to explain the details.

How's the preparation going on your side?
We've got good news and bad news. Good news is, we've established connection to the Disruptor and we're ready to go.
Bad news is, the Disruptor’s electric capacitor is damaged.
Simply put, it’s out of power.
Fortunately, there should be a backup power outlet.
To use the Disruptor, we'll have to repair that outlet first, then wait for a full charge.
Any questions?
In theory, we could. In practice, it's difficult.
First, it could dodge our attack. Not even a perfect hit can kill it. It will be gravely injured, but not dead.

No matter how fast I build it... Jinzhou won't be able to hold out that long.

dialogs.content: Do you know why there are names engraved on the abandoned turrets here?
Many years ago, the battlefield was filled with smoke as the Jinzhou Garrison regiment fought bravely and successfully pushed back the TD tide, reclaiming a small portion of the front line.
In those times, the majority of soldiers were ordinary people, and the demands of war were such that not everyone who departed left something behind.
Engraving the names of fallen comrades onto stone monuments might just be a way of commemorating their sacrifice and creating a sense of unity.
The group then devised a method to engrave the names of the deceased soldiers onto the turrets and continue the tradition.
The engravings here are their names.
I didn’t know any of them, but my grandpa said them so many times that I just remembered them all!
When I was a kid, he barely mentioned his war experiences. Lately, he has become increasingly forgetful and tends to reminisce about his younger days.
Grandpa was probably scared of forgetting, so he wanted other people to remember in his place.
Anyway, I’ve heard it a million times and can’t forget it even if I tried, and even if Grandpa forgets, I’ll remember it for a few more decades.
I can recite the names engraved on the monument backwards now.
Look, this is Shenyin, he’s nicknamed the Divine Eagle because of his incredible marksmanship.

He stuck to the front line with his gun for two whole days so that the others could retreat without harm. When he eventually returned to rescue him, he discovered that his leg had been shattered, he had lost a significant amount of blood, and yet he had managed to stay in his firing position until his last breath.
This is... Little Bean, she doesn’t have a name, that’s what everyone calls her.
She died as the first one to rush out and pull the alarm when the TD wave suddenly erupted, getting the TD’s attention and giving the others a chance to react.
Do you still want to hear more?
This one is Yuandong... next to this one is Beimo...
Yuandong was a military doctor, and when the TD wave broke out, he died fighting without any medical support.
Beimo was discovered in a cave-in after a week-long battle, and he rescued around twelve soldiers from starving to death beneath the sealed ground.
Here is Ziyu, and this is Xiaohua...
Do you still want to hear more?
Well, then I’ll stay here a little longer.

Apologies, I haven't even introduced myself yet...

Hero...? It's not as grand as that. It started by trying to help children fulfill their wishes.
However... I do hope you can keep that between us.
Imagine how disheartening it would be for people to learn their wishes were granted by a single person.
I just want to do something within my power to pass on the joy we've all felt at least once in our lives.
Thank you for understanding, {PlayerName}.
Seeing everyone's wishes come true and everyone enjoying the festival is enough for me.

At first, I suspected an overload of Patty's analysis module due to an accumulation of wishes over the years.

It'll only be a matter of time before all the wishes stored in the Moontree Lodge are devoured by this abnormal code.
Xiangli Yao pulls out a tablet showing you four indecipherable files.
I've isolated the four wishes with unreadable codes, pinpointing the source of the discrepancies.
I plan to track down whoever made these wishes, try to fulfill them, and uncover the root cause of these anomalies.

Feasibility: 0%. Causing physical harm or manipulating human memories are actions strictly prohibited.
This is Xiang-LEE, Patty's work buddy. Patty gathers and analyzes the wishes, and Xiang-LEE helps make them become a reality.
Hmm... Xiang-LEE is the first prototype of its series, and we used to call it by its serial number.
My colleagues at the Academy began calling it Little Xiangli out of convenience, and over time, it became the name we use now...
Well, it seems to like this name a lot, so consider it... a birthday gift from everyone at the Academy.
You have a good eye, {PlayerName}. Xiang-LEE is indeed a very reliable companion.
Analysis Conclusion: The wish exhibits strong self-denial and self-destructive tendencies, indicating a high level of danger. Prompt physical care and psychological intervention are advised.
Patty does not understand. This wish. Patty does not. Cannot. Hurt humans.
Just as I've suspected. This is the reason why this wish failed to be interpreted. The desire to "disappear" directly conflicts with Patty's underlying logic of not being able to harm humans.
Written words are different from data. Data represent precise and unified content, while words may harbor meanings deeper than they seem on the surface.
It is often the case that words spoken aloud sometimes contradict our innermost thoughts.
Those willing to entrust their wishes to the Moontree Lodge hope their desires will be chosen and fulfilled. This suggests that Xiaosheng still hopes for his voice to be heard.
This is just my personal belief, but I suspect he's not truly ready to give up. I think the thought pains him.
Which means he's...

{PlayerName}, I want to uncover the true desire hidden in his wish and help him fulfill it.
Will fulfilling his "true wish" help to ease his suffering?
Yes. I hope it will.

Fortunately, we know that he's a researcher, so it shouldn't be too difficult for us to find him.

I'll decipher these codes, and then we can... Oh, excuse me...
Investigator Xiangli...! We have a problem! We've got trouble in the lab!
Prototype 49's core has gone out of control, emergency protocols failed, and it's overheating as we speak...
Lock down the lab. I'm on my way. What about the experiment logs?
Already sent to your Terminal, sir.
All right, tell everyone to stay calm. We still have time.
There's been a momentary setback in the research. I need to handle it right away.
I'm afraid I'll have to leave the task of finding Xiaosheng to you, {PlayerName}.
Thank you, I'll meet up with you as soon as I have the issue resolved. Here, take Xiang-LEE with you to help with the investigation.
I already have a few speculations as to the contents of the code. I'll call you once it's confirmed.
Good luck, my friend.

dialogs.content: A bunch of Exiles? What's there to fear?
We've been told to investigate. Don't rush in.
I say we storm in, and take 'em down. All of 'em.
H-Have you lost your mind? I'm not going with you!
A bunch of Exiles? What's there to fear?
We've been told to investigate. Don't rush in.
I say we storm in, and take 'em down. All of 'em.
H-Have you lost your mind? I'm not going with you!
I'm sorry. Though I do practice Taoism, geomancy and fortune-telling aren't my strong suit.
Moreover, this matter concerns chance, and you can't force it.
I see. Sigh, then I'll come up with something else.
That might be the best solution.
Oh, hi, {PlayerName}. It's nothing big. Uncle Dong asked me to help him decipher a divination lot, but… I'm not skilled in that art.
It's a long story. Although I know a bit of divination, I'm self-taught. So, I decided to find something to lend some credibility to my efforts.
Yeah. Long ago, a famous diviner visited Jinzhou, rumored to possess the gift of communicating with spirits and predicting destinies. People flocked to him for guidance.
His moon-reading skill was said to be exceptional. Uh, I guess you're not familiar with it, {PlayerName}.

You half fill a specially crafted porcelain bowl with pure water, recite an incantation, and observe the reflection of the full moon in the water to discern fortune and misfortune. That's the moon-reading divination.
When that diviner performed it, the water would emit a golden glow, adding a touch of mystery to the moon's reflection.
Unfortunately, no one knew where he went. It's said that when he left Jinzhou, he left a letter and a divination lot.
In the letter, he mentioned meeting a mysterious person in Jinzhou. After a deep conversation on divination, he felt his understanding was too shallow and lost interest in reading divination books.
Frustrated, he decided to give up his career, but he couldn't bear to part with the porcelain bowl that had accompanied him for years. So, he hid it somewhere in Jinzhou.
Then, he left a divination lot as a clue, hoping someone would find it one day.
That's right. Since the bowl belongs to that famous master, it must be great for divinations. So I want to have it on my stall and enhance my credibility.
Though I haven't heard of this divination master, Uncle Dong does have a point. In this line of work, possessing powerful artifacts does lend credibility to one's abilities.
I bet that master would be happy to see his treasure recognized by people again.
Oh, haha, I almost forgot our main business. It says, "To seek your true self, observe the lake at a deck. Place your trust in innocent young souls."
This lot doesn't seem related to fortune-telling, so I'm a bit confused. Any thoughts, {PlayerName}?
A deck where people can appreciate the lake… Do we have a place like that in Jinzhou?
I've been to several places that match the description. Found nothing so far. Perhaps the time wasn't right.
Anyway, as long as we have a clue, there's a way to find it! Uncle Dong, we'll help you find that porcelain bowl!
Great! I'll be sure to pay you a hefty sum! Best of luck, Jianxin, {PlayerName}!

Hello there, little girl.
Hi? How can I help you?
Something strange…? I come here a lot, but something strange...
Oh, yeah! The cats!
Cats…?
Yeah, that's right! There's a spot around here where cats love to stay.
Often saw them just sitting there, not moving at all. Mom said they're fishing in the lake but...
Cats… What's your take, {PlayerName}?
A-are you Patrollers?
A-are you bad people, then...?
Haha, of course not. We're here for a long-lost treasure.

I believe using it in the Plumpcake would elevate the flavor.
But it's rare and only grows where Tacet Discords roam, making it hard to come by.

Alright, I'll let you use my stove.

But these are said to only grow in the depths of Whining Aix's Mire, where many monsters live...
...On second thought, with {PlayerName} and Lady Sanhua, getting those seeds would be a breeze. Can't wait for your Plumpcake!

Onlookers pause to applaud her mastery in action.
Done. {PlayerName}, please give it a try.
How do you like it?
Thank you. I'm glad you like it.

This is for you, {PlayerName}.

Me? I don't need it. Eating cake isn't part of my duty.

Been tossing and turning all week. Can't switch off these thoughts at night... I can't take it any longer.
Been scrolling through the forums lately? There's this thing blowing up called "Nighttime Blues Syndrome" on the Huaxu Hive.
(Definition of noun: "Nighttime Blues Syndrome"—A popular term used to describe the state of today's youth that have lost their enthusiasm towards life due to excessive work and life stress.)
(Symptoms include avoiding social engagements, reluctance to work, insomnia, and signs of depression.)
(Further analysis reveals an 87% correlation between the syndrome's traits and the emotional state of "Xiaosheng," inferred from the wish made at the time.)

A few colleagues from other departments even used it as an excuse to ask for leave yesterday. They wrote, "The world is such a wonderful place, filled with different kinds of sadness to experience each day."
Eh...Lucky bastards. Taking time off whenever they want. And look at us, sweating bullets over research with no results in sight. How are we supposed to sleep?
Is that the latest thing? You know I don't usually visit those forums, but this term... Maybe it's because everyone's feeling the pressure lately.
Relax, take some time off. You can leave the rest of your work to me. Don't let it get into your head. Smile, and everything will be A-okay.
Hmph, you sure are optimistic at a time like this.
Anyway, I really need to pass out for a while. She's all yours.
With heavy steps, the researcher heads back inside the Academy.
Um. Hello... Were you listening to our conversation the whole time? Anything I can help you with?
Wait a second. It's you, isn't it...? The one who sucked in a Tacet Discord with your bare hands... {PlayerName}?!
I didn't expect to meet you at a place like this... Are you here for something? Is it about the monsters? Or maybe Ech... No, never mind...
..."Xiaosheng"? A pretty average name, if you ask me. But I've never heard of anyone with that name at the Academy. Can you... provide any extra information?
Uh, maybe I can help you find him.
Searching "Nighttime Blues Syndrome" and "Xiaosheng" as keywords. There are 417 relevant results found.
Search results consist of forum posts made under the username "Xiaosheng." Example result: "Another crappy day today..."
Wait a minute, analyzing someone's online behavior without their consent is a violation of robotics protocols!
Searching protocol... Confirmed. Violation of protocol detected... Xiangli, I'm sorry. Initiating self-destruct sequence...
Apologies.
Hahaha. Its creator gave it some good features. It's fine. But do you mind me asking... why are you looking for Xiaosheng in the first place?
This question involves the individual's privacy. We are unable to disclose any details to those not directly involved.
I understand... Speaking of which, this robot looks rather familiar. Could it be from the Moontree Lodge by any chance?
I see... I heard that making wishes at the Moontree Lodge tends to come true. I was thinking of trying it out myself at some point.
Ah, got it, got it.
Hmm... it's almost time to set up the centrifuge. I need to make my way back and check on the samples.
You notice Shifan appear a bit flustered for a moment, but he quickly returns to his easygoing and friendly demeanor, politely bidding you farewell.
No information was obtained regarding Xiaosheng's identity. Acquired new keyword.
Yes, we can always check the forums for any updates later.
Now then, let's try our luck somewhere else.

I must confess, the Academy's current research in this domain is rather limited.
If we are to approach it from this angle, I'm afraid I may not be able to help the boy much... At least before the Moonlit Fair arrives.
...I concur.

Courage, perseverance, and support from his companions were all indispensable elements.
Your idea of finding a real-life role model to show the boy a more grounded version of heroism... is indeed a viable approach.
So, have you decided who this hero should be?
A fine suggestion. I have always admired the Magistrate of Jinzhou.

The honorable Madam Jinhsi, our great magistrate of Jinzhou, was handpicked by Sentinel Jué. Her status as the Sentinel's Appointed Resonator is rare among all past magistrates.
Our Jinzhou was leaderless for years until Jué finally chose her to be the next Magistrate, and she answered the call.
To further elaborate, we must start with the "Battle Beneath the Crescent"...
The Norfall Barrens, scarred by countless wars... Discarded weapons scattered like bones.
Our soldiers had fought to reclaim the land for years, to no avail.
Ovathrax, the dreadful Threnodian monster, fed on the frequencies of "weapons" turning our fallen soldiers into deadly Tacet Discords...
General of the Midnight Rangers, Geshu Lin, bravely rose to confront the threat.
As twin moons aligned, General Geshu Lin vowed to vanquish evil, raising his blade against the blood-red crescent that foretold destruction.
His sword blazed with black flames, laying waste to all who dared stand in his way. Victory seemed certain...
...Until the Retroact Rain began to fall.
Raindrops fell upwards as in the past. Monsters raged, loyal souls fell to blood-soaked sands... Infernal carnage!
Issuing his last command, Geshu Lin demanded all soldiers stand firm, no matter what happened.
Sacrificing his body to the black flames for power, Geshu Lin charged at the Ovathrax with all his might... And he was never seen again.

After the fall of their leader, the remaining soldiers despaired... Until a deafening roar of the <ano=Teal Dragon>Qingloong</ano> struck like lightning. A lone youth bravely stood up to lead. A hard-won retreat!
After the battle, that young man who tamed the wind ascended to fame, becoming the new General of Midnight Rangers, selected by Sentinel Jué.
On the other hand, General Geshu was blamed for the massive losses that occurred under his command, earning him a notorious reputation in Huanglong...
That battle struck us hard, but our Sentinel rose from its long slumber to select a new Magistrate who guide us into the future.
Despite the previous disaster, Jinzhou was off to a promising start under our Sentinel and the new Magistrate's guidance. The people held hope for a better tomorrow...

content.content: Is this the effect of that strange time pattern you mentioned?

dialogs.content: Time on Mt. Firmament used to simply flow slower than in the outside world. Visitors were safe as long as they remained within the Temporal Barrier.
But what we're seeing now is different. The flow of time has gone haywire. This is what we call the Temporal Disruptions...
What was once slow and steady has become chaotic and turbulent. Some areas are frozen in time, while others speed up or slow down unpredictably.
No one knows how much they'll age after leaving Mt. Firmament, but aging from youth to old age may be a blessing compared to the unknown fate that awaits.
Leaving Mt. Firmament could turn any mortal to dust in just a moment. Such is the power of time within its walls.
These poor creatures, trapped in the Temporal Disruption, are the most pitiful of all... Their bodies and minds have been ravaged by the chaotic time, leaving them in unimaginable suffering...
So, it looks like the Fractsidus did manage to capture our Sentinel, leading to the Temporal Disruptions we are facing now.
I had wished that my theories would turn out wrong...
...As expected, my Terminal isn't working. We can't reach Jinhsi.
The Temporal Disruption is preventing it from functioning.
We can't waste a moment. Jinhsi's fate isn't the only one at stake—all the inhabitants of Mt. Firmament are in danger.
We need to hurry to Hongzhen, a town nestled at the heart of Mt. Firmament. Jinhsi would likely pass through there on her search for the Sentinel.
So it can't hurt me...

This crisis hit Hongzhen hard.
People were going about their day as usual, but then chaos erupted without warning. They didn't even have the time to escape.
Our town is made up of ordinary individuals, and we had no way to defend ourselves against the Temporal Disruptions.
Thanks to Magistrate Jinhsi, we didn't get too many casualties.
We understand our Sentinel is not to blame for what has transpired.
Jinzhou stands thanks to the Sentinel's never-faltering protection. It saved our ancestors from the Tacet Discords. Without the Sentinel, this land would be uninhabitable.
The current situation could be much worse without the Sentinel's aid. We are grateful for its help and can't expect anything more from it.
...As our Sentinel once protected the people of Mt. Firmament from Tacet Discords, it seems we'll need to rely on Magistrate Jinhsi this time.
Many outsiders are unaware, but in ancient times, a colossal vehicle descended upon Mt. Firmament alongside our Sentinel. This became the Mianloong Chamber as we know it today.
People in Hongzhen believe our Sentinel came from a faraway star and the chamber serves as its hibernation pod.
But with our limited technology, we still struggle to comprehend its workings.
Speaking of which... Our Sentinel's health is worsening. Lately, it has been spending longer periods of time in the Mianloong Chamber, essentially going back to "sleep" more frequently.
We've tried asking about it, but no response.
The defense mechanisms outside Mianloong Chamber were built by the Court of Savantae.
Back in the day, researchers from the Court of Savantae would often come to Mt. Firmament to study the strange time fluctuations. This caused tension with the locals.
Local people believed it was disrespectful to the Sentinel, especially when they tried to enter Mianloong Chamber.
After some deliberation, local people understood that the Court of Savantae posed no threat to the Sentinel.
A deal was struck: the locals would refrain from disrupting their research, and in return, they would build defense mechanisms to keep outsiders from interrupting the Sentinel's rest.
The Sentinel was believed to have agreed to this compromise by remaining silent during negotiations.
Activating the Cipher Key is a complex process, and we've stored the Mianloong Chamber's controller separately.
It's an extra safeguard. By splitting the key and its control panel, it'll be harder for malicious individuals to access them.
Long ago, the Sentinel protected people of Hongzhen from Tacet Discords, and it also revealed a harsh truth—
Leaving Mt. Firmament shortened one's lifespan exponentially. The longer someone has lived inside the Temporal Barrier, the less likely they can make it out alive.
Later, a group of brave young people who could afford the aging left Mt. Firmament, and they eventually built Jinzhou city.
Others stayed and worshiped the Sentinel as their god, vowing to protect it for generations and carving its likeness into the mountain.

Speaking of which... Our Sentinel's health is worsening. Lately, it has been spending longer periods of time in the Mianloong Chamber, essentially going back to "sleep" more frequently.
We've tried asking about it, but no response.
The defense mechanisms outside Mianloong Chamber were built by the Court of Savantae.
Back in the day, researchers from the Court of Savantae would often come to Mt. Firmament to study the strange time fluctuations. This caused tension with the locals.
Local people believed it was disrespectful to the Sentinel, especially when they tried to enter Mianloong Chamber.
After some deliberation, local people understood that the Court of Savantae posed no threat to the Sentinel.
A deal was struck: the locals would refrain from disrupting their research, and in return, they would build defense mechanisms to keep outsiders from interrupting the Sentinel's rest.
The Sentinel was believed to have agreed to this compromise by remaining silent during negotiations.
Activating the Cipher Key is a complex process, and we've stored the Mianloong Chamber's controller separately.
It's an extra safeguard. By splitting the key and its control panel, it'll be harder for malicious individuals to access them.
Long ago, the Sentinel protected people of Hongzhen from Tacet Discords, and it also revealed a harsh truth—
Leaving Mt. Firmament shortened one's lifespan exponentially. The longer someone has lived inside the Temporal Barrier, the less likely they can make it out alive.
Later, a group of brave young people who could afford the aging left Mt. Firmament, and they eventually built Jinzhou city.
Others stayed and worshiped the Sentinel as their god, vowing to protect it for generations and carving its likeness into the mountain.
I pray for your safe return. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have other responsibilities to attend to.
Did Xinyi and Jinhsi know each other?
Jinhsi was chosen as a baby for her Resonance Ability, and raised in City Hall to become the Sentinel's Appointed Resonator.
All the government workers there helped care for and teach her at some point, including Lady Xinyi.
She grew up with immense responsibilities, forced to suppress her true nature from a young age. Thinking back, Jinhsi was only a teenage girl when she became the Magistrate...
She has been burdened with unimaginable weight that most cannot fathom.

Changli was right. They used the Court of Savantae's research to trap our Sentinel in its resting chamber.
They used the Chronosorters.
Our captured Artificer revealed that the Fractsidus sent a death squad to invade Mt. Firmament. They had a two-fold plan…
First, to place the Chronosorter in the Mianloong Chamber while it was still operational; and second, to lure the Sentinel back to Mt. Firmament.

Although their death squad was no match for the Sentinel, by forcing its hand, the powerful Resonance Ability of the Sentinel would clash with the energy of the Chronosorter. This would ultimately cause harm to itself.
What if the Fractsidus modified those Chronosorters?
A whole bunch of them, pushed to their limits, all working together to deliver one massive blow.
But not even that was enough to take down the Sentinel.
After the first hit, they set up modified Flare Crests in the Mianloong Chamber to form a special force field along with those Chronosorters.
It prevented the Sentinel from replenishing energy and eventually restricted its movement and perception.
So... We must free the Sentinel from that force field first.
...It would be a task more complicated than it sounds.
The people of Hongzhen have lived with the Sentinel for generations. We can usually tell if it's in good shape or not.
But now, the Fractsidus want to capture the Sentinel... They won't just stop at Mt. Firmament. Madam Magistrate, I'm sure you didn't come here just for the Sentinel...
Please tell us what you know, Madam Magistrate.
Yes, I will tell you everything.

So the Sentinel is actually injured, and it's been getting worse... The Fractsidus attacked while it hasn't healed yet. Their plans are devious as always.
Madam Magistrate, you've already laid out this plan so far.

It's always a challenge to decipher the Sentinel's intentions, but there were many theories about it in City Hall at the time. I couldn't fathom why it went through such great lengths to retrieve you from Mt. Firmament and raise you within our walls.
But now that I reflect on it, perhaps the Sentinel saw in you the potential to one day restore the Temporal Program and ensure the survival of Jinzhou's inhabitants.
I just never thought.. You'd be willing to follow through with that prophecy…
It was here on this very mountain that I first encountered the Sentinel.
Back then, I was too young to remember anything. Even the image of Mt. Firmament has slipped from my mind.
But this time... As soon as I stood at the base of Mt. Firmament, I felt a wave of recognition wash over me. Memories long buried resurfaced with sudden clarity.
Lady Xinyi... I was born with my life, my everything connected to our Sentinel.
But my duty as its Appointed Resonator is not the only reason for my decision.
...I'm following the heart of my younger self before I became Jinhsi: The girl who used to laugh with pure joy as she felt the snow from Mt. Firmament on her face.
I am a seed, born on Mt. Firmament, carried by the wind to every corner of Jinzhou. But now, I have returned to my place of origin.
It's time for me to take root and grow into something greater...
Sigh... No matter what happens or what choices you make, please remember: the people of Hongzhen will always have your back.
Mt. Firmament has been stagnant for eternity. Perhaps a sudden crack of lightning is what we need to break through the fog of uncertainty that has lingered over us for far too long.

Jinhsi, it has been quite some time.
And greetings, {Male=Lord;Female=Lady} Arbiter. Or should one address you as "Rover" now?
One cannot discern the cause of your arrival, yet its significance heralds Jinzhou's fateful juncture.
Shall a "child" who has lost their memories take up arms and fight for their fate? Or shall they retreat to their cradle and slumber?
The seed of the future shall be sown in this very moment.
Once the situation settles, an explanation shall be provided. For now, one must implore you to simply engage, decide, and observe.
Jinhsi, your journey has been an arduous one. Aside from aiding one in this predicament, surely there are other inquiries you wish to make?
I cannot bring myself to ask for more. All I seek is the truth.
Mt. Firmament is in grave danger... Regarding the Temporal Mandate and your injuries... Please, do not keep the truth from me any longer.
One understands your concerns. The timing may not be optimal for this disclosure, yet in the midst of crisis, one must act with expedience.
For one will soon perish.
One such as this, of immortal nature, is designed to endure for all time.
Yet one suffered severe harm in ancient times, and now relies on the Mianloong Chamber for survival.
This is not the optimal solution.
For a long time, one has had to use this chamber to replenish energy, hoping to delay the inevitable doom.
Yet fate cannot be defied. The Fractsidus have conspired against this one. Now, the injury only worsens... The Mianloong Chamber can no longer prolong one's life.
Jinzhou... The city of Jinzhou will be no more.

Ever since one descended upon Mt. Firmament, using the power of Temporal Mandate to repel Tacet Discords, time has been in disarray within this location. The fate of Jinzhou was sealed from that moment on.
Over the past millenia, one has defied the laws of nature and sustained Jinzhou at the cost of one's own life force.

Otherwise, the Temporal Disruption would wreak havoc not only on Mt. Firmament, but on the entire region of Jinzhou. If this were to happen, all life will be engulfed in a chaotic storm of twisted time flow.

Jinzhou shall forever remain frozen in time. The past and the future meld into one, rendering life indistinguishable from death. The ceremonial rituals and endless battles persist, intertwining joy and sorrow into an eternal blur.
All inhabitants of Jinzhou shall endure this perpetual fate until time itself ceases to exist.
...It is this one's own doing, and one must put an end to it.
In the coming days, one will exert every ounce of strength to freeze the time in Jinzhou at the cost of one's remaining life.
In that moment, Jinzhou will fall into stillness, but not perish. In the distant future, the people of Huanglong may discover a method to rescue Jinzhou.
Is there truly nothing else we can do?
This is not the optimal solution, but it suffices as an option.
Please forgive me... but I cannot do as you say.
A decade, a century... What if nobody comes up with a solution? By that time, the world will have turned its back on this forgotten city...
...And who would be willing to spend precious resources rescuing a small city in a far-off corner of the world?
Jinzhou's fate deserves better than an uncertain future.
Whilst one may not live to witness the future, one can still envision endless possibilities yet to come. In my deduction, this method proves to be the most effective and stable.
Magistrate Jinhsi, as you express doubts, pray tell how do you propose to solve this issue?
The flow of time upon Mt. Firmament is in disarray, and it can only be contained through one's utmost effort.
If one does not freeze the time now, the situation in Jinzhou shall surely worsen a hundredfold, or even a thousandfold, after one's passing.
..You once predicted a destined battle between us... Is it true?
Correct.
...I was lost at first, struggling to grasp the prophecy's meaning. Only when I learned of your actions alongside the Court of Savantae did it all become clear—

By clashing two resonating powers, a Second Resonance Awakening can be induced. Through this, I am able to push my Resonance Ability beyond its limits and invoke the Temporal Mandate to restore the flow of time.
...Though I will be forced to raise my blade against you...
RIDICULOUS!
If you clash with my Resonance power, even the smallest mistake will result in Overclocking and leave you nothing but an empty husk.
You are well aware of its excruciating effects. The pain you feel now is but a faint scratch in comparison to its true torment.
Moreover, you will be trapped within the fissures of time itself. Your being will be relentlessly shredded and mended, day after day, denied any respite for eternity.
But I can restore the errors in the flow of time. Isn't that why you saved me all those years ago? I'm just doing what you've been doing all along... Going against fate to keep Jinzhou safe.
Jinhsi, you are given one last opportunity. Let me freeze the time, and I can ensure your safety.

There is little chance for you to retreat unscathed.
But I can at least win some hope for our people!
Even if it costs me my soul, my everything... I cannot die without trying.

dialogs.content: Yes... It's me.
I've lived in Jinzhou my whole life and never ventured into Hongzhen, yet even I know of the legend.
To me, Jué is more than just our Sentinel or a revered divine being... It raised me and saved me from certain death.
I've been thinking about it on our way here.
If the Sentinel predicted our fight, why would it even bother saving me in the first place?
Now I understand why. Because I am the Sentinel's Resonator. I may not have any extraordinary abilities, but I do possess the Temporal Program that it accidentally lost.
If Jinzhou ever faces a similar time crisis, I... I might be the only one who can set things right.
...In our Sentinel's prediction, the battle between us is supposed to happen in the distant future.
It had been waiting for an opportunity, a right moment to tell me the truth. That's why it didn't explain.
Now may not be the opportunity the Sentinel has been waiting for, but my body cannot hold up much longer...
I have to go and face it while I still can… to learn about the truth, or complete our destined battle.
Give up... my duty? I never thought about it...
To be honest... I did doubt myself many times.
It was the endless kindness of you, Changli, Xinyi, and everyone in Jinzhou that gave me the courage to push on.
Even Jué's decision to bring me back to life... Whether out of pity or not, I am truly grateful. The thought of it warms my heart every time.
Jinzhou holds everything that's dear to me. Even without the title of Magistrate, I could never leave Jinzhou behind.
I'm okay...
The pain I'm feeling is nothing compared to those trapped in the Temporal Disruptions.
I must find the Sentinel as soon as possible. We draw from the same source of power—saving it means saving myself.
If there is truly no other option in the end...
Then I will have to fight it. I refuse to back down.

If it means keeping everyone safe, then I have no regrets giving my own life.

We're not in a situation where death is our only option, are we?
Thank you for placing your trust in me.
Come to think of it, many good things have happened to me since you arrived in Jinzhou.

dialogs.content: Are you guys interested in Mt. Firmament tea?

I heard it took seven steps to make tea outside this mountain: preparing teaware, warming teaware, putting in the tea, brewing the tea, discarding the first batch, pouring the tea, and then serving the tea.
It's not much different from our local tradition, though we're a little more particular.
Just on warming the teaware alone, we don't use boiled water but a scoop of the Sagaci Springs water, heating it with the spring's natural heat.
The teaware would get an earthy aroma from the heat, so when you pour the tea, your nostrils are greeted with a scent as if the leaves were freshly plucked from the snow.
Here, I just made it with the premium Firmament snow tea leaves. Try it.

dialogs.content: Hello.
Yes? You are…? Oh, I see. You folks are here for the snow monster too?
Imagine a tank-sized ape, with the power to freeze everything around it into ice sculptures.
I saw it once as a kid, just a glimpse of its back while tagging along with my dad in the mountains.
(Sounds like a Tacet Discord with freezing abilities.)
So, how do you intend to find the snow monster this time?
This time? I never actually encountered it. If I had, I wouldn't have lived to tell the tale!
But, I did come across… evidence of its hunting.
Evidence of its hunting?
Okay, long story short.  I went hunting in the mountains and found some strange contraptions at the base of Loong’s Ridge.
I thought they were left by the Court of Savantae. No idea what they were for. You know, I haven't found anything related to the Court of Savantae there before.
Maybe they have a secret vault nearby?
That's what I thought. So I followed the contraptions trying to find it.
Did you find it?
Of course not. This is a tale about running into a snow monster,  not about a thief hitting the jackpot with a vault!
I trekked up the mountain and saw some... animals. Oh, not just any animals, there were Tacet Discords too.
Tacet Discords? They didn't attack you?
Nope. When I found them, they were all frozen solid.
Birds, deer, even the Tacet Discords—every one of them frozen stiff. You could see every hair crystal clear.
Can you believe it? Even the snowflakes around them were frozen. Gave me the creeps, I tell you.
So you think the snow monster did all this?
Who else would it be? What else could turn living creatures into those… terrifying ice sculptures?
I totally forgot about the vault and ran like the wind, terrified that the snow monster would jump out from nowhere and turn me into a popsicle like the rest of them.
Yes, why didn't I think of it sooner... The Court of Savantae must've sealed that monster with one of their contraptions, and someone let it out by mistake!
That explains everything! No wonder it's been centuries since the last time people saw the snow monster…
Hold up, didn't you say you saw it as a kid?
Did I? Ha… Hahaha, well, yes, besides ME, it's been centuries since anyone saw the snow monster!
Uh, wait! And my father! He saw it too.
Qianyue doesn't ask more questions, but the skeptical look on her face suffices to show her opinion.
By the way, if you're planning to hunt the snow monster, why not grab some of my poison arrows? They're made to take down wild beasts quickly.
Think about it. You'll be out there, staring down that snow monster, wishing you had something to defend yourself with. Trust me, you'll regret not taking these.
Smart move. Here. It took me years to craft these beauties.
But… they look just like regular arrows?
Hey, open your eyes! These are no ordinary arrows. The tips are poisoned. The one I used is colorless, odorless, safe for humans, but deadly to beasts!
…Well, maybe keep them to yourself for now.
Fine, your call. Just don’t say I didn’t warn you when the time comes.
Anyway, you're not the only ones curious about that snow monster. Excuse me, got another customer… adventurer to attend to.
The hunter leaves in a hurry, taking his deadly, invisible, and odorless poison arrows with him.
Well, I've got all that recorded. I'll sort through it later.
I can't help but feel… these two incidents aren't quite what I had pictured.
The herb collector didn't even get a clear look. From his description, sounds more like a rare Tacet Discord than a monster.
But the whimpering or howling he mentioned does pique my interest. If it was a Tacet Discord or a monster… why didn't it attack him?
That makes sense. Maybe a Tacet Discord got stuck in a trap or wedged in a crevice?
That makes sense. I've heard some Tacet Discords are friendly towards humans.
Hmm, now that could be the real story behind this "evil ghost."
As for the hunter, he gave a really detailed account.
If he were making it up, he wouldn't have included verifiable details like the creations of the Court of Savantae.
Which means the frozen animals are real. The Court of Savantae creations are real, but…
That's right! No snow monster, just a ruse to sell those poison arrows.
He did see the frozen animals, but he didn't know who did it and how.
Spreading rumors about the snow monster was just a way to lure in hunters.
Yeah, who froze those animals? Tacet Discords? Doesn't quite add up.
Something's off about these two sightings. Maybe we need to visit the locations for answers.

dialogs.content: Hello? Excuse me.
Yes…? You are…
Story…? It's not a story! It really happened to me!
I was almost killed on that mountain! Just the thought of it sends shivers down my spine, like it's still lurking out there, watching...
Look behind me, you don't see anything, do ya?
No…?
That's a relief. With so many people in Hongzhen, I bet that thing wouldn't dare show its face. But that place… I wouldn't set foot there again.
What do you mean by that place? Where is it?
Curiosity killed the cat, they say. Getting mixed up with that monster will only spell disaster. I must've lost my mind insisting on checking it out…
Madam Xinyi…? So, she heard the rumor too? Not surprising, she always takes everything here seriously.
Gathering tales…? I've heard those pages are filled with countless regional folktales, so it’s only natural you’d want to add this.
Alright, if you're here to listen, I'll tell you exactly what happened.
Hold on! Let me start the recording first… Alright, please go on.
It all began three days ago. I was deep in the mountains hunting for a rare herb and lost track of time.
By the time I stumbled upon the herb, night had fallen. Fearful of beasts prowling after dark, I decided to take a shortcut back to Hongzhen.
When I reached Loong's Crest, I heard some... strange noises coming from the darkness. They sounded like metal clashing and scraping, mixed with eerie cries.
I thought it was just a poor Scarefrost Deer caught in a trap, so I pressed on. But the deeper I went, the creepier it got.
What kind of noises?
Hard to describe. Whimpers? Howls? Whatever it was, it wasn't human, and it sure as hell wasn't any beast I'd ever crossed paths with.
More like a twisted combination of both.
The noises gave me goosebumps. Then I remembered the story my grandmother once told me.
Long ago, the Sentinel and the Court of Savantae worked together, using their bizzare creations to seal some real vicious monsters.
Their bodies crumbled to dust over the years, but their evil souls hung around, craving revenge on the Sentinel.
Revenge on the Sentinel? That's wild!
Ahem, I'm talking here, young lady. Interrupt again and I won't say another word.
Oh, I'm so sorry…
Where was I? Ah, yes, the evil souls. I was in a dilemma, you know. Terrified as I was, curiosity gnawed at me, urging me forward…
Suddenly, out of nowhere, two lanterns appeared in front of me. It happened so fast, I didn't even realize it was impossible to have lanterns out in the wilderness like that.
The lanterns seemed to float, barely visible. They flickered once, then a few seconds later, flickered again.
It wasn't until then that I realized they weren't lanterns at all, but eyes! Eyes as big as lanterns. How big would its head be?
I turned and ran, and that monster kept howling behind me. Believe me, I've never heard anything so bone-chilling.
I didn't dare look back, just ran for my life. I lost track of time, but eventually, I saw the lights of Hongzhen and knew I was safe.
I heard you passed out at Hongzhen's entrance, right? Thank goodness the night patrol found you. Otherwise…
Non-nonsense! I didn't pass out! Just… a bit tired from the running! Yeah, I was tired!
Anyway, whatever was chasing me must be the souls of those monsters! One wrong step, and I'd have been its next meal!
Alright, that's all been recorded. What's your take, Rover?
Yes, I agree. I've heard nerves can make you see things that aren't real. Maybe it was just a Scarefrost Deer... or a passing Tacet Discord?
If you're really curious, go see the monster for yourself. I spotted it near Loong's Crest. Just remember, I did warn you.

Alright, if you're here to listen, I'll tell you exactly what happened.
Hold on! Let me start the recording first… Alright, please go on.
It all began three days ago. I was deep in the mountains hunting for a rare herb and lost track of time.
By the time I stumbled upon the herb, night had fallen. Fearful of beasts prowling after dark, I decided to take a shortcut back to Hongzhen.
When I reached Loong's Crest, I heard some... strange noises coming from the darkness. They sounded like metal clashing and scraping, mixed with eerie cries.
I thought it was just a poor Scarefrost Deer caught in a trap, so I pressed on. But the deeper I went, the creepier it got.
What kind of noises?
Hard to describe. Whimpers? Howls? Whatever it was, it wasn't human, and it sure as hell wasn't any beast I'd ever crossed paths with.
More like a twisted combination of both.
The noises gave me goosebumps. Then I remembered the story my grandmother once told me.
Long ago, the Sentinel and the Court of Savantae worked together, using their bizzare creations to seal some real vicious monsters.
Their bodies crumbled to dust over the years, but their evil souls hung around, craving revenge on the Sentinel.
Revenge on the Sentinel? That's wild!
Ahem, I'm talking here, young lady. Interrupt again and I won't say another word.
Oh, I'm so sorry…
Where was I? Ah, yes, the evil souls. I was in a dilemma, you know. Terrified as I was, curiosity gnawed at me, urging me forward…
Suddenly, out of nowhere, two lanterns appeared in front of me. It happened so fast, I didn't even realize it was impossible to have lanterns out in the wilderness like that.
The lanterns seemed to float, barely visible. They flickered once, then a few seconds later, flickered again.
It wasn't until then that I realized they weren't lanterns at all, but eyes! Eyes as big as lanterns. How big would its head be?
I turned and ran, and that monster kept howling behind me. Believe me, I've never heard anything so bone-chilling.
I didn't dare look back, just ran for my life. I lost track of time, but eventually, I saw the lights of Hongzhen and knew I was safe.
I heard you passed out at Hongzhen's entrance, right? Thank goodness the night patrol found you. Otherwise…
Non-nonsense! I didn't pass out! Just… a bit tired from the running! Yeah, I was tired!
Anyway, whatever was chasing me must be the souls of those monsters! One wrong step, and I'd have been its next meal!
Alright, that's all been recorded. What's your take, Rover?
Yes, I agree. I've heard nerves can make you see things that aren't real. Maybe it was just a Scarefrost Deer... or a passing Tacet Discord?
If you're really curious, go see the monster for yourself. I spotted it near Loong's Crest. Just remember, I did warn you.
