And we've crossed paths with the Rover again! Can't get luckier than that!
We shouldn't have let {PlayerName} get caught up in this mess.
{Male=He;Female=She} was worried about us and insisted on coming.
Is that so? Then our gratitude to you is even greater for your timely aid, {PlayerName}.
To find the brightest truth, one must delve into the deepest shadows. Such bravery deserves to be hailed, my friend.
Where is everyone on the Pilgrim's Sail?
I was patrolling the coast earlier when I saw their ship drifting into the mist. Time was against us, so I departed alone without alerting the crew.
T-thank you.
Don't be afraid. You're safe with us. You've got some skill, you know, holding your own for so long in the trial against the Tacet Discords.
Trial? Ha, I don't buy into the Order's nonsense.
I've worked hard all my life and stayed true to the Order's teachings about forsaking earthly pleasures for divine favor. And what do I get in return? Heavier taxes.
When pirates ransacked my merchant fleet leaving me with nothing, I turned to the Order for help. They said it was a divine trial and left me to rot.
I stood before the Sentinel's statue, asking if my suffering was really Their will, but all I got was... silence.
Why should I wait for peace in the afterlife when I could be living for today? How is that a crime?
As for salvation... I don't believe in it, and I certainly don't need it.
Here's a proposal. How about joining our troupe?
We are wanderers adrift upon the seas. Or perhaps you're more familiar with the name—the Troupe of Fools.
The Troupe of Fools? Could it be...
Yes. We are, like you, by the Order's decree... marked as Fools.
Fools on the Pilgrim's Sail often meet their demise in a storm or they're swallowed by the waves... Even if they do survive, they still face hunger, thirst, and the unforgiving wrath of nature.
Maybe it's luck that brought you here so swiftly, and unharmed at that.
Look around. This is all that remains of the Pilgrim's Sail... This is always their final destination, where the Fools meet their end.
Yes. The pilgrimage is nothing but a banishment in disguise. The path to salvation they speak of doesn't exist.
Otherwise, how could this once sacred place now look like such a hellish wasteland?

Wait, sacred place? No wonder the others were talking about it on the ship. They believed the Order's promise that prayers at the Sacrificial Arena would grant them forgiveness... They must be heading up the mountain now.
I didn't expect their faith to lead them that far.
If only they knew it was just one of the Order's lies.
Captain! First mate! We're here to help!
More hands make light work. I called in some help to escort him back to the base once the mist cleared.
Ah, the first mate's foresight is unmatched! Then the three of us can head up the mountain.
But beware my friend, by the end of this pilgrimage, you will witness the Order's cruelest deceit. The dangers ahead will only intensify.
Please, save them... I hope it's not too late.
Don't worry. There's more to our troupe than you think.
This Wingray can fly us up the mountain.
You two go first. You'll find I'm very convenient to bring along.
Alright then... All hands, prepare to ascend!

dialogs.content: See? I wasn't lying!
Tacet Discords' frequencies are perpetually fading, inching toward their end.
Their only way to maintain their existence is to consume other frequencies as food.
The Dark Tide and mist enveloping this isle have drawn in countless Tacet Discords. Their frequencies should have been enough to feed the dragon.
If what you saw is true, then...
The Order must've used some trick to control the dragon, making its frequency fade away faster than it should.
That means they could be responsible for why the dragon began attacking all living beings, including humans...
In time, it ended up becoming a harbinger of death.
I found this during the previous battle.
It seems the Fractsidus had their hand in this case as well.
Mm? So you know them too. Seems we have much to discuss.
Our troupe usually earns a living by performing on the nearby islands. Sometimes, we take on escort missions for merchant ships as well. That's how we first got acquainted with the Fractsidus.
At first, they were just lurking about, raiding ships. But as the Carnevale drew near, their actions grew suspicious. We noticed them lingering around a certain sea.
Remember Cetus the Tidebreaker, the creature that attacked you when we first met?
After we parted ways, we went searching for it to find out what had gone wrong.
This is what we found on its tail... another Lycoris.
Alas, the Tidebreaker slipped away into the deep, beyond our reach. Still, this bloom leaves no doubt. The Fractsidus is behind its strange behavior.
We saw what they did to the dragon. The Cetus's violent outburst must be their doing as well.
They say the Carnevale is a ceremony to resonate with the Sentinel. Those who claim the Laurel may be graced with a miracle—a direct communion with the divine.
At first, we thought you were merely a curious traveler, intrigued by the Carnevale and our Sentinel. But now, seeing how far you've come, there's more to your quest, isn't there?
Our troupe has always sought the Laurel, and we won't sit back while others threaten the Carnevale. If they're your foes, then our paths align!
Remember I mentioned one of ours who once claimed the Laurel?
He wasn't with us when we first met. But once we reach our base, you can speak with him about the Sentinel.
It won't be long now. After such an adventure, a well-earned rest awaits.

dialogs.content: Here we are, ladies and gentlemen. Allow me to present to you our sanctuary, a haven for all the surviving Fools at the edge of the world.
It is, my friend. We built this base from the ground up, and I dare say it's a triumph worthy of the ages.

They say the most dangerous places are the safest. Penitent's End has always been forsaken, and now, cloaked in the sea of mist, even the Order's envoys wouldn't dare set foot here. It's the perfect refuge for us.
The mist does shield us from the Order, but it brings its own set of problems.
Precisely why we must tackle its effects without delay.
By the way, if you'd like to speak with Mr. Bardolino, our Laureate, you'll find his tent deep within the base.
Feel free to talk to the others while we handle our tasks. We'll catch up once we're done.

dialogs.content: First Mate! What should we do with these stage props?
Load the light boxes on the heavy suitcases. Place the lights on top and secure them with chains. Keep the fireworks well away from the curtains.
And don't forget to check the freshwater reserves and all cabin doors.
Roger!
Usually, the crew handles these jobs themselves.
But since we're prepping for the Carnevale and working on stage setups, it's fair they ask for my advice.
Here, the role of captain is best suited to someone who can ease the newcomers' fears and worries.
Brant is a natural. As for me, I'm more comfortable managing these kinds of tasks.
There, there. Don't be afraid...
The frequencies mixed in the mist are unsettling Lario. I'm trying to calm it down so the crew can board.
Wanna give it a try? Just place your hand on its forehead and channel your Resonance Energy, like this...
*Soft, reassured noises*
You really are special... The Echoes here are naturally drawn to you.
Echoes can sense and respond to human frequencies. They reflect how we treat them, for better or worse.
They're like reflections of who we each are.
I've heard Lario's scientific name is Pliosaurus Somnii, an incredible creature first seen in the dream of its discoverer.
It used to escort our ships across the seas, and then, of its own accord, became our stage. It has braved countless storms with us.
Throughout our many travels, we've never found another like it.
It must've been lonely, after so many years alone, drifting... That's why it chose to sail with us.
When I was young, much younger than I am now, I performed in a play that was banned by the Order.
And... that was it. I was sent here with all the other performers.
The play was about freedom, love, and hope. How could something so beautiful be considered taboo? I... I don't understand.

dialogs.content: Welcome back, Brant! I... I heard a lot of voices coming from the mist. It's scary...
Don't be afraid, Morrias. They're all friends from the troupe, people we've sailed with.
You said you want to be a captain, right?
Sailing has its own trials—sea monsters, storms, whirlpools, undercurrents, you name it. When such challenges arise, you've got to trust your helm and your crew.
They'll stand by you through thick and thin, and your job is to guide them safely through it all, till you reach the journey's end.
I understand... Everyone has been so good to me, always looking out for me. When I grow up, I'll be a great captain and take care of them too!
That's the spirit, kiddo! You've already got the heart of a captain, and that's no small feat. You're the captain of your own ship!
Bravery like that deserves rewards. Here, take this.
Wow, Captain Sparrow's Legends! Thanks, Brant!
And... can I maybe have a sip of the stuff you like to drink? The Troupe Strength?
Ah, well... Ahem! That's a special brew for captains who've faced the fiercest storms. When you're ready, your own glass of Troupe Strength will be waiting.
Really? I'll work for it!
It's a drink made of Waterlamps, fermented, distilled, and aged to perfection. Not for young ones, of course.
We brew it ourselves, each of us with our preferred strength. It's not worth much, but it's one of the few pleasures we can have here…
As the captain, it's my duty to be the crew's compass. This face must not show any fear or sorrow.
This isle is fraught with hidden threats. Many who were banished never made it to join us, claimed by the Tacet Discords. Their Reverberations became part of the mist...
Those who did make it have their own dreams to chase.
Some will eventually leave to follow the call of their hearts, their silhouettes forever etched into the mist.
We hope they find their promised lands. The troupe may be a safe harbor, but it's certainly not the final destination of their journey.
We honor their names and stories in our plays, passing their legacy down through the crew.
Beriarti the Fire Eater, Toscanini the Night Watcher, Fernando the Fish Killer... Their stories remain vivid in my memory. One day, I'll compile them into a book. Mark my words.
Over the years, we've bid farewell to many and welcomed countless new faces... It seems this cycle will never end.

When I was a boy, I saw the Sentinel's statue in the Cathedral of Mercury. Curiosity led me to point at the statue and ask, "How can you say it's the Sentinel when no one has ever laid eyes on it?" I didn't know the consequences that would follow.
That question earned me a pilgrimage. At the time, I thought it was some grand adventure.
On the Pilgrim's Sail, I was cared for by other Fools who shared what little they had and shielded me from the grim reality with their kindness and smiles.
But all I could do was watch... as they passed away, one by one. From that day forward, I swore to wipe away the tears of the innocent.
Every adventurer needs a rest, and every ship must find a port. For us, that meant finding a sanctuary.

When we finally reached this forsaken isle, the destination of our pilgrimage, we fought the Tacet Discords to claim our territory and scavenged what we could from the ship's wreckage. From that, we built all this...
Though the night may be long, the dawn always follows! That, my friend, is what we should set our sights on.
Welcome back, Brant! I... I heard a lot of voices coming from the mist. It's scary...
Don't be afraid, Morrias. They're all friends from the troupe, people we've sailed with.
You said you want to be a captain, right?
Sailing has its own trials—sea monsters, storms, whirlpools, undercurrents, you name it. When such challenges arise, you've got to trust your helm and your crew.
They'll stand by you through thick and thin, and your job is to guide them safely through it all, till you reach the journey's end.
I understand... Everyone has been so good to me, always looking out for me. When I grow up, I'll be a great captain and take care of them too!
That's the spirit, kiddo! You've already got the heart of a captain, and that's no small feat. You're the captain of your own ship!
Bravery like that deserves rewards. Here, take this.
Wow, Captain Sparrow's Legends! Thanks, Brant!
And... can I maybe have a sip of the stuff you like to drink? The Troupe Strength?
Ah, well... Ahem! That's a special brew for captains who've faced the fiercest storms. When you're ready, your own glass of Troupe Strength will be waiting.
Really? I'll work for it!

dialogs.content: Arragh!
Ha! Eat this!
Who are you? A new recruit? Can't you see we're trying to have a fistfighting contest here? Back in the day, a brawl like this was the pride of the streets!
People from every district used to gather on a certain bridge over the river. And first one to toss their opponent into the water got the bridge and the bragging rights.
The victors were hailed as champions, their names sung in the streets. They earned titles and glory beyond measure.
It's a shame the Order banned it. What was their excuse again? Oh, right—"breaking solidarity among citizens."
It's madness! A good brawl was a way to blow off steam and ease some of the hostility between the people before it grew into something dangerous.
And look where we are now. No more epic matches, just a simmering pot of trouble. Can't make sense of it...
I got caught smacking someone with a stick in the street.
Yeah, I gave him that stick.
And I'm that someone.
Whether it was for a good reason or not, as soon as you break the Order's doctrines—fraternity, Ragunna's "unity," or whatever—you're sent off on pilgrimage.
Once on board the Pilgrim's Sail, we only had each other to rely on. Out here, sticking together is the only way to survive.
Speaking of which, we never did settle who won that fight, did we?
Hmm, now that you mention it, we didn't.
Then let's do it now! C'mon! Let's go!
Haha, don't worry, they've been at this a hundred times before! How about a wager? I'll put up my lucky half-coin!
Then again... neither of them ever actually wins, do they? Betting might be a waste... Eh, who cares? It's the fun that matters!

dialogs.content: Relax, young man. Life's only just unfurling its sails for you. Why sit there like one of those dour statues in the Order's halls? Don't be afraid to show a little spark!
I... I was just thinking about my future. Is Ragunna truly lost to me forever?
Ah, some have found their way back, but under the Order's watchful eye. Is that really what you want? A life without freedom?
Listen, you don't need a grand stage to leave your mark. A true Ragunnesi can turn even a ragged tent into the finest theater. That's what I'm preparing to do.
I might be an old man now, but don't let that fool you. I was once crowned with the Laurel, you know!
You? A-are you... Mr. Bardolino?
In the flesh! Hahaha!

As I took my final bow on stage, a bright light pierced through the clouds, shining down from the sky. And then, a radiant Laurel descended upon me. And I heard a voice—it was the Sentinel's voice, ringing in my head.
I asked Them a question that had puzzled me since childhood, the ultimate philosophical riddle—"What should I eat tonight?"
And They answered, "The body is the temple of the mind. To keep your mind sharp, do consume healthy food, such as the Laurus Salad."

But why Laurus Salad? I was baffled, and the meaning still eludes me to this very day. I've never been quick-witted though, and the Order's doctrines never quite took hold. Acting, however, that is where my true passion lies...
But why did a blessed Laureate like you get banished by the Order?
Back when I won the Laurel, Ragunna was led by the Holy Maiden. She promoted all sorts of grand celebrations during the Carnevale, an unceasing tide of revelry...
Stages sprang up on every corner of the city, performances dancing through the streets, and shops adorned in vibrant hues. Even on rainy nights, you could still hear music playing in the square.
Some performers wove their critiques into their acts. Sharp as she was, the Holy Maiden noticed. She refined city policy with each whisper of dissent.

Ah, those were the golden days, my friend. The Holy Maiden once said that if she were to leave this world, she'd want no majestic tomb or a solemn funeral, but the grandest Carnevale as her final farewell.

And then... she really did leave us. The current Primus took her place, and in the name of "mourning the Holy Maiden," issued all sorts of bans on the Carnevale. But is that really what she would have wanted?
The Order's grip tightened, and the Carnevale performances were reduced to dull, monotonous shadows of their former selves.
One year, I strung a wire from a Gondola to the top of the clock tower in Liberty Square, and another from the tower to the Fisalia's mansion.
Then, I disguised myself as one of the La Guardia to fool the Acolytes and climbed to the roof along the wire...
Midway through the Order's performance, I hopped on a Wingray with a Cloudcaster, showering the entire city with flowers.
Yes, it was a magnificent sight. The Wingray soared higher than the Acolytes could reach. They couldn't do anything but watch golden-pink petals rain from the sky for three whole days.

They struggled to clean up the flowers from the streets, and it took a downpour to wash them all away. That Cloudcaster, adapted from a music van, became the prototype for the one we use on stage today.
But that's all in the past! To this day, I'm still not sure what crime they pinned on me. Maybe walking the wire without protection? Ha!
Anyway, I'm just an old relic now. But you lot, you're the main characters of this era, facing down every obstacle with fire in your bellies!
But isn't our fate already sealed? Without the so-called "salvation" the Order preaches, we're doomed to our banishment. Just lost souls, dying in obscurity...
Life is short, and we weren't born just to atone. The Order may banish us, but they can't take away our right to sing.
Death is one of many possible ends, but it's certainly not the worst. Perhaps being forgotten is what the Order wanted for us.
They want to erase all traces of our existence, grind us into dust, and drag us into the abyss... But we'll fight the tide and live our lives to the fullest.
Members of the troupe may come and go, but they've never truly left us. Their deeds and songs are passed down through the ages.
One day, our voices will echo across every land, our words will reach every corner of the world, and by then, even the Tacet Discords in the Stormy Sea will know our names.

That's the spirit, boy! Even if I can't earn myself a proper title, I'll become Rinascita's most enigmatic legend. When I'm gone, I'll leave behind a coffin that sings, or maybe turn into a lark, singing every day and night...

dialogs.content: Is everything going smoothly with your family, Ms. Carlotta?
Yes, thank you. The Order's scheme was uncovered as planned. Uncle Capollo was rescued, and <ano=Head of the Montellis>Grandfather</ano> has handled the rest.
I still owe you thanks, {PlayerName}, for improvising with me in front of that Priest.
You've got a sharp mind. No pain, no gain, as Grandfather used to say. I'm pleased we're on the same page.
Your kindness is much appreciated. The Montellis won't forget this. In return, I'll share everything I know.

I believe you've noticed that the Order has been undermining the family under the guise of its doctrines. Alienation, monopolization—just a few tricks up their sleeve. Their true motives, however, run deeper.
Their alliance with the Fractsidus speaks volumes. While we don't know the full extent of their conspiracy, one thing is clear: their sights are set on this year's Carnevale.
{PlayerName}, the Carnevale is likely where you'll find clues about the Sentinel.
Legend has it that the Sentinel, Imperator, has been secluded in the heavens, cut off from the mortal realm. The last record of the Sentinel is from the Carnevale a decade ago.
At that time, the entire city was shrouded in mist. Ghosts roamed the streets, a dragon roared from the sky and a sea behemoth raged, summoning towering waves... Do any clues come to mind?
The mist might be coming from the Remnant Clouds in the Nimbus Sanctum. Lorelei has the power to purify and control them, but the Fractsidus interfered…
Remnant Clouds corrupted by evil will disrupt Echoes' frequencies. If the mist had spread to the city, it would have stirred the Echoes into chaos.
We are lucky that you and Zani, along with that Acolyte, awakened Lorelei in time. You prevented the mist from spreading and averted the Waveworn. The Fractsidus must still be licking their wounds.
The Montelli traitors used Lycoris in experiments to turn Echoes back into Tacet Discords... If they were successful, the "ghosts" seen ten years ago may have also been created this way.
"Ghost" is just a dramatic name given by the Ragunnesi for Tacet Discords. They look nearly identical to Echoes, especially in the mist.
With your help, Grandfather has thwarted their plan. No corrupted Echoes will appear at this year's Carnevale.
The Order has allied with the Fractsidus to control the dragon... From what I saw when I connected with its frequency, they might be planning to command it to attack Ragunna during the Carnevale.
After the Tacet Discords took over this isle, the Order used them as an excuse to forbid any entry. It might be their way of concealing the dragon's existence.
But without the Lycoris, the Dragon of Dirge is now off the table.
The Remnant Clouds spreading, experiments to turn Echoes, and the dragon's manipulation... The Order plans to recreate these disasters at this year's ceremony.
The Order and the Fractsidus are allies. To prevent the Carnevale's sabotage, we must stop them. But... what is their motive?
The Primus called it a divine punishment and took the opportunity to appear as a savior. A perfect way to build legitimacy.
The Order relies on the people's faith in the Sentinel. With the Sentinel's ten year absence, faith in the Order has waned. They must be desperate to restore that trust.
It is for this reason that the Order has been forced to revive the festival.
Let's consider the implications. If the Carnevale proceeds unhindered, how would it affect the Order?

The current Primus claims to be the Enlightened One, the Sentinel's Resonator. However, based on the prophecy we found in the ruins, this role is meant for the young maiden who is destined to heed the divine oracles during the Carnevale.
The Carnevale is the only time humans can directly communicate with the Sentinel. Normally, it's the Primus who conveys the Sentinel's words.
A successful Carnevale offers a chance for citizens to meet the Sentinel in person. But for the Primus, and possibly the Order, it poses a threat if they've been fabricating the oracles.
To sabotage it while still maintaining their authority... they partnered with the Fractsidus.
The Fractsidus will cause chaos during the Carnevale, and the Order will swoop in as the saviors, restoring public trust just as they did before.
So far, you've helped us crush three of their schemes, but one remains...
We have evidence that the Cetus is being manipulated, and the Fractsidus are setting up their final plan. With their whereabouts unknown, we'll need to adapt our strategy as the Carnevale unfolds.
From what I've noticed, you're not one to act passively or pin your hopes on others. You prefer to strike first and steer events in your favor.
Winning the Laurel might give you the chance to talk with the Sentinel. The Sentinel's Resonator may also be present. So...
Our aim has always been clear—to restore the Carnevale to its former glory with a performance for the ages.
If the divine truly exists, would they wish to see their people living without freedom or witness a festival twisted into a tool for tyrants?
If we win the Laurel, we'll show that such punishment is absurd. But if that's truly their design... we shall break those divine shackles ourselves.
Whether divinity exists or not, we will fight for Ragunna's freedom, where everyone has the right to live and pursue a future of their own choosing!
The Montellis share this vision. Only in a free society can a fair and open market thrive.
However, the troupe alone is too weak, the family is under close watch, and our enemy hides in the shadows... We need your strength to find our way forward.
Thank you. I'm pleased we've reached an agreement once more.

dialogs.content: Our rehearsals are rather straightforward. No scripts, just pure intuition and our senses guiding us! That's what makes Commedia Improvviso truly come alive!
For our improvised comedy, we start with a theme. From there, we build our lines and act on the fly, responding to the unfolding show and audience reactions.

But with the limitless capacity for human creativity at play, the plot can sometimes veer into the... well, unconventional. To prevent things from spiraling too far, we set an "anchor" for the performance.
Pardon my interruption, but I'm quite curious. What sort of bizarre plots have you encountered?

Well, something like "A humble craftsman from a small town sets sail on a rainy night, stumbles upon ancient ruins, is reincarnated with super powers, and then decides to conquer the galaxy, becoming the Emperor of the Stars..."
So, we draft a basic outline that assigns roles and guides the plot's direction.

And this time, our outline is: "A kingdom is attacked, monsters run rampant, and the Demon King has kidnapped the Holy Maiden. A few brave heroes accept the minister's quest to defeat the Demon King and rescue her."
This outline holds special meaning. We want to pay tribute to the play once performed by the Blessed Maiden herself, which was also about a hero facing a Demon King.
Good people have their wishes fulfilled, heroes appear in a time of crisis, justice triumphs over evil, and united friends are undefeatable.
This is the tale the Blessed Maiden once told, and it's a universal story we want to portray.
To me, the world is a stage, and performing is much like combat. Coordinated movements, quick thinking, sharp reflexes, and, above all, trust in your allies.
What I'm getting at is that you both are very skilled and capable. We don't have many dos and don'ts, so relax and express yourselves freely on stage!
This rehearsal is to help you get familiar with basic stage movements, techniques, and the troupe's style, and to build good rapport.
Exactly. I'll handle the stage lighting, Brant will narrate, and the rest will take on the role of the audience.

dialogs.content: It seems we have some time before the train arrives. How about a little chat to pass the time?
Well, then. Where shall we begin?
"The city, an abomination of chaos, claims its first death at birth. Its mortality has become our sustenance, like a whale that slowly sinks into the abyss."
This comment on Ragunna comes from Rosselli, a painter from the past. Tragically, he died in poverty, his work overlooked. Now, ironically, even a mere sketch of his commands over a million Credits.
Now. What is your impression of Ragunna so far?
Passionate... Indeed. Passion is a quality the Ragunnesi possess in abundance. It's also why the Carnevale is so eagerly anticipated.
Indeed. Ragunna is not as glamorous as it seems. Beneath the veneer of prosperity, avarice reigns supreme.
Indeed, faith is Ragunna's crown jewel. Our devotion to the Sentinel stands unrivaled throughout Rinascita.
A most prudent response. Perhaps you're still acquainting yourself with Ragunna, or you simply prefer discretion. Either way, I take no offense.
Ragunna has many facets. Most people only see one side of it, but for me—
It's like two sworn enemies are forcibly bound together. That's Ragunna—a city where tradition and innovation, openness and isolation, ceaselessly wrestle for dominance.
That is why the Montelli and Fisalia families are in a constant clash, as you may have seen.
The Montellis champion innovation, staking all on the Carnevale. Meanwhile, the Fisalias cling to tradition, colluding with the shadows that lurk in Ragunna's depths.
Fortunately, this long struggle behind the curtains will soon come to an end. Not because of the two families, but because of you.
Me?
Yes, you. The Fated One. Perhaps you're not merely entangled in Ragunna's conflict, but are, in fact, the very eye of the storm. The city's fate may well rest upon your shoulders.
You may have not noticed it yet, but we are... and have been in the same boat for a long time.
Ah. There's the train. It's time to say goodbye now.
I didn't catch your name.
I'll tell you next time. As for now, let's keep it a mystery.
Until we meet again, Fated One. May you find your own path in Ragunna.

dialogs.content: Have you also come to repent and seek forgiveness?
The Sentinel has revealed a path to resist temptation and corruption. We need only devote ourselves wholly... to Lorelei.
We're just here to see Lorelei.
Patience. I see your eagerness for enlightenment, like our new brothers. You've removed your masks, but your hearts… they're still veiled.
Everyone here wears a mask. Everyone in Ragunna. Without exception, never unmasked. This is the source of our suffering. The mask veils our hearts.
Like our new brothers, they wear peculiar masks of madness. Poor souls tormented by evil desires. May they find peace in Lorelei's embrace.
Yes, their masks are filled with madness, but even wrongdoers can seek redemption from Lorelei. The Sentinel granted Lorelei this authority, and no one can take it away.
Follow Lorelei's song and your heart, and you may meet our lady. But if your transgressions are... beyond redemption, you'll be lost in the sea of clouds forever.
So what should we do to see Lorelei?
Do you seek an audience with Lorelei? Sadly, you've come at a bad time. Lorelei is furious, and our mortal bodies can't withstand her wrath. We've sealed the path to her domain.
We appreciate the explanation, but we believe Lorelei is in danger... We're here to help her. Someone's planning to exploit her powers...
The path has been closed. You must leave.
(Sigh) Doesn't look like we'll be talking our way past him. Let's find another way, {PlayerName}.

The door has been shut. Simply sing along and it will open before you!

But most of these are worn out and don't look like modern Rinascita script. Phoebe, can you read any of it?

We should investigate further.

dialogs.content: That flower... looks like the petals we found in Whisperwind Haven.
It's the Fractsidus. I've dealt with them before, and I've seen a flower just like this.
How long have I been in slumber... This nightmare... How long was I trapped in it?
Are you also part of the dream?
No, we are not... Might you be Lorelei?
I am. Travelers from afar, I sense… the kindness pulsing in your hearts. You must be the ones who broke the chains of my nightmare.
The oathbreakers, hiding behind their Masks of Madness… They tainted the Nimbus Sanctum with corrupted blooms, drowning me in rage and sorrow. Endless nightmares became my prison.
Masks of Madness... I recall those people at the entrance of the Atrium mentioned it.

Had you not freed me from my nightmare, I would never be able to fulfill the Sentinel's task… The tides of the Nimbus Sanctum would have engulfed the whole of Ragunna, just as they once claimed the sacred temple now lying in ruins beneath you.
Wait. The Sentinel? Does that mean...?
Yes, the Sentinel molded me from a mindless being to the form you see, and bestowed upon me the most precious gift... A soul.
They commanded me to restrain the clouds and prevent the Remnant Energy within it from... dissipating.

Using the computing power of the Stellar Matrices, the data we extract from these frequencies is as detailed as DNA analysis.
We build our candidates' profiles with this info and store them in our talent pool.
We Gardeners visit each candidate in person, check their background, and bring that information back to Tethys.
Tethys then determines the test content for each individual.

dialogs.content: Once, the Blessed Maiden was just a simple peasant girl. During the Sentinel's Gratitude Rite, the young Fleurdelys managed to sneak past the guards and drink the sacramental wine—every drop.
Perhaps it was the intoxicating wine in Egla Town or simply her lack of experience with spirits, but she soon found herself quite drunk.
Swaying on her feet, she ascended the ceremony's grand platform, lifted her threadbare dress, and began a rather ungainly dance.
Seizing the sacred horn, she played a carefree folk tune, dodging the guards and weaving through the crowd with surprising agility.
Remarkably, the crowd, as if drawn by an unseen force, followed her lead, transforming the solemn ceremony into a wild parade of cheers and revelry.
Naturally, the Order was less than pleased. The Pilgrim's Sail did not yet exist, so Fleurdelys faced three days of confinement. During that time, she used her prison walls as a canvas.
That unforgettable day of disordered revelry left a lasting mark on all who witnessed it.
Is it not remarkable? A rebellious girl, chosen by the Sentinel to become the Blessed Maiden.
If the Sentinel indeed permitted such a girl to serve as Their spokesperson, it suggests that all this joyous revelry is not something They disdain.
Perhaps They too enjoy poetry, painting, tears, laughter, romantic tales of knights, and dancing amidst crowds—much like ourselves.

content.content: The divine is always beyond our comprehension.
Perhaps, the true intention of the Sentinel isn't to rule their people by faith.

dialogs.content: The people of this island came from diverse civilizations now lost to time, but through plays and tradition, they sought to preserve memories of their heritage.
In the past, while the clash of cultures led to conflict, the Ragunnesi united through faith, restoring balance, even if precarious.
To maintain this unity, we have always needed both a Sentinel and a "play" based on a shared legend that gives us roles.
Yet, this play has endured for so long that we have become defined by our roles—noble, commoner, believer, merchant. What was meant to unite us now stifles us.
Now, we yearn for a day when we can truly set aside our titles and positions, express our true selves, and join together in celebration...
Yes, born from hope and idealism, it reminds the Ragunnesi of our initial vision of equality and freedom. It also affirms our true worth.
While the Order's true intentions remain unclear, we are certain their influence has already eroded the very foundations of our society.
People revere the divine figure the Order has constructed, yet they also live in fear of punishment.
Legends become accomplices in fostering ignorance, and faith becomes the loyal executioner of cruel punishment. An invisible cage has trapped us all...
Speaking of freedom within a cage is absurd. Fear and ignorance are our foremost enemies.
This year's Carnevale will spark a flame fierce enough to burn down that cage.
Rest well, and tomorrow, we shall take the stage together at the Carnevale.
Good night. May your dreams be sweet.

Things aren't as bright for the Montellis as they may seem. The Order, Fisalias, and the Fractsidus... Any attempt to break the status quo puts us at risk.

Especially with you, just as Carlotta did.
Now that you mention it, let me be clear.
Carlotta is dear to me, and nothing will change that.
But she's from the lesser branch of the family. Tradition says I, the rightful heir, should manage dealings with the Black Shores, not her.
Restoring order and benefiting the family as I intended... that's what I meant in the letter by amending a slight misstep.
The leader of the Black Shores must have sent you here with a purpose. Tell me, and I will offer you support far beyond what Carlotta could provide.
The choice is yours, of course... But as the family heir, I will not see my authority undermined, even by those I consider allies.
So if you can't stand by my side, I'd prefer you stay out of the Montellis' affairs.
Otherwise... believe me, you won't want to find yourself at odds with us, no matter how strong you are.
You're welcome to remain an observer from the sidelines. But once you join the table, you play by the rules—my rules.
Well said. But the rules are not set in stone, are they?
What matter of intrigue brought you and {PlayerName} together at this hour, Uncle? A table... are we speaking of a splendid card game, then?
Your timing is most unfortunate. Our little chat just finished.
Pity. I didn't think you'd pull {Male=him;Female=her} aside for a private word, especially after all Rover and I have been through together.
But since you've finished, would you excuse us now?
Carlotta, you stay. I have more to discuss with you.
Meet me at the <color=yellow>rendezvous</color>. Beware the "eyes."
A gun is a powerful tool, but only in the hands of the worthy.
I understand, Uncle. I've never forgotten where my privileges come from, nor will I covet what's not mine.
The Black Shores, the Carnevale... my sole principle is whether they benefit the Montellis.
I will execute any command that strengthens the family, and crush any threats to our standing.
...Very well. Keep your words in mind.
Uncle, about Benett... have you heard?
That family thief stealing from the vault? Why, are you suggesting I failed my duties?
Not at all, I just happened to overhear someone talking about it in passing...
(Carlotta warned me about eyes... So she probably wants me to avoid unnecessary attention.)
(Not sure why, but staying under the radar is never a bad idea.)

Ah well, a cigar without smoke... My granddaughter told me Ragunna's rain is a bad omen. Can't argue with that now, can I?

Oh, did it capture your interest as well? Or are you simply passing the time until the rain ends?
Haha, it's only the investor's nature in me. I find myself irresistibly drawn to items of unique value.
Then it seems you will have to put up with me for a while.
The Montelli family prides themselves on their eclectic taste in art. Any style by any artist can find its home within their quarter.
Art knows no boundaries of time, place, or the mind. Here we stand, united by the rain, drawn to the same painting.
They say in art, we glimpse pieces of our own soul.
What do you make of this piece? Care to share your thoughts?
You step closer to study the collage.
Small, irregular shapes nest within larger circles, their edges melding together to form a delicate harmony.
This balance, however, feels precarious, as if two opposing forces are on the verge of collision.
You have keener eyes than I expected. Seeing essence beneath the surface.
Hahaha, it is typical of symbolism to conceal ideas in a play of colors and forms... But sometimes, simplicity is more powerful.
Indeed. True artistry lies not only in what is painted, but in what is left unsaid.
I share the same view, except that I'm somehow saddened by the part that forsakes its character to achieve balance.
...Perhaps chosen by the artist for its uniqueness.
Now is not the time to cling to the existing balance, but to embrace the unknown, seek change, and carve out one's path... just as she once did.

"Glory in Decay," the impressionist Pasoli's latest piece... Didn't know you had such refined taste.

content.content: I was discussing it with an old gentleman.
He left soon after the rain stopped.

dialogs.content: I dodged those pesky "eyes" the whole way here, worried you'd been kept waiting too long. But it seems you've kept yourself entertained.
So the old gentleman was simply hiding from the rain, was he? I see... The Montelli Quarter does attract art enthusiasts. Anyway, I'm glad prying eyes didn't follow.
When it rains in Ragunna, surprises are as common as puddles. A delay is only a small splash.
Calling you here with little explanation and a word of caution... I can only imagine your confusion.
The Montelli's path is not always paved with roses, but with thorns as well. As the heir apparent, my uncle bears many burdens.
Seeing me work with you on the Carnevale under Grandfather's orders might have unsettled him, leading to a hasty, misguided move.

content.content: How do you feel about this?

dialogs.content: In truth, I haven't thought about it, and my opinions hold little weight.
The current plan has proven effective. I believe it's wise to trust Grandfather's judgment, as I always do.
Besides, I now have more important duties to fulfill.
The shark in our midst has finally made its move.
Recently, several of our partners claimed to have found a superior seller and ended their dealings with us.
Meanwhile, Benett, our vault keeper, was reported to have embezzled and sold vault assets. It's said that he tried to flee but was killed by Tacet Discords outside the city.
I am not so sure... I've worked with Benett before. He was principled, bold but not reckless, not one to easily betray. And...

The night he died, he sent a photo to my Terminal—a blood-stained page of an anthology, marked with three phrases. "Thy eyes guide my course in the tempest," "When forty winters siege thy beauty," and "The planet turns right, twice and a half."
The meaning is yet to be revealed, but he is clearly conveying a message.
All evidence points to Benett being the key to uncovering the shark lurking in our waters.

The Montelli family is a symbol of liberation for Ragunna. We uphold freedom and equality for all. Our vault is the heart of our family, and if it's corrupted, it threatens not only us, but risks plunging the city back into oppression and isolation.
As much as I hate to suspect family members, I cannot rule any of them out.
You, however, are different. As an outsider who has aided us in capturing the initial traitors... I hope to not be proven wrong, but I feel that I can trust you.
My uncle's words were clear. Only those at the table can play the game. To engage with my family, one must have both standing and purpose.
So, I offer you a new identity in our upcoming inquiry—Cat's Eye, a provisional member under my patronage.
If you wish to join, you must undertake the final assessment and pledge your loyalty to the Montellis.
Oh, don't worry, we aren't harming anyone. It is but a subtle adaptation of the rules.

Also, have you looked closely at your own eyes? They share the same luster as Cat's Eye gems.
Now, Cat's Eye, will you stand with me to catch the traitor within our family and avert this looming threat?
I understand decorum is important to the Montellis. But among friends, can't we be a bit more... informal?
What made you say that?
Hmm, you're curious who I am beyond my role, is that it?
Hmm, I just might entertain that thought.

I haven't faced a true challenge since I got here. Would you accept my help? I'm sure I'd learn a thing or two.

But here's something I can tell you. Someone tried to steal from the vault recently.
Oh, Margherita's! Nothing quite like it, hm? And the pizza... Oh, it's a favorite in my circle, too.
Ah! Always a solid choice when on the move. Perfect spot for a bit of catching up.
You know, the last time I was there, I heard talk about a thief stealing from the vault. Is that true?
Well, cat's out of the bag now. See that house right there? That's where the thief lived. We came to search for clues.

content.content: Did you recover the stolen goods?

dialogs.content: No, not yet. We've looked everywhere but found nothing.
To be honest, I doubt we'll ever find them. The thief has probably sold everything off by now, and we are short on manpower. That's a needle in a haystack if you ask me.
Well, our boss is the Padrino's son. He has his methods.
Our job is to follow orders, not to ask questions. Just do what we're told and do it well.
That's right. If you spot anything unusual, keep an eye on it. Could be your big break. With a bit more time, I think you'll do just fine.

You rendezvous with Carlotta after her investigation and share the information you gathered.
So, they found nothing, but assumed Uncle wasn't concerned?
That makes no sense. Everything that happened recently ties back to the vault. If Uncle wished to protect his position, he'd be quick to retrieve the items and resolve the situation.
Curiously, Benett was last sighted in the vicinity of <color=yellow>Liberty Square</color>, where you met Uncle.
Last night, I was investigating the area before I happened upon your private meeting.
But when I brought this up to him afterward, he didn't seem privy to any details.
As for my search of Benett's home, nothing of note turned up, just as the two agents reported.
I found no spoils, not even the faintest trace of them being stored or moved... Everything about his living space fits the profile of a typical junior vault employee.
I've also asked around about Bennet after our previous collaboration. He was ambitious, but never greedy. I was even told he refused the bribe offered by a business associate during an operation.
The Montelli family is ever generous with wealth and opportunities, welcoming all who aspire to make their mark in Ragunna. Mere profit would never make him betray us.
For now, more evidence is required. The entire matter might need to be approached from a different angle...
Shh, hold still... See that man over there, the one that looks like a gray dove?

After him, quick.

Right, Old Duncan?

I will never forget that <color=yellow>stormy</color> night, nor any of the members who were caught in it.

I don't know.
To grieve for my last friend in the family? To blame him for being so reckless and greedy?
Or to figure out how this fool ended up in such a mess, hoping to find the lost items and settling his debts, so he may rest in peace?
I tried to persuade him to leave with me, but failed. In Ragunna's game, the Montelli family has only two options.
We either play to win, or are forced to leave with nothing.
Every Montelli has a chance at their desires, but what's the price... They stake everything they hold dear—family, love, faith, principles, and even their life.
Now... his ambition and greed have cost him everything.

Given your familiarity, you might help us in locating these items...

No, leave me be! Don't bother me!
The void... the endless void has consumed me. I want no part in anything... Who are you, and who am I?

Terminals are divine artifacts from the Sentinel, brought to Rinascita by the first Primus.
What you possessed were nothing but privately made replicas, existing solely by the grace of the Primus. How dare you defy our cleansing of such blasphemy!
We never stopped asking the Order for permission to wear the Terminals, but every single request is denied. You won't even tell us why!
You've controlled the Terminal supply, and the family stopped trading with us... These are all we have left. Why should we hand them over?
I can sense your fervent desire for the artifacts and the blessings from the Sentinel... But whether you are worthy of the terminals is for the Order to decide.
If you willingly part with your wealth in devotion to the Order's divine cause, the door to forgiveness might still be open.
But should you persist in your defiance... we'll have to escort you to the Penitentiary for judgment.

The Order's arrogance is known, but such blatant actions... Is it because we're far from the heart of the city?

The Sentinel and the Primus have declared free trade as our undeniable right. Scarlet Velvet is always entitled to trade as they please, regardless of their previous partnerships.
You preach the doctrine, yet fail to adhere to it yourself. If I were you, I'd be on my way to the Penitentiary. Willful transgression... is the worst blasphemy one can imagine.
Mark my words! The day Montelli is brought to its knees by the Order and Fisalia will be the day you beg for the Sentinel's mercy.
When that day comes, all shall be under the Order's control. And it will not be long in coming.
The Acolyte departs with his entourage. Scarlet Velvet signals the others to leave and assess the damages.
Ernesto, the bartender, said you needed to see me.
You may have just defended us, but you heard it—your family has left us in a mess. Frankly, I don't see the point in having this conversation.
But since Ernesto said it's about Benett, I'll give you a minute, for his sake. Speak quickly.
Regardless of the bigger picture, your side ended the deal. We were informed on short notice to stop all trade.
And it's not just the Terminals—no more "jewelry," "perfumes," and all that nonsense. You saw what happened today.
Not to mention I haven't seen a Montelli for nearly two weeks.
Where were you when we were fighting against the Order and the Fisalias?
There was a slight issue of a traitor in the vault, so our hands were tied.
A direct approach works best at times. Actually, what that Acolyte claimed is news to me. Surrendering control and ceasing trade... are not in the Montelli's vocabulary.
The Montelli creed has always been family first, and a pioneering spirit second.
With your grandfather, maybe, but he won't be around forever. When Capollo takes the helm... you won't have a say.
The real question is whether we can get our trade back on track. Can your family still be trusted? What I need is a solid promise from someone in charge—can you do that?
One thing's for sure, I don't want to see the family who first broke the monopoly to trade with us commoners end up defending it.
I'll speak with my uncle and grandfather to see what happened with our cooperation.
You know what? This is supposed to be your family's business. Why am I saying this to you... Excuse my earlier words.
So... Ernesto told me Benett's gone. What happened? He seemed fine the last time we met.

content.content: Some say he got what he deserved for stealing from the vault.
And there are rumors that you helped him fence the stolen items.
Of course, we think there's more to the story.

Nothing shady, okay? He knew his stuff—never took advantage of us, never budged on prices either.

For him, it was always business first, friendship second. When he was running late, he'd stay up that <color=yellow>hill</color> sometimes. We even set up a shelter there after it happened a few times. That's all.

It seems Benett may have anticipated the trouble ahead.

...Something is strange here.
These items aren't exactly rare, but they're not everyday objects either. They seem out of place here. Looks like Benett left them deliberately.

Do you recall those three lines from the anthology? The ones Benett sent to me in the photo?
"Thy eyes guide my course in the tempest," the woman in the painting here seems to stand in the gloomy rain, but her eyes remain bright.
Like the secret "code" in drinks, what matters is never the objects themselves, but the shared rules and agreements between both parties.
Now, the book. It appears to be about winter, which is likely related to the second line, forty winters...
You flip the book to page forty, and there, written in large numbers, are 1, 9, and 0.
The last one is a rotor device, the planet...

<color=yellow>MLCL190468</color>? That format—It's a vault storage code.
Of course it is. Benett was a vault keeper. But what was he trying to convey in such a cryptic manner?
<color=yellow>Four letters</color>... the highest clearance level in the vault. Could it be...
Hold on.
Carlotta? Uh... you asked me to keep an eye out for Benett's Terminal. Well, I've found it.
That's for me to know and you to wonder.
But... it was not in good shape after what it went through. If you can use it at all, the data and records inside might need to be recovered.
Understood. I'll have someone pick it up for restoration.
Wait, wait... n-now? You're not even... gonna check?
Oh, it's nothing, really. Just worried it might be too tricky to repair.
Alright, we'll inform you when there's more to share.
We're returning to the Montelli Quarter first. The Terminal will be fixed there. As for the codes, we'll figure it out once we arrive...
{PlayerName}, you might not know this, but Benett was never granted the highest clearance in the vault.
Isn't that a good sign? It means Benett might not be guilty after all, just as you suspected.
But it's replaced by another suspicion, one I am reluctant to entertain but am... forced to consider.
Only <color=yellow>Grandfather, Uncle, and I</color> have the highest clearance.
Liberty Square, our proximity, the vault's security clearance, a traitor among the top brass... the indifference toward the stolen goods, and the authority to end dealings with Scarlet Velvet...
There's someone all evidence points to... Were I to entertain it... it all starts to makes sense. Uncle...
But if it was truly him—the heir to our family—who betrayed us, wouldn't that be utterly absurd?

I'll be with you no matter what. So let's see where this leads.

Someone extracted the core data module... It's empty now.

By doing so, we've broken the Order's monopoly. We've given more people the means to protect themselves in their ventures, giving them choices they didn't have before.
The Order is aware of our discreet business, but they turn a blind eye as long as we don't openly challenge their authority. The hefty taxes we pay maintain this... delicate understanding.
As a result, no family member would ever divulge our Terminal secrets, much less allow the modules to fall into the wrong hands. What exactly are you planning, Uncle?
No, we must find the core module...
Carlotta, where are you?
Uncle, may I ask you something first? Before the Carnevale, the Priest showed me your pendant. How did he come by it, and what led to your capture?
Does it matter? All you need to know is that it's handled, and I'm in the clear now.
Were you mistreated? Did they coerce you into doing something against your will?
Heed my words. Whatever you've uncovered, put it behind you, and all will be as it was. No grudges, no consequences, only family.
Now, we've had some trouble with a shipment over at Septimont. As the rightful heir, I'm giving you a new order. Take care of it, and I'll pretend none of this ever happened.
I refuse.
Excuse me?
I said I refuse! I can't act as if nothing happened. I won't let a family member die unjustly, or see our modules fall into the wrong hands.
Don't trouble yourself with the module. Yes, our family's ambition has led us far, but it's exacted a price paid in blood and tears. What harm is there in choosing the safer, easier path?
I can't believe you just said that. So, you're refusing to tell the truth and reveal the module's location, is that it?
Why do you insist on tearing everything apart? Have you ever thought about what Padrino would say? What others will think of us? I've given you an out, all you need to do is accept it.
Then so be it.
Your course is set. As is mine. But mark my words... I will stop you, Mr. Capollo.
I'm sorry you have to see this side of our family.
Really? I just wish... No, I did promise I'd try to drop the pretense with you.
I may need more time to come to terms with all this. I don't regret uncovering the truth and exposing the traitor… I'm just saddened that my uncle is the one behind it all.
We were meant to be the guardians of our family's ideals, to carry the torch forward. And yet, now…
Well, wallowing in emotion won't solve anything. Our priority now is to recover the data module. Every moment it's missing puts our family at greater risk.
The core module is difficult to carry around. They must have hidden it... The dock Benett visited, used for storage... Could it be there?
We need to adjust our strategy. My conversation with Capollo will have alerted him. He's likely to move the module sooner than expected. I need to inspect the dock for any clues.
Indeed, but time is not on our side. If Capollo acts on this, I might lose my window to secure the module. Our sole advantage now is that we're operating as a pair.
I need you to take this terminal to <color=yellow>Pierre</color> at the bank. If the dock turns out to be a dead end, we will need other leads.
I know that securing the module alone won't suffice. I must uncover Capollo's true motives...how it will affect our family. I'll figure it out, I promise.

content.content: And you knew why I'm here.

dialogs.content: Remember that painting we discussed earlier?
In a fragile equilibrium, the smaller piece is forced to repress its true nature. It's confined to a seemingly flawless structure, stripped of its autonomy. I don't want the same fate for her.
But I can't simply impose my path upon her, expecting blind obedience. She must find her own path, with a partner she can fully trust.
As for those who betray their own blood, there will be no leniency. Even my own son is not exempt from this.
However, before I intervene, I want to see her plan take shape. My hand should only be played as a final measure.
The old give way to the new, that is the way of the world. But for us Montellis, the courage to break from the past matters far more than clinging to it.
So, I ask you this favor. When the time is right, give this to her. She will need it.
It's a little tricky... but you're lucky to have my expertise!
This Terminal is defunct, but I've retrieved all its data, even the overwritten and isolated bits.
The Terminal has been tampered with, but nothing was intentionally erased. It seems they wanted to overwrite the data to avoid detection.
I can show you. Do you have a Terminal? I'll send over the data so you can see for yourself.
I assume you've taken care of Benett's body?
We... dumped him in the Tacet Discord zone overnight. We'll claim he was killed by those monsters tomorrow morning.
Sir... are you sure? Are we really going to work with the Order... after they made you kill one of our own?
We're in too deep now. Handing over the data module to the Order will cement out position as an ally of the authorities. We'll replace the Fisalias! The other Resonators in the city are irrelevant.
And Benett... I would have taken care of him regardless.
He knew too much. He deserved it for pursuing the Scarlet Velvet matter. Anyone who gets in my way shall meet the same fate.
Y-Yes, sir...
We all stood together on that stormy night, each one of us losing someone dear. And we all share the desire for our family to find an easier path forward.
The best way to avoid sacrifice isn't fighting, but aligning ourselves with superior powers and knowing when to yield.
You may have left the family, and I should expect no more favors from you. But I ask this of you one last time. Please, put this Terminal in Carlotta's hands.
What's in it? Carlotta.. What will happen to her?
Nothing, save for the standard location tracking data every Terminal holds.
In three days, I'll be negotiating on behalf of the family with the Order. I just want to make sure Carlotta doesn't interfere in the meantime. She'll be given a chance to join our side, I promise.
Think about Benett. If you take care of this, I will overlook what he stole and let it be a thing of the past. I know you care more about your late friend than you're willing to admit.
Unbelievable. What is Capollo even thinking? Killing one of our own... It's a complete betrayal of our family! I must record all this madness with something...
My Terminal? No, it's too risky. Wait... I have Benett's body... Nobody's going to pay attention to a dead man's Terminal.
I'll record it, then overwrite with new data.... I have to keep this record well... In case I also...

content.content: Carlotta... Tsk, I can't reach her now.
I must go check on her immediately.

My girl could not have accomplished this without your assistance.
I had faith in you two, but you surpassed my expectations.

dialogs.content: As anticipated, the Fractsidus is on the move.
Now, remember the rehearsal we did yesterday? All our preparations have led to this very moment.
She intends to use those Lycorises to summon and control the Tacet Discords. If we destroy the Lycorises, we can neutralize them.

Now that you mentioned it, we did see a bunch of kids running around with wooden swords and bedsheets for capes.

Ah, those youngsters are just reenacting the knight's play. The Night Reveries are a kind of a performance, too. They can be traced back to the legend of a brave knight who slayed a giant in Whisperwind Haven.
Since then, the legendary knight has become an irreplaceable symbol of humility, honor, and bravery for the town. The oath the boy just recited is one of the legacies the knight left us.
Knights from far and wide would gather here before setting off to the depth of Whisperwind Haven in search of the legend's origin.
As more knights filled our streets, an odd one emerged. These days, folks like to call him the "Mad Knight."
He only shows himself after dusk. Folks say he roams the outskirts, hunting down Tacet Discords. Get too close, and you might find yourself on the sharp end of his blade!
That's how he became the "Mad Knight," the talk of the town. We reckon he's cursed now from wrestling with those wretches for so long.
To placate this restless soul, the town created the Night Reveries—endless dramas of the knight enacted by the Echoes. Townsfolk and visitors alike were advised to stay indoors at night.
But... there's one lad who stands apart. Fancies that the knight isn't mad at all. He believes a true knight would never betray their oath, no matter the cost.
For him, every swing of a knight's sword must carry meaning. To prove his theory, the boy is hell-bent on becoming a knight and challenging the Mad Knight to a duel.
Yes, Carlow. We all thought it was just another childhood fantasy, but he's held onto that dream to this day.
Becoming a knight doesn't sound too bad. Hehe, you get all the cool points plus who can resist that suit of armor?!

dialogs.content: Raise your glasses! Shout it loud, friends!
To us, to the Carnevale, and to our very own Laureate, {PlayerName}!
A name that echoes through the world, destined to roam the skies before shaking the earth!
Hahaha! There you are, my friend! A compliment, if too subtle, loses all its charm!
Don't be fooled by how he looks. Brant is already deep in his cups, drunk as a skunk.
Oh, let him enjoy himself. The taste of victory is still fresh, and after such a battle, we should celebrate to the fullest!
Drink your fill, everyone! This round's on me!
HOORAY!!!
Hmm, I see… Someone's been eavesdropping.
A devout Acolyte wouldn't enter such a place without a good reason.
The Montelli family is known for its hospitality, but freeloaders... will not find us so welcoming.
Friends, let's keep the mood lively!
Come, let's discuss the information we've gathered so far.
During the Carnevale, you heard the Sentinel's voice and found a girl named Cartethyia. We've dug up some information on her.
In the Order, every high-ranking Acolyte is given a new name.
We contacted the Acolyte, Phoebe. After some digging in the Order's records, she confirmed that before taking on her holy title, the Blessed Fleurdelys was called... Cartethyia.
But the Blessed Maiden... she martyred herself twenty years ago...
The family will uncover the truth. The only remaining clue is the "inverted tower" you mentioned hearing about from the Sentinel, but even that feels elusive...
Judging by your expression, you must have discovered something new, right?
Do you recall what we learned from the stained glass in the Tower Ruins? There were two divinities at the dawn of Rinascita.
If one refers to the Sentinel, then the other, who could stand alongside Them, might be the Threnodian.
The two are undoubtedly linked, so uncovering one could lead us to the other.
Remember Gilberto, from the Fisalia family? It took a lot to get him to talk, but we finally got some information from him.
As he tells it, the Fisalia family's long-revered deity is none other than... Leviathan, the Threnodian from the sea's depths.
It's hard to believe, I know. But recent events have only reinforced what we discovered from the stained glass.
The Fisalia family has been on this island since the founding of Rinascita, so their worship of the Threnodian may have persisted for centuries.
We will attempt to establish contact with the Fisalias to build an alliance and gather more intelligence.
Rest assured, negotiation is what we do best. If necessary, we'll present them with an offer they can't refuse.
Excuse me for the interruption. Greetings, esteemed guest.
The Primus wishes to invite you for a conversation at the Cathedral of Mercury. Would you be so inclined?
How curious. Since when has the Primus become so interested in social calls?
It could very well be a trap.
I'm merely conveying the Primus' invitation. The choice is yours.
Remember, you're not alone. If anything happens, just let us know.
Very well, please follow me to the Cathedral of Mercury.

dialogs.content: Never before have I seen a day so steeped in both shadow and light.
The birds sing, the flowers bloom… yet this world knows neither true joy nor eternity.
Come closer, Righteous One, there's no need for hesitation.

I am Fenrico, the Primus of the Order of the Deep. Your deeds have reached my ears, and I have long wished to meet you. Alas, the burdens of this world delayed our meeting until now. I beg your pardon for the wait.
Please accept my respect for you—you and your troupe have shown great talent and ambition, breathing new life into Ragunna.
I ask you to deliver this message to your companions: from this day forth, the troupe shall have permanent rights to perform within the city.
All mortals stumble, but through pilgrimage, they have cleansed their souls and atoned for their transgressions. They have earned their right to return to this divinely blessed land.
I understand that questions weigh on your heart. In the presence of a just Divinity, speak freely, and I will answer with all the honesty I possess.
By the great Sentinel Imperator, I swear to you. There shall be no deceit in my words.
You have walked a path similar to Theirs. Indeed, you have the right to meet Them.
However, due to the Dark Tide two decades ago, the Sentinel's body was gravely wounded and remains in a state of recovery.
If you wish to meet Them, I will convey your request.
I see the thirst for truth in your eyes. It is clear that doubts still linger in your heart. Please, voice your concerns.
Fleurdelys... She was the emissary of the Sentinel, and we are grateful for her contributions.
Twenty years ago, during the Dark Tide, she sacrificed herself to seal the calamity. She fulfilled her duties in this world and returned to the <color=yellow>divine embrace</color>.
Do you know how the Dark Tide came into being?
In Rinascita, wars were waged in the name of faith, tearing apart the Sentinel as our faith divided, weakening Their divine power.
The Dark Tide's true essence is the divine blood shed from the Sentinel's wounds.
That tragic past left deep scars, and with Their divine power drained, They could not prevent the Dark Tide's surge twenty years ago.

The Blessed Maiden chose to martyr herself. She <color=yellow>once again</color> resonated with the Sentinel and, through her sacrifice, restored some of Their divine power, bringing an end to the Dark Tide.

Yet, the Sentinel remains in a state of healing and still requires a mortal representative. Following the Blessed Maiden's departure, I was granted new authority to cleanse the aftermath of the Dark Tide.
I received the Divinity's blessing and became the new Enlightened One. By Their will, I fulfill the tasks left unfinished in this world.
Therefore, we must unify all beliefs, ensuring the purity and unity of our will to prevent another tragedy...

(He said she "once again resonated with the Sentinel," was that really a Second Resonance Awakening? Sentinel Jué had a trial with Jinhsi, but my permission was needed to transfer the Sentinel's power...)
I swear, my words are without deceit.
I see in your eyes that you have walked further on the path of justice than I anticipated.
O dear Sentinel… please forgive my transgressions.
The Dark Tide brought us a bloodstained lesson. To keep our people from faltering, I bound myself to silence, locking away what I witnessed on that fateful day.
Fleurdelys, the Unrighteous, deceived us all. She was not the Blessed Maiden chosen by the Sentinel... The true maiden has yet to reveal herself.
You must know that a being capable of rivaling our Divinity exists in this world—humanity's eternal adversary, the evil of all civilizations... the Threnodian.
As the Sentinel has Their Resonator, so does the Threnodian.
Fleurdelys was shaped—both body and spirit—by our ancient enemy. Her actions were intended to plunge this city into fear and chaos.
This is the truth I witnessed—Fleurdelys was the <color=yellow>Threnodian's Resonator</color>.

Twenty years ago, during the Dark Tide, she sacrificed herself to seal the calamity. She fulfilled her duties in this world and returned to the <color=yellow>divine embrace</color>.
Do you know how the Dark Tide came into being?
In Rinascita, wars were waged in the name of faith, tearing apart the Sentinel as our faith divided, weakening Their divine power.
The Dark Tide's true essence is the divine blood shed from the Sentinel's wounds.
That tragic past left deep scars, and with Their divine power drained, They could not prevent the Dark Tide's surge twenty years ago.

The Blessed Maiden chose to martyr herself. She <color=yellow>once again</color> resonated with the Sentinel and, through her sacrifice, restored some of Their divine power, bringing an end to the Dark Tide.

Yet, the Sentinel remains in a state of healing and still requires a mortal representative. Following the Blessed Maiden's departure, I was granted new authority to cleanse the aftermath of the Dark Tide.
I received the Divinity's blessing and became the new Enlightened One. By Their will, I fulfill the tasks left unfinished in this world.
Therefore, we must unify all beliefs, ensuring the purity and unity of our will to prevent another tragedy...

(He said she "once again resonated with the Sentinel," was that really a Second Resonance Awakening? Sentinel Jué had a trial with Jinhsi, but my permission was needed to transfer the Sentinel's power...)
I swear, my words are without deceit.
I see in your eyes that you have walked further on the path of justice than I anticipated.
O dear Sentinel… please forgive my transgressions.
The Dark Tide brought us a bloodstained lesson. To keep our people from faltering, I bound myself to silence, locking away what I witnessed on that fateful day.
Fleurdelys, the Unrighteous, deceived us all. She was not the Blessed Maiden chosen by the Sentinel... The true maiden has yet to reveal herself.
You must know that a being capable of rivaling our Divinity exists in this world—humanity's eternal adversary, the evil of all civilizations... the Threnodian.
As the Sentinel has Their Resonator, so does the Threnodian.
Fleurdelys was shaped—both body and spirit—by our ancient enemy. Her actions were intended to plunge this city into fear and chaos.
This is the truth I witnessed—Fleurdelys was the <color=yellow>Threnodian's Resonator</color>.

dialogs.content: Sailors cheer as hearts ignite, soon we'll break these chains so tight. Set the course, embrace the storm, sailing on 'til light is born...
Oh, hello! I'm writing a sea shanty!
Did you know, Ragunna gondolier's songs are usually in 3/4 time. It matches the flow of water perfectly.
When they row, their strokes go "slow dip, quick lift," which fits that rhythm.
But for our troupe, we use a 4/4 signature with strong and weak beats. It's catchy and perfect for sailors to sing along to as we work together to tackle the waves.
Actually... boarding the Pilgrim's Sail was my choice.
I used to compose hymns for the Order. Sounds prestigious, hm?
But the same old rhythm and lyrics started to wear on me. Music should be alive! So I decided to take the pilgrimage, believing I'd find new inspiration from the divinity.

Hmph, you probably already know what the pilgrimage really is. I was foolish to believe the Order's lies, but luckily, the troupe found me and brought me in. Ah, have you seen any of our performances perhaps?
We don't do those lofty soliloquies that give you existential dread. That doesn't mean our plays are shallow—they're just more hopeful and speak directly to the heart.
We do Commedia Improvviso, a style of play that's all about those fleeting, beautiful moments of everyday life.
We sing of love that endures, enemies who become allies in the fight against evil...
The Order may scoff at such stories, but they're real, human stories—full of ambition, dignity, and everything that makes us human.
Traveling with the troupe, I've learned to see the beauty in the small things, and I've met people facing similar and unique life struggles.
Only those who walk in the fields can really see how the crops grow. It's the same with music. You can't truly know it until you've listened.
That's why I'm always chatting with the crew, gathering ideas for my ballads and shanties—the true rhyme of our time.
The Cloudcaster... Oh, I use its base as a desk. Our first mate lent it to me so I could write more comfortably.
Here it is. Careful, it's heavy.

dialogs.content: C'mon, fish. Come to my net.
Me? Just prepping dinner. The storm's passed, so it's the perfect time for fishing!
The captain once told me a secret: the fiercer the storm, the more fish it brings. Sometimes we even see fish swept up by the wind, raining down from the sky!
Usually, yeah. But when we dock on an island, the captain and first mate will buy some other food from the locals.
Legal? Ha, who cares! We're not even a legitimate troupe according to the Order.
Back in Ragunna, I was just a fledgling fisherman when I accidentally caught an Orastie.
Turns out it's a sacred fish, only meant as an offering to the Sentinel. Mortals aren't allowed to catch it… but it swam right into my net! Not really my fault, was it?
Though, the Order didn't see it that way. They banished me here, like tossing a fish onto dry land.
Luckily, the troupe found me. I can still fish like I used to. Otherwise, I'd probably be dead or living as a pirate.
Though, to be honest, life here ain't too different from a pirate's, except we're not hunting for treasure but for smiles and cheers from our punters!
Yeah. I borrowed the reel for my fishing rod.
We scavenge all sorts of stuff from the beach and fix them up as needed. Nothing goes to waste! Don't be fooled by appearances, this stuff can be pretty versatile!

I'd rather be a wild flower, ignored by all, in my own power. Than a rose that bends and sways, bathed in grace, but lost in dismay...
Isn't it obvious? I'm practicing for the Carnevale!
I'm the troupe's soprano and helmswoman. Steering Rinascita's Echo ship isn't just about strength, it's about resonating with the Echoes.
After years at sea, I've learned that some Echoes are sensitive to our songs and will react to them in different ways.
The Order warns of sirens lurking in the Stormy Sea's mists, but they don't scare me. I'll show them who the real siren of these waters really is!
Who knows? Ask the Order and they'll give you a hundred reasons.
I can't even remember how long I drifted on that Pilgrim's Sail, but the troupe found me just in time and took me in.
What's past is past. It's the present that counts. Let go of the bad days and enjoy the moment. This is the way to live, hm?
Cloudcaster... Hmm, it does ring a bell.
Here, the resonance unit. It helps me find the right pitch and rhythm. Works like a charm! You should give it a try too.

dialogs.content: In the presence of the just Divinity, feel free to express your doubts. I shall speak without reservation.
I swear by the great Sentinel Imperator there will be no deceit in my words.
We must create a land that aligns with the Sentinel's vision. We must purge this land of individuals who stray from the righteous path to ensure that our collective will remains unified and pure.
However, we honor the deeds of Napoli II, the founding Primus, and offer those who have strayed a chance for atonement.
The Pilgrim's Sail follows Napoli's path. He too once endured this arduous journey, yet emerged victorious, earning an audience with the Sentinel.
The trials are not mere sufferings but steps toward redemption. The penitent who confront the trials with sincerity will be allowed to return to the divine's embrace.
Unity is our shield, bound by the law of eternal continuity.
Though we revel in the joy of the Carnevale, we must also be vigilant.
For division is a chronic disease plaguing this city. The growing indulgence among our citizens has already invited divine punishment.
We, as stewards of divine will, must guide the people, erecting barriers of reason against the floods of passion. This is the only way to withstand the ever-changing tides.
We uphold the Sentinel's principles of justice. The gates to our divine land remain open to all who seek it.
This is a city of inclusiveness, welcoming all visitors… including those who try to overstep their bounds.
These charlatans misled our people with lies and flattery, diverting them from the divine will.
But your timely intervention corrected their course, sparing them from a ruinous fate. Once again, I offer my sincerest gratitude.
May the Divinity bless you, and may you always walk the path of righteousness.

dialogs.content: How beautiful... but why was it covered?
Really? You don't know this painting?
Isn't it just a landscape?
Be my witness, {PlayerName}—what I'm about to say is purely to satisfy our Acolyte's curiosity. No hidden agenda.

This piece, titled "Ballad Beneath the Stars," may appear simple at first—just a shepherd tending his flock under a vast sky. However, the pattern on the shepherd's clothes resembles the Order's emblem, only flipped upside down, and the number of stars matches the recorded blessings bestowed by our Sentinel Imperator.

What's more, the number of sheep is the same as the Sentinel's wings. Given that some fanatics claim the Sentinel's divine messages are fabrications, when you connect the dots, doesn't it seem like this shepherd is hinting at something?
Uh... What?
According my interpretation of the Codex, I don't see how this painting implies anything untoward.
Maybe not to you or some of your fellow Acolytes, and certainly not to the Montellis or the painter. But there are others who don't share that view and their voices are often the loudest.
That's why this painting is covered—to avoid stirring up trouble.
Very prudent, but it's still a shame people can't admire its beauty anymore.
What about the risk of people slandering the Order? Doesn't that bother you?
Just like some will appreciate a piece of art, others will hate or misinterpret it. The same goes for the Order.
People's views are shaped by their backgrounds and experiences. What's precious to one might be another's poison.
Everyone is entitled to their opinion. As long as they genuinely believe it, I don't see a problem.
Locking this painting away is perhaps the best option for now, but I believe it will eventually return to where it belongs, for everyone to see.
If more people thought like you, we'd see a lot less trouble in the world.
