content.content: Are these Echoes the Archdemon in the opera?

dialogs.content: Oh, no. They're just abandoned Echoes.
They used to have homes and their own masters. They still don't understand why they got kicked out all of a sudden one day.
Even after being abandoned, they never forgot about their masters and managed to find their way home... but their masters were no longer there.

They scoured the whole of Rinascita, refusing to give up and accept the truth... But even now, when they've reached this Land of the Banished, they still couldn't find a single trace of their masters.
Just when they were about to lose hope, they found solace in the emotional frequencies left on personal items.
So they made this place their home. Little by little, they scavenged things to bring the home from their memories to life.
That's how they came across the "star."
Yes. They're not really the brawling type. The Tacet Discords scare them, so they sneak around, grabbing anything not nailed down while trying not to get caught.
With so many Tacet Discords wandering around the Strand, all they can do is scatter Golden Fleece, spooking the Tacet Discords to give them the chance to sneak out.
They're willing to risk it all to find trinkets to make this place... feel more like home.
Whether you're a person or an Echo, everybody needs a place to call home.
They heard the Pegasus opera from their masters.
That's why they went for the star when they saw it rolling away. They wanted the good, hopeful frequencies it was radiating.
These Echoes knew the star wasn't theirs, but they weren't keen on giving it up, either. So they cooked up all those spooky tricks to scare us away.
Turns out, this maze wasn't hiding an Archdemon or a hero. Just a bunch of Fools.
Good idea. Let's bring these Echoes along. Plus we could use some extra help with the opera.
And all this stuff they worked so hard to collect... Let's bring it with us too. It must mean a lot to them.

dialogs.content: As the tides receded, a new world and an unexplored adventure awaited you.
Yangyang and Chixia found you unconscious at the Gorges of Spirits. Together, you decided to head to Huanglong's Jinzhou City, marking the beginning of your journey.

Jinzhou, a border city in Huanglong, had long been a battleground against the Threnodian Ovathrax. The Midnight Rangers, led by General Jiyan, fought tirelessly against the waves of Tacet Discords—nightmarish entities created by the Threnodian—near the Norfall Barrens...

Meanwhile, a mysterious organization known as the Fractsidus operated covertly within Jinzhou. They were aiming to resurrect the Threnodian. Somehow, they seemed especially interested in you, going so far as to extend an invitation...

You met Jinhsi, the Magistrate of Jinzhou. She explained the double threats Jinzhou was facing: external attacks from the resurgent Threnodian, and internal turmoil caused by the mysterious disappearance of Jinzhou's Sentinel.
As the Magistrate and the Sentinel's Resonator, Jinhsi resolved to travel to Mt. Firmament and uncover the truth about Jinzhou's missing Sentinel, Jué. A confrontation seemed unavoidable...

The rise of the TD Outbreak unleashed Ovathrax's latest creation: the Dreamless, an incomplete entity. With Jinzhou City under siege, you joined the battle, eventually defeating the Dreamless and absorbing it with your bare hands.
Jinzhou's immediate crisis was averted, but Magistrate Jinhsi was nowhere to be found...
You sought guidance from Sanhua, who directed you to a ferry near Mt. Firmament. There, you encountered Changli, your "Wayfinder" into the mountain.

This secret realm, where the flow of time warped and twisted, required a price for entry. However, you seemed curiously unaffected by the temporal distortion, while Changli seemed unbothered by its effects...

Within Mt. Firmament's Hongzhen settlement, you discovered that many animals and residents had been frozen in time, trapped by the erratic temporal flows. The Fractsidus had also infiltrated the area.

Xinyi, the mayor of Hongzhen, informed you that Jinhsi had only recently departed for Mt. Firmament's peak, in search of the Sentinel. Due to the temporal distortions, what had been days to you was merely moments inside the mountain.

Deep within the Mianloong Chamber, you finally found Jinhsi. Together, you faced the Sentinel, Jué. Jué explained its dilemma: to keep its power from spiraling out of control, it had chosen to remain confined within Mt. Firmament.
If the situation continued, its only recourse would have been to freeze time across all of Jinzhou, hoping future generations could find a solution to undo the damage...

At the mountain's peak, you stood by Jinhsi as she endured Jué's trial, proving the strength of human will. With your help, she stabilized and inherited the Sentinel's power, finally bringing an end to the temporal chaos on Mt. Firmament...
Jué revealed the truth: You were none other than its Arbiter, the founder of Jinzhou.
Jinhsi's unyielding resolve, coupled with the Temporal Mandate granted by Jué with your approval, allowed her to make it through the impossible trial.
Following Jué’s guidance, you set out on a new path, seeking answers to the mysteries of your origins. Your next destination is the base of an enigmatic organization known as the Black Shores.

You confronted a crisis in the Port City of Guixu alongside Yangyang. Shortly after, the Shorekeeper guided you to the Black Shores, a place shrouded in mystery. The Tethys System of the Black Shores had suffered a catastrophic failure, unleashing data-based pollution that corroded everything it touched.
Once again guided by the Shorekeeper, you delved deeper into the Black Shores, determined not only to save this ravaged place but also to recover memories of your past...
The Shorekeeper revealed that you were once the leader and founder of the Black Shores, an ancient organization spanning ages, with her serving as your loyal assistant.
The current crisis, it seemed, was intricately tied to your forgotten past, and the Lament recorded by the Tethys System during the disaster in Port City of Guixu held crucial secrets...
To resolve the chaos caused by the Tethys System, you and the Shorekeeper entered a simulation it had created, reliving the final hour before the Lament struck Port City of Guixu.
As the disaster drew near, the Tethys System tried to absorb you as its new core. In a desperate bid to protect you, the Shorekeeper was sucked into a black hole...

You reclaimed the mantle of leadership, steering the Black Shores toward redemption. You broke free from the mistakes of the past, liberated the innocent trapped in endless suffering, and rescued the Shorekeeper from the Tethys System's grasp.

Now free from the burden of her mission, the Shorekeeper revealed another clue. She suggested that the key to understanding your connection with Abby—and Abby's recent strange symptoms—might lie within Rinascita.
Rinascita is a nation to the southeast of the Black Shores, making the Black Shores archipelago the perfect starting point for your journey...

dialogs.content: Grandpa, what’s the Carnevale like?
Well, there are so many stories about the Carnevale…

At first, it was a festival to thank the Sentinel. Back then, people had just escaped the sorrow of the Lament. They’d lost their homes and felt a deep respect for the Sentinel, so the ceremonies were always very serious.
One day, the Sentinel’s voice came down from the heavens:
"Solemnity is not the only name of gratitude or remembrance." The Sentinel wanted people to build a future with joy and hope, to honor the past by living fully in the present.

Since then, everyone began following the Sentinel’s guidance. They put on their fine clothes, sang their favorite songs, and put on plays. Gradually, the Carnevale turned into the celebration we know today.
Every year, the Sentinel chooses the best performer and gifts them the Laurel as a sign of encouragement.
One of my old friends was actually a Laureate, hehe...
For kids like you, this festival is a time to hang out with friends and eat all kinds of special treats.
Wow! So… does that mean I don't have to do homework as well?
Hooray! Carnevale! Why can’t we have it more often, Grandpa?
Ah, that's a bit complicated, dear. But don't worry, Grandpa will explain it all to you one day…

dialogs.content: Before you stands a man clad in pure white—or rather, a hologram of him—and his grand throne.
Though merely a projection, there is an undeniable gravity and majesty to his presence.
This must be Fenrico, the Primus of the Order of the Deep, just as Priest Alessio described.
From what you’ve gathered and experienced, it seems clear that he is the Resonator of the Sentinel, Imperator.

You take a moment to study his figure. A golden mask conceals half of his face, while the other half reveals a deep furrow in his brow. His gaze lowered, carrying an unreadable expression. What lies behind it? Compassion? Or perhaps something deeper, such as... an unspeakable grief?
Why would he leave this projection in the Cathedral?
As you mull over these questions, a sudden chill creeps over you. For a fleeting moment, you feel as if his gaze has shifted, directed straight at you. But when you look again, his face is unchanged.
Was it an illusion? You can’t be sure. But for now, you’d best focus on tracking down the channel Gilberto used to make his escape.

dialogs.content: My friend from afar, I see you're getting close to the Montellis.
Even though Fisalia has been quiet, we still have ears everywhere.
But I want to give you a heads-up—don't trust them too much.

Phoebe?

My parents won't let me leave the Fisalia district, so I can only learn about the outside world through her.
Our elders always say the other side is dangerous, full of bad people. But the new stories Phoebe brings back are always exciting!

dialogs.content: Levito, oh... Levito...
You were a true genius. And me? A mere mediocrity... a petty person even. I betrayed you...
Huh? Who's there?
...Never mind. Friend, if you have a moment, could you indulge me in a brief confession?
Do you know Levito? He was once the Order's lead musician.
I saw him as my primary rival for the chief musician position and went head to head against him on every matter.
To ensure I got the spot, I publicly disparaged his work. I stooped so low as to spread rumors that his work broke the Order's doctrines. All the slandering I did... They worked. Led to his downfall.
I did these things because I was simply jealous of his talent. I couldn't compose such beautiful pieces, nor conduct the Vox Sancti to perform in such perfect unity...
To this day, I still cannot surpass him.
Then words came suddenly one day that he boarded the Pilgrim's Sail. I never heard from him again... only later did I learn that the appalling truth of the pilgrimage.
If anything happened to Levito during his pilgrimage, my part in this shall not be pardoned...
If I could, I would tell him in person of my remorse...
Every night, I repent and punish myself with unbearable guilt. But when daylight comes, I put on my mask again.
Thank you for listening. As you can see, my arrogance... is just a facet of my self-loathing and guilt...
I fear my secret being revealed, yet my heart can't stop whispering it in the night...
This guilt... it's nearly crushing me...

dialogs.content: Here's to a world of discoveries and wonders! Welcome to the Pioneer Association of Ragunna.
The Pioneer Association of Ragunna operates under our visual production division, the Wutherium Film Studio.
We're dedicated to capturing reality through our lenses, showing not just the devastation of disasters but also the transformations they bring.
Our mission here is to capture and preserve these changes to offer people a new way to see the world.
Whenever you need it, C-MOSS and I will be ready to capture every important moment for you.
I'm confident that we'll create many treasured memories here in Ragunna.
Pleasure to meet you! I am Fulmine, the head of the Wutherium Film Studio. We are the visual production division of the Pioneer Association.
Umm... Did you happen to pick up any film on your way here?
Well, like the ones on my head.
My Resonance power, "Film Memory," lets me turn memorable moments and dreams into strands of film-shaped hair.
Nifty, right? Sometimes even lost ideas resurface in the film!
But lately, all those late nights have started taking a toll... I'm losing hair, and along with it, some of my precious film.
Some of it is a bit... personal. If anyone ever saw them, I'd just die of embarrassment—ahhhh!
So, {PlayerName}, if you come across any of my films lying around, could you please return them to me?
...And um, promise me you won't peek, okay?
Here's to a world of discoveries and wonders! Until we meet again!

We're debating our next destination. We're still on a Pan-Ragunna Tour, after all.

See, each island nation has its own preferences, you know.

Take Septimont, for example. They favor plays like "The Three Hundred Knights of Capitoline" and "Assassin's Journey"—you know, action-packed, filled with historical sagas and war. That's their thing.
I like them too, but Elisha doesn't share my enthusiasm.

I'm giving Lario a good scrub. See all those barnacles? Still plenty of cleaning to do!
When we first found Lario, he was covered in seaweed and barnacles, roaring in a way that could turn the bravest sailor's knees to jelly.
Captain Brant said everything was fine and went to speak to the creature alone. We were all a bundle of nerves, I'll tell you that much.
When he came back, he told us this big fellow's name was Lario. No harm intended, he said, just thought we "smelled nice" and wanted to be friends.
We didn't understand at first, but now we know Lario can't clean himself at sea, and over time, he gets covered in barnacles. Must be terribly uncomfortable for him.
Lario is an Echo, so nobody knows why barnacles still grow on him. Another mystery, I suppose.
Anyway, whenever we went ashore we gave him a good scrub. That's when we really started to bond. He was so happy he even let us dance on his back!

dialogs.content: Thank you, Cantarella, for everything you've done for us for all these years.
Now that we're leaving, you'll be left alone here…
You should never have had to bear such a heavy burden.
I still remember what you told me back then, during the trials. You said you wanted to leave this place behind, go somewhere far away where no one knew you, and live freely...
But now, you're staying in this cold castle, bearing it all alone…
As long as I am the head of Fisalia, what happened here remains buried. No more trials, no more innocent lives caught in this web.
My freedom for theirs—a fair exchange, wouldn't you say?
It's time to leave, my dear.

Mr. Aalto was right. Bloom Bearers attract other Bloom Bearers!
Sorry, I forgot to introduce myself first. My name's Ariosto, and I am the undercover Bloom Bearer sent here to investigate Rinascita's recent issues.
The Black Shores has also sent other Bloom Bearers to Rinascita, but to keep things under the radar of the Order, we decided to split up.
If you head southeast toward Septimont, you'll likely run into some of our colleagues. Compared to Ragunna, Bloom Bearers enjoy a bit more freedom there—less surveillance and fewer rules to follow.

But... how should I put it? Things aren't quite as smooth in Septimont. Our operations face their own set of challenges, and the Bloom Bearers' work there hasn't been progressing as well as we'd hoped.
As you know, the Black Shores is a neutral organization, so we don't have the right to meddle in their affairs without the consent of the local officials.
Our relationship with Rinascita's city-states is… well, "delicate" is one way to put it. We've been providing warnings about the Lament crisis—Ragunna being the prime example, of course.
By the way... Come closer, gotta keep our voice low for this... Have you run into any... obstructions from the Order during your mission?
I see. It happened to me as well. On the surface, Ragunna appears peaceful, but behind the scenes, the Order has been plotting something.
People from the Order was hot on my tail when I was investigating this matter, and even had my Terminal taken from me. Luckily the Montellis extended a helping hand...
It was the same Ms. Carlotta who told me that a member of the Black Shores would be arriving in Ragunna soon. I decided to find {Male=him;Female=her} quickly and share the information I have.
I borrowed this costume and a mask from the Montelli to blend in with the crowd, so I could get back to the city during the Carnevale. Well, at least my hard work finally paid off.
Us Bloom Bearers, we endure hardship, but the Lament must be stopped at all costs! That's our Bloom Bearer Creed!
You must already have some sense of Ragunna's situation. Now, let me share a wild thought with you...
You saw that Sentinel statue in Ragunna, right? That statue is strikingly different from the appearance of Sentinel Imperator we recorded in the Tethys System.
Now, take a deep breath—because I'm about to say something big. What if, just what if... the people of Ragunna have been believing in a false Sentinel all along?
Wait... Enough talk for today. I can't shake the feeling that we're being watched.
My mission isn't finished. I'll stay in Rinascita and continue digging into their historical records about the Sentinel. My next stop is Whisperwind Haven. If fate allows, we'll meet again.

content.content: Or perhaps, you already have plans with someone else?

dialogs.content: My answer is no to both questions.
If someone were to approach me with a special drink right now, I wouldn't decline a conversation.
But at least when I came here, I simply wanted some fresh air.
The day is beautiful. The performers' melodies drift from the opera house, and the streets are alive with chatter and shouts of people.
The city and its people shimmer—golden, vibrant, precious.
In this fleeting moment, I can forget about the troubles.
Oh, you know how it is—endless deliberations, meticulous planning. There are a lot of things to consider.
Like... My new dress from Nyarla's? What to wear for the next ball? Or perhaps which treasures to bid for at the auction?
Haha, okay, I'll cut it.
Capollo... He has been disowned and dealt with. It's left me with a tangle of new challenges to manage.
My priorities remain the same: doing whatever that benefits the family. But now, with this new role entrusted to me, I carry new responsibilities—and with them, new strengths.
As the next head of the family, it's my duty to face these responsibilities head-on, and to shape myself into the leader this position demands.
But before this fleeting moment of peace is stolen away by duty, on an afternoon like this—
Will you sit with me, Cat's Eye? Share a drink, share a bite?
Let's set aside the "codes" hidden behind every glass for once. Like ordinary folk, we'll just savor the flavors for what they are, as they were meant to be.
Thankfully, you have no pressing matters to attend to. On such a peaceful afternoon, sharing this moment with Carlotta feels like the right choice.

content.content: Like the "Scarlet Velvet Ribbon" tied to Scarlet Velvet?

dialogs.content: Precisely.
"Opal" is more than just a drink—it's your key to reach me. Order it at any bar in Rinascita, and the Montelli network will ensure your message finds me.
Of course, you could also order it to flaunt our bond. It'll grant you the protection of Montelli.
Why? Because its recipe is a secret known only to me and a select few Montellis.
Hehe, there's no need for promises. I've already placed my trust in you, completely.
Alright, then. Here's the recipe—listen closely. White rum, rose nectar, pomegranate juice, a pinch of black pepper, and a touch of fritillaria powder.
Got it?
Alright, I'll repeat it for you. White rum, rose nectar, pomegranate juice, a pinch of black pepper, and a touch of fritillaria powder.
Be sure to remember it well.

content.content: What would it take to create a special blend?

dialogs.content: You mean a signature drink named after you, {PlayerName}?
Let's come up with one, then. Feel free to choose from any flavor or color, or select a symbol that resonates with you.
No limits—let your creativity shape your perfect beverage. You'll find it in the bars once you make your choice.
...You've always felt a bit distant to me, whether you're making decisions or fighting. It fits the first impression I had of you.
Oh? I didn't expect you'd go for an unusual blend. It might actually work pretty well as a "code."
My opinion? Hmm, that's hard to say... Maybe something with a base of herbs and fruity flavors, rather than a pure grain spirit.
It reminds me of the quiet kindness tucked away beneath your remarkable strength.
But there's no need to rush. You'll have plenty of time to decide what kind of blend embodies you best.
And before that, shall we savor this moment?
You understand her unspoken message—some questions aren't meant to be answered right away.
She wants to preserve this moment of tranquility, untouched by worry or haste. By your side, she feels at peace, and she hopes you feel the same.

It feels like nothing ever happened, as if it was just a fleeting night's dream. But you know it was real, because Cantarella stands right beside you.
*yawn* That was a really long nap.

Our family's purpose has always been clear—to resist the Threnodian's spiritual interference and hold fast to our faith in the Sentinel.
The cruel trials were designed to find a Maiden with an unbreakable will, someone who could withstand the Threnodian's whispers and fix her eyes on the true light.
Yet, in pursuit of that "noble cause," innocent lives were sacrificed without question.
I can't accept the so-called "necessary sacrifice," one that tramples the will of others in the name of duty. It's nothing but living off the weak.
Though it's important to kindle the flames, none should forget those burned to ashes—those lives shouldn't have been squandered.
After all, we are more than just firewood.
Yes. When I took up the Sword of Divinity, I felt a <ano=Fleurdelys>presence</ano>, someone far more capable, more suitable. A new possibility emerged.
I asked the Sentinel to transfer my Second Awakening power to that girl.
The Sentinel had always wielded the power of separation, but instead agreed to my proposal to combine our strengths. With that power, she confronted the Threnodian.
We triumphed, for the moment, but the Threnodian proved to be more difficult than we expected.
To stop the brutal Divine Trials and secure us the final victory, I chose to become the family head, drawing on every resource available to achieve our goal.
I pretended to align with the Order to keep the Threnodian off guard, all while searching for a way to fully liberate the Sentinel and end the Threnodian once and for all.
And then... I found you.
Hehe… I have been watching you from the moment you set foot in Rinascita.
Now, I daresay I know you inside out.
Just as you chose your path, I've chosen mine. I will see it through, whatever it may cost.
Besides, compared to what you've endured, my hardships aren't worth mentioning.
You defeated the Threnodian in the Inverted Tower, saved the people of Rinascita, and freed those young girls... and me as well.
The girls are now back home, and the Threnodian's whispers have finally faded from this castle.
And with the Order's concessions, the shadows over Rinascita are vanishing. Peace has come to us once more.
Thanks to you, the days of pain and sacrifice have ended. A calm life… that is the miracle you've brought.
As the head of Fisalia, I must offer you a fitting reward for all the efforts you made.
An elixir for eternal youth, perhaps? No, judging from the power of your Awakening, it seems you may already possess that.
Then, let it be the elixir that turns stone into gold.
I, Cantarella Fisalia, hereby offer {PlayerName} the family's entire legacy—every elixir and every hidden secret.
Hehe… the Fisalias make no unprofitable bargains. It's my privilege to give it all to you.
Hehe, this is "our" home now.
It's been a long day. You deserve a sweet, peaceful sleep.
Here, a special elixir I've prepared with Albizia flowers—their gentle, lingering fragrance can waft through reality into your dream.
Now, close your eyes... and rest. Good night.

dialogs.content: Sails of the departed drift on and on, souls above the clouds, hearts claimed by the sea...
Oh, hello, {PlayerName}.
It is... this one came from a rather unusual experience.
Tell me, {PlayerName}. What do you think of the sea?
Someone once said the sea is a city of the dead. You can hear the endless cries of the wind and waves, but never the voice of anything living.

When you spend days, weeks, maybe even years adrift, loneliness creeps in and twists despair into something monstrous. And yet, when you see a flicker of light out there—something you dare call "hope"…
That's when people stop thinking straight.
Is this from someone from the Fool's Troupe?
No, it was someone who's long gone now.
He died ten years ago in a shipwreck. I wasn't there to see it happen, and his face has almost faded from my memory. But...
On my last voyage, I saw him. He was on another ship. A lively one if I might add. I could hear the laughter and clink of glasses.
Hold on. Didn't you just say it's rare to see anything living on the sea?
Exactly. That's what makes it unusual. When I saw him, he looked just as he was all those years ago, not a single day older. And in that moment, everything I'd forgotten about him came rushing back.
Are you saying… he might still be alive?
Surviving ten years on the sea, without even a scratch? What do you think, {PlayerName}? How likely is that?
Almost impossible, right? My thoughts exactly.
Yet when the light of "hope" is right in front of you, you can't help but chase after it. No matter how violent the waves or impossible the odds, you have to see it for yourself.
Sadly, when we got closer, Battier and Brant reported back the waters were teeming with Tacet Discords.
It would end badly. No doubt about it.
That's why I need your help, {PlayerName}.

I'll admit, this seems more of a personal request from my side. But when you're out there dealing with those Tacet Discords or trying to find the man, regardless of the results your safety comes above all else.
He had the same blue hair and eyes as me. He used to call it the color of the sea, a blessing from the ocean itself.
After he died, I stopped believing in nonsense like these. Most sailors still prefer to hold onto their superstitions though, as a way to boost their spirits before heading off to sea.
{PlayerName}, I wish you safety... and the best of luck.

dialogs.content: {PlayerName}, fancy running into you here.
Won't you dine with me? Ms. Margherita asked me to sample her newest pizza, but my goodness, these portions...
Did you hear what the Order's Acolytes found while clearing the abandoned library? A manuscript of a poem with an accompanying music sheet.
The public has already caught wind of its contents. Did you know it was signed as Golden Anthem?
They say it was their last work, written aboard the Pilgrim's Sail. I reckon the original finder fished it out of the sea and put it in the library, not knowing what it was.
Shhh... quiet. They're criminals. Best not to mention them in public.
Shh, that name is not to be spoken of in Ragunna.
Simply put, the Golden Anthem was once a renowned Poets Society.
Their three members were once the Sentinel's cantors, but the Order banished them for insulting the Divinity.
Allegedly, their Pilgrim's Sail caught fire and none on board survived, and thus their last known work disappeared.
Well, since the manuscript is no longer a secret, how does the tune sound?
Give me a second, let me think...
Ah! Hear that? It's exactly what they're playing now!
Well... it would appear they were possessed by Daemons, just as this very article suggests.

This article was recently published in the Ragunna Literary Journal... Quite the perspective, wouldn't you say? Vengeance borne of resentment—such dark and twisted characters are hard to resist.
Perhaps someone unwittingly played that tune just now and opened the Plushies to possession by the Daemons.
Then again, it's all conjecture. Those in the Poets Society died years ago, and who's to say what really happened?
Now, if those vengeful spirits really do exist... well, out of all the patrons here, they went straight for you, {PlayerName}. Curious and curiouser...
By the way, it just so happens that I made a copy of the Poet Society's last work.

Follow the song to find her!
{PlayerName}, Carlotta, it's been too long!
You really must adore that song. I remember hearing you sing it when I was little.
When I was a child, whenever I passed by Ciaccona's house, I'd always hear music drifting from the courtyard. Lively, spirited and so full of emotion...
Oh, I remember it well! Those two guards of yours were like giants from Septimont, easily two hundred pounds of pure muscle!
Back then Ciaccona's family conducted the Order's choir.
How should I put it... Well, as they say, families are always rising and falling.
But a song is a song whether sung in a grand hall or beneath the open sky. As for family matters... let the past stay where it belongs.
Anyway, the two of you came in such a hurry. I suppose you're not here to take in the music.
Oh so... So you eavesdropped on a man rambling on in C3-sharp, and then poof, out pops a "monster"?
It is the point! I need to know what kind of music could possibly have the power to conjure up those "monsters" of yours.
Let me see... it should sound something like this! About that sharp, {PlayerName}.
I know right? We should suggest to Ms. Margherita that she add new signage: "Sing with civility, it starts with us!"
Ahem, can we discuss restaurant etiquette later?
Of course. But I still need to know what kind of music could possibly have the power to conjure up those "monsters" of yours.
The Golden Anthem... that name should never be spoken.
They're criminals. To conspire with them is to risk banishment at sea, or worse.
Don't worry. This won't be the first time we've crossed paths with the Order.
...Fine.
From what you've told me, the composers of this poem cursed Rinascita spelling the fall of Ragunna.
When the poem is played some type of horror appears. If I understand correctly, that's what attacked you and Carlotta.
If you ask me this story is a right load of codswallop. I don't believe a simple little poem could curse Rinascita.
Then you...
We need to get to the heart of this poem and music mystery. Let me join you. I can't resist a good adventure.
I'll help you find the link between the music and those Daemons. But in return, I want you to hand these pages to me for safekeeping.
Then we have a deal!
Since you believe this music summons them, how about we test it for ourselves? I've already memorized the sheet music.
It's risky, but there's no surer way to find out, wouldn't you agree, {PlayerName}?
The final work of poets banished to distant seas and condemned to death...
What, I wonder, did the verses forged in flames truly sing of?

This is where Ragunna's musicians lay their old instruments to rest.
For the people of Ragunna, the sea is everything. We live and sleep by the sea, and our souls drift out to sea when we pass.
Since an instrument is an extension of the musician, it's only fitting that it's buried by the sea. May its dreams be long and sweet before returning to the waves.
I'm certain this is where the poets of the Golden Anthem laid their instruments to rest before their banishment.

So I stood under that tree and prayed for an apple to fall on my head.
You know, just like in those stories where inspiration strikes after an apple hits you. And, well... at least you'd get a snack out of it.

The apples never fell. I stood under that tree until I couldn't any longer, but still no inspiration came.

What's more, the hymn we're practicing... it was composed by bad people. Teacher calls them "heretic poets."
Myron and the others never complain. They're always eager to sing praises to the Sentinel on stage.
But now, their dreams are all dashed because of me. Myron, Patero, and Shia's voices are in perfect harmony. But I can never keep up.
And I don't like this hymn. Myron and the others are too young to realize that heresy is a grave offense... But I know...
I-I just don't understand why the Order wants us to sing songs written by criminals.
The more I thought about it, the more out of rhythm I became. In the end, I could barely sing at all.
That song just now? I... I've already forgotten how it's supposed to sound.
Well... what do you think a hymn should sound like?
A hymn... as the books state, is a song of praise for the Sentinel who leads the lost to the abundant lands...
No, not that...  I mean, how does it make you feel? Try to remember what you were feeling when you were singing alone in the corner just now.
Oh... um... I didn't want to hold everyone back, and I really wanted to help everyone have a great performance at the ceremony.

To find their melody, we should try to follow the route they once took.

Oh yes, how did I miss that. The wind is the finest recorder of melodies.
It rises from the primal, churning endlessly, echoing in our ears without end. I believe the melodies left by the Poets Society were witnessed by the wind, and it will carry them to us.
Playing a tune, of course. I want to capture the mood they must have felt when they were here... I'm curious as to what they left behind.
Ciaccona plays her instrument. The wind stirs, and the melody of the Poets Society fills the air.
Rimbaud and Selena must have returned to Ragunna by now. That lithograph of the Sentinel's true form… it has to be here somewhere.
Did that gentleman guide us intentionally? Who exactly was he...
Backpack stuffed with papers, claiming to be a common artist traveling in search of inspiration.
Yet he spoke like a nobleman... But I can't afford to think about that now.
If not for his help, we'd still be singing praises to a false Sentinel!
He's right. We cannot continue to sing for the Order anymore.
We must enlighten the people of Ragunna. They deserve to know the truth.

Resentment and curses are not songs of their own style. As for the true mastermind, we still have no direct proof linking him to the Order.
We must confront his lies and put an end to these Daemon incidents...
But once the truth of the Golden Anthem and Imperator is revealed, it will no longer be just a matter of Daemons... But... is now the right time?
The will of the people is strong. This mastermind is so sure that the lies about the Sentinel will go undiscovered, and that no one will easily believe the truth.

Yes... Let's get going then.

About the Poets Society's legacy. There's something important we'd like to share. Could you help us gather everyone?

Exactly. Someone used the story of the Golden Anthem to stir the public's curiosity. This is what created the Daemons.

Surely you're not suggesting this was all the Order's doing? I dare say... such remarks would be considered a grave crime punishable by banishment.
Are you from a noble family? The city's elite have a habit of siding with the Order.
Haha, I'm afraid you misunderstand... I admit I do get that question quite often. I am but a traveling playwright.
Your presentation brings me back to a play I wrote in my youth.
A group of birds locked inside a cage. Convinced they will never fly, they do nothing but stand on a perch.
Then one day, the cage door opened. The young birds flapped their fragile wings attempting to fly, but plummeted to the ground one by one.
Many consider their fate a tragic one. What say you?
...I see it differently.
Even if they met their end falling into the abyss, they still had a chance to glimpse the sky and spread their wings.
And what of those who chose to remain in the cage, having witnessed their predecessors fall to their demise?
Will they still dare to reach for the skies after realizing the cost of choosing to fly? Does the "truth" exist to protect, or to harm? That is the question.

It was none other than Acolytes from the Order who salvaged the poets' lost works from the wreckage. They've long known of their existence and hid the poems in the Order's library.
It's possible this was a sham all along. Choosing to make it public now likely means they're using those poems to obscure the real truth.
Now, considering the fact that the untraceable article first began circulating among poets, musicians, and playwrights alike...
I think it's fair to say its author is a regular of such secret circles. He may even be the Resonator we've speculated about.
His collusion with the Order is why these rumors are allowed to run rampant in the streets.
I'll have someone follow this secret circle's trail and see what we can find.
We should also share these findings with Ciaccona. As a poet, her insights would be much appreciated.

That's strange, she was just there a moment ago.
...Just like when we were children. Gone without a trace.
When she and her family disappeared without even a goodbye.
Ms. Margherita, have you seen Ciaccona?

Thank you for letting us know, Ms. Margherita.

And here I thought you'd be much wiser than this.

Allow me to share the answer, Sir Acolyte. Do you remember the very first voice from the heavens? The one the people of Rinascita kept alive in their hearts as they built their homes on this land?
Surely you've seen The Golden Bough, yes? A play where people from various clans wear masks, singing and celebrating together. An occasion you now call... "Carnevale."
And? What of it?
It is words and songs. We are not your enemies. What you face here is something that is hard to describe, something I call "Reverberation."
It exists forever, and you can never defeat it.
Hmph. You pitiful fool. Off to the seas with that "Reverberation" you believe in so dearly.
The Order of the Deep seeks to banish us to the seas because they know they can't banish the truth...
Hear that? The bell they tolled... I will be the one to carry its sound forward.
Oh, the parallels... so striking. Just like the day the Poets Society boarded their Sail. You, Ciaccona Toccata, blaspheming against the Sentinel.
Ha! So this is the resonance they babbled on about? After all these years, another group of fools is ready to march down the same path.
Why are there always those who believe the Sentinel is some damn horse?
The poets were at least clever enough to hold their tongues. But you have the nerve to parade your blasphemy through the streets. It almost makes those poets look noble by comparison.
Is that so, Sir Acolyte? I do hope you dream of this "Sentinel" of yours every night then.
Spare me your sarcasm, you insolent bard! You're nothing but a mouthy relic, the last of what remains of your wretched family! Do you not repent for your crimes?!
Ah, so you've already tasted their fate, haven't you? You and your family, banished in the name of... blasphemy!
Such a dramatic turn of events! As cantors of the Sentinel, both the Toccata family and the Poets Society committed the same crime. Tell me, what is the connection between you and those poets?
You're nothing but a figment of my imagination. None of this concerns you. It was a price we were willing to pay. We have no regrets.

I believe the opportunity has presented itself for the truth to be—
Opportunity. Indeed... The moment of choice dawns once more.

Isn't this what you're afraid of?
You've unraveled the hand behind it all... but the Order will never allow such truths to see the light.

Surprise, surprise, the melody led me right to you.
Well... I suppose this won't count as me getting distracted, right?
If Carlotta asked you to find me, has something happened?
Lady Carlotta told me you encountered the supposed Martyred Maiden—Cartethyia.
She dispatched search teams soon after, but there's been no sign of Cartethyia since.
That's why she asked me to use my Forte to recreate the frequency you experienced at the time, to see if any details you might have missed become clearer.
Recreate the frequency?
Well, it's a little tricky to explain in words... Think of it like being in an immersive portrait. Can you tell me about your meeting with Cartethyia?
The more details the better. Even the smallest things count.

Laureate?
Our Tacet Marks are glowing again. It appears there is a special connection between them.
What is the meaning of this?
Someone used their Resonance ability to help me relive this moment, but this seems... unexpected.
How did you first come to notice me?
The Sentinel—Imperator's voice guided me to you.

Well, Imperator called you "the Lost," and Primus Fenrico claims you are the Resonator for Leviathan, the Threnodian.
But you really don't have any idea?
I... I've actually been searching for the answer to this question, too.
My memories are fragmented. I remember becoming a Resonator, and the moment I was given the name Fleurdelys.
I also remember fighting... something. But the details and the outcome of that battle are lost to me.
You seem deeply concerned about the Sentinel. Tell me, why is that?
Hmm...? You rang?
Whoa! Check it out! Our frequencies got split apart.
Basically, we're sorta in that "hover mode" you once joked about. Nothing new to me though.
Yeah. Sorta, kinda.
This must be the frequency that's entangled within you. Is it some kind of Echo?
Yes... I'm experiencing a similar kind of frequency split. Though there is little that remains of my Resonance powers.
I feel its frequency weakening... I understand why you're eager to find the Sentinel.
You said you heard the Sentinel's voice. Was there anything else They said?
They spoke of being ensnared in an inverted tower suspended in the sky.
Ensnared? Does that mean behind the seals there's...
I'm sure you've noticed that "I" was drawn here only as a frequency.
My true form currently resides inside an inverted Sonoro Sphere suspended high in the sky. At its center stands a tower, its gate locked by three seals.
I've sensed a voice calling out to me from behind them... Could it be the Sentinel?
Say, it's really faint so I barely noticed earlier... Is that a Threnodian smell I'm getting from ya?
The scent of a Threnodian...? You can perceive the Threnodian?
It's not an exact one-to-one with that big "Ova-thracula" meatball I had, but I'd never mix up a flavor I've already tasted.
Abby has a nose for these sorts of things. We came across Threnodian powers before in Jinzhou.
So it's safe to say Abby can be trusted.
Do you think I'm the Threnodian's Resonator?
If we're making assumptions, let's err on the optimistic side first.
Given your current situation, it is possible you were affected by the Threnodian's powers during your battle alongside Imperator.
That could be the reason behind losing all your power, too.
Hmm... I take it this theory would benefit you as well?
After all, that unique Echo of yours needs the Sentinel's powers for treatment, does it not?
Even in adventure tales, it's not always the witch who loses her memory, it could also be a Blessed Maiden trying to regain her powers!
In that case, it appears we share the same goal of finding the Sentinel.
Spending so much time alone in the Sonoro Sphere gave me plenty of time to consider countless possibilities.
I've braced myself for whatever may come until I find the answers I'm seeking.
I want to know what's going on with Imperator in that tower. And I want to speak with you in person.
How can I reach your Sonoro Sphere?
A part of the Sonoro Sphere is actually on land, though its outer perimeter is surrounded by a barrier.
I cannot leave, and no one can enter.
I'm afraid that won't do...
That barrier also acts as the power source that maintains the Sonoro Sphere's integrity. If it's destroyed, the entire Sphere will collapse.
And the ruins along with the Tacet Discords it houses would come crashing down on Ragunna. It would be catastrophic.
You said no one can get in. Has anyone tried?
Yes, I've occasionally sensed someone wandering outside the barrier as if searching for a way inside.
Perhaps they know something?
Any distinguishing features?
Emm... Almost like a deep-sea jellyfish?
I-I wasn't able to get a clear look. I can only describe the feeling I got from her as a Resonator.
It would seem this Resonance ability can only last for so long.
I'll look for a way to find this person you mentioned.
Something tells me you will keep your promise.
No matter the outcome, this may be my chance to find the answers I've been looking for.

Oh...

I have a feeling this is going to be a very exciting song!

Why does she want to talk with me?
Milady has expressed a desire to clear up some unfortunate misunderstandings that occurred previously.
Tell her I accept the invitation, but at a later time.

I have "Shadow of the Ancient," "Lady Bane," or maybe "Entangler of Hearts"?
Hello... That's why they're called rumors. I'm just doing my due diligence by being faithful to the source material.
So, ready to dive right in?

Word is, they select the new head of household by having candidates ingest each other's poisons and wait to see who's still breathing when it's all over.
Stories about the current head of the Fisalias get even wilder. They say she didn't go through the usual selection process. Instead, she took the throne by poisoning her predecessor.
Others say she's a master in the art of manipulation, drowning her victims in hallucinations until they agree to her terms without even realizing it.
In any case, the Fisalia family aside, she's someone you definitely want to handle with care.
If you're set on meeting her, I'd be extra careful if I were you.

(Can't rule out the possibility that they're the same person. Looks like I'll need to pay her a visit.)
{PlayerName}... {PlayerName}...
Oh, thank goodness... You're finally awake!
How are you feeling? Any headache? Tingling feet? Upset stomach?
Phew... I tried everything, but you just wouldn't wake up. I thought you were...
Wait a second, did you actually fall asleep listening to my music? Oh... It kind of breaks my heart to know you reacted like that when it wasn't even a lullaby.
No, it was really helpful.
Helpful for your sleeping troubles, hmm?
Oh...
So my Forte created a special connection that led to some unexpected developments...
The girl, is she friend or foe...? What truths lie behind the seal...? And who is that mysterious wandering figure...?
I have a feeling this is going to be a very exciting song!
Ahem... I'll pass this information on to Lady Carlotta. So, what do you plan to do next?
Pardon the intrusion. {Male=My Lord;Female=My Lady} {PlayerName}.
My name is Sebastian. As per Milady's instructions, I have been entrusted with the honor of inviting you to the Fisalia estate for a discussion.
(The Fisalia family? The one that's likely worshipping the Threnodian?)
Why does she want to talk with me?
Milady has expressed a desire to clear up some unfortunate misunderstandings that occurred previously.
Tell her I accept the invitation, but at a later time.
I will convey your message to Milady.
Didn't expect the head of the Fisalia family to come looking for you, especially while they're still in the middle of negotiations with Lady Carlotta.
She's just as unpredictable as the rumors say.
I suppose you would want to know more about her before taking up her invitation, hmm?
She's known to be a recluse and rarely makes public appearances. No one outside the family even knows her real name. They just call her the "head of the Fisalia family."
I've heard quite a few rumors. Which one would you like to hear first?
I have "Shadow of the Ancient," "Lady Bane," or maybe "Entangler of Hearts"?
Hello... That's why they're called rumors. I'm just doing my due diligence by being faithful to the source material.
So, ready to dive right in?

That won't be necessary.
To keep our honored guest waiting would be… most improper.
Especially when it was I who extended the invitation.

Honorable Laureate. The new Crown of the Carnevale.
Very well. If you insist, I see no reason to refuse.
You may also call me Cantarella.
Hmm... the Laurel is a gift of the Divinity. What claim have I to crown one as distinguished as yourself?
I should be the one to apologize for not understanding our guest's attempt at lightening the mood.
Very well. You may also call me Cantarella.
Now. Shall we proceed to my study?

Won't you have a seat?
I hope you'll accept this tea as my way of apologizing for the incident with Gilberto.
Members of the family may have troubled you, but there is no stain that can't be washed away. Every sorrow has its own way of fading, don't you think?
You still hold a grudge. Won't you accept my apology?
This tea... Is it from Jinzhou?
I see. Let's set aside such past unpleasantness for the time being.
I invited you here to ask that you might serve as a mediator.
Before we get into that, there's something I want to know.
I imagine it concerns... the Fisalia family's true beliefs?
It would seem Gilberto's mind is beyond saving.
But let's not dwell on that. What is your opinion on the current state of Ragunna, {PlayerName}?
So you've noticed something is amiss. As expected from someone who's felt the weight of a Threnodian invasion firsthand.
And what exactly do you find most unsettling?
Why haven't the Threnodian and the Sentinel ever shown themselves?
Because the Threnodian's invasion of Ragunna... has long since concluded.
The Threnodian, so named Leviathan, possesses the power to merge and assimilate. It uses distorted beliefs to spread a spiritual plague that slowly devours civilizations from within.
Though the previous two attempts were thwarted, the tall mast of the galleon that is Ragunna has already been snapped in half.
Now the blissfully ignorant masses walk hand in hand toward an abyss they cannot see.
Friend or foe? As a newcomer to this land, can you really tell them apart?

content.content: Are you implying the Order worships the Threnodian?
You're one to talk, given how strange your family's been acting.

dialogs.content: Yes and no. On one hand, there's the truth of the Order's beliefs…
On the other, there's our family. The Threnodian doesn't take kindly to those who know the truth. We've always been under Its whispers.
Once the soul fractures, the mind will follow until only a puppet remains.
Now that we've come this far, there's nothing for me to hide.
My only hope is that once you learn everything, you will carefully consider my request.

{PlayerName}, what you see in this sanctuary is the Sentinel in Their true form.
A majestic steed that galloped with the wind, not a creature of the ocean's depths.
The Order worships a half-horse, half-sea creature Divinity, a form the Sentinel assumed only after being corrupted by the Threnodian.
Although the Sentinel's will has yet to fade, who knows how much longer They can endure.
{PlayerName}. I wish to ask you to persuade the Sentinel of Jinzhou—Jué—to come to Rinascita. To save Imperator.
In return, I will agree to whatever condition or request you make.
Both Jinzhou and Jué owe you their future. That makes you the only person capable of this task.

content.content: A Sentinel cannot leave its commissioned region.
Jué leaving Jinzhou would be a betrayal of duty.
Jué is still in the middle of a recovery.

dialogs.content: I understand the position you are in. Word has it that you're currently staying at a hotel and are at odds with the Order.
Perhaps a stay at my estate would suit you, for the remainder of your time in Rinascita?
I can offer you a glimpse into Rinascita's past, and you'd be spared the Order's unwelcomed attention.
There might still be a path forward.
Carlotta once helped me interpret some stained glass images. The story it told was very similar to what you've described.
Only more biased towards the Order. It mentioned a maiden who would emerge as the Sentinel's Resonator and later save Rinascita.
Do you think that's also a lie?
Care to elaborate?
The part regarding the maiden isn't entirely fiction.
The Sentinel does indeed appoint a maiden to be Their Resonator, though not in the way the Carnevale would have you believe. No, it's through resonance with a very particular artifact.
That's because Imperator wields the power to split and manipulate space.
With it, They can withdraw a portion of power. That power's frequency will match the Imperator's own.
This is how the Sword of Divinity—Tyrvine—came to be. A blade sealed with the very powers of the Sentinel, and the artifact used to select Their Resonator.
To resonate with the sword is to resonate with the Sentinel. Only the chosen one may hope to draw it.
Then... what about Cartethyia?
The Martyred "Maiden"...? The nature of her resonance is unclear to me.
Perhaps she resonated with the Threnodian, or perhaps with the Sentinel in its corrupted form.
But choosing her could not have been the Sentinel's will. That's because...
The Maiden was already dead.

In the past, each year the Fisalia family would hold the Divine Trials to select those with the strongest will. These young women would attempt to resonate with Tyrvine's powers—while Overclocked, of course.
Though none succeeded, some saw fragments of the truth hidden within the resonance.
I was one of them... There was a moment, where I glimpsed the Sentinel's corrupted form and the inverted ruin suspended in the sky.
I also learned that only Tyrvine can break the barrier of that Sonoro Sphere.
When I awoke from that vision, I discovered a line of words inscribed onto my hand.
I would never mistake my own handwriting. That is precisely why I am searching for other possibilities.
The words were—"The Maiden is dead."
(An inverted ruin suspended in the sky... her and Cartethyia's descriptions bear many similarities.)
(If Tyrvine is the key to entering the Sonoro Sphere, it stands to reason that Imperator may have played a role in the Sphere's creation.)
(If I can confirm that Tyrvine was truly left by Imperator, at least it would prove that neither are lying.)
(Cantarella said she was Overclocking when she tried resonating with Tyrvine.)
(That's exactly what happened with Jinhsi. Could Imperator be trying to restore Their power through a Second Awakening?)
(If that's the case... my permission should cause a reaction. That's one way to confirm what they're saying.)
By all means.
...I suppose all that's left is its symbolic value.
However, do handle it with care. It is a family heirloom... I've heard of your unique methods and formidable strength.
{PlayerName}... Who are you really?
The Sentinel's... Arbiter?
No... you're likely a far more special entity.
Well, I have some information and theories of my own. Care to hear them?
Please. Enlighten me.
Just as I expected... The Threnodian "took notice" of you the moment you learned the truth.

Greetings, I am Cartethyia. And you are?
Cantarella Fisalia.
Oh, a Fisalia... It seems your ties with the Order are more complicated than they appear.
I had the privilege of watching the Blessed Maiden's performance at the Carnevale once.
I'm rather surprised. After all this time, you still look exactly as you did that day.
But you and I should be around the same age.
I'm also unsure of what's happened to me... I've been searching for answers.
This must be the Sword of Divinity—Tyrvine, the one with the Sentinel's powers sealed within.
You shouldn't have knowledge of this sword.
Memories flowed into my mind just as you entered the Sonoro Sphere, granting me information about the sword's origins.
(Cantarella said that only those who resonate with Tyrvine are granted glimpses of its knowledge...)
Would you mind if I tried touching it?
The question of whose Resonator I am... is now perfectly clear.
If I am not the Sentinel's Resonator. Then that must mean...
Don't jump to conclusions just yet. That doesn't prove you're the Threnodian's Resonator, nor that you aid Its cause.
Huh?
This connection formed between the Sentinel and the Threnodian, the second Dark Tide, and the forming of this Sonoro Sphere...
Right now, you're the sole survivor of whatever happened that day. You really don't remember anything?
As you spoke, I remembered a few more things. There are two other swords.
The Sword of Discord—Hognis, and the Sword of Virtue—Haultir.
Yes, did you see them too?
Placing the three swords on their respective pedestals should break the seal over the main tower...
But why would this information be revealed to me now...? Is this the Threnodian's doing?
If we do nothing, we'll never get any answers.
Instead of speculating, we should use the clues we've gathered so far.
Lady Maiden...
Please. Cartethyia would suffice. I am but a fake after all.
I've waited for this moment, this chance to save the Sentinel... and my family.
I will not turn back, even if this does turn out to be a trap.
If the thought of the final answer troubles you, then I suggest you step aside. {PlayerName} and I will take care of this matter.
Since you are willing to overlook the possibilities of a trap, then there's no reason for me to worry and turn away.
I underestimated your resolve. I'm sorry.
Simply place Tyrvine on the pedestal behind me and this tower will elevate itself.

I believe it's to prevent them from falling to the ground.

I imagine it's also a symbolic reminder that our beliefs have been turned on their head.
This view matches with what I saw at the time.
Until you get used to the gravity here, I suggest we travel via "Phaom."
It's the name I gave to a Gondola.

I should ask you that! What did you do just now, huh?
I was dozing when bam! Outta nowhere a giant blue ball landed on top of me.
It almost squished me!
I'm guessing putting Tyrvine on the pedestal has something to do with it.
Oh, hey! It smells just as "unnatural" as that big gigantor back in Jinzhou.
The Sentinel of Jinzhou... If what our little Echo friend says is true, then the frequency that entered your Tacet Mark could be Imperator's powers.
Huh? But the Sentinel isn't even here.
The power to split and manipulate space...
It is reminiscent of the moment of Tyrvine's creation. Only this time the place of confinement has become your Tacet Mark.
But why would it do that?
I believe it was meant for the "true" Maiden.
Under the right circumstances, the one to wield this sword and enter the Sonoro Sphere would be the Sentinel's Resonator, the Blessed Maiden.
The Sentinel entrusted Their power to the Resonator so that she could lend assistance when the corruption of the Threnodian altered Them. Quite logical, isn't it?
You don't seem too thrilled about it.
If Imperator set this in motion, then Their original plan has already failed.
Cartethyia, that means your guidance holds the key now.
But...
I believe in you.
Is there anything else you remember?
I... just remembered the day I was crowned by the Order, and the moment the Dark Tide descended upon us...
Hmm?
But I didn't see the Dark Tide.
That is all I can remember...
Is that what you saw?
You witnessed it as well, Cantarella?
No. I only saw fragmented, blurry images...
They seemed to belong to other places within the Sonoro Sphere.
I believe this is where we should rest. We'll wait until sunrise.
You're the one who needs rest most of all.

Gehinnom, the one you mentioned earlier, what happened to him?
I understand...
Thank you...
Anna... Casidomo... Olmnat... everyone...
I am finally... finally able to face all of you...
I am not your enemy, and your sacrifices were not in vain...
Hey {PlayerName}, just now there was...
Shh... later.
Someone needs a quiet moment.
Sorry you had to see me lose my composure.
I've found my true self again. It does not matter if I am indeed the Threnodian's Resonator.
Because I know who to stand by and who to cut down.
Some of my memories have returned, thanks to you and Cantarella.
Feeling better?
No, not yet. Not until we free the Sentinel and defeat the Threnodian.
That is why we need to investigate the frequency you absorbed earlier.
Aha, my turn to shine!
That blue thingy in your Tacet Mark totally tastes like Threnodian!
Of course not, it reeks! Just the smell alone is enough.
The Threnodian's energy has also been split... Could it be the work of the Sentinel?
Like I said, it's mixed up with something. Too tough to chew.
If the Sentinel splits Their own energy to prepare the "true" Blessed Maiden...
Then why would They split off the Threnodian's energy, and then channel it through Hognis to the person who unsealed the passage?
Possibly, but the Threnodian's energy would damage the body of the Sentinel's Resonator.
You wouldn't be affected since Abby resides within you.
But surely a second frequency would interfere with the resonance of the Sentinel's "true" Blessed Maiden.
The answer might lie in the other frequencies that got mixed in.
But the frequency of the Sentinel's "true" Blessed Maiden is supposed to clash with that of the Threnodian's.
A fusion of the two would endanger her life.
The answer might lie in the other frequencies that got mixed in.
Huh?
You are a Resonator born of the merge between the Sentinel and Threnodian. What if you used their abilities to split it yourself?
I haven't forgotten how I became a Resonator, and I know I don't have the ability to do that.
Do you think the mixed frequencies Abby felt... came from me?
But why would I do that?
The answer might lie behind the third sealed passageway.

Same as before? We'll keep watch tonight and continue our journey tomorrow.

I understand...

Meaning...
They might still be able to hear and feel.

After all, these frequencies are strong enough to manifest in the real world.
Really?

The real Blessed Maiden is dead.

Soon, thou shalt recall all.

Merge with Leviathan, a measure of last resort. At the time, I had no other recourse.

The Threnodian is a taint upon civilization. Only by partaking of Its blight could I seek to comprehend It.

But we may yet shackle It.

I offered knowledge of the "Resonator," yet concealed one small truth.

After centuries of failure, by sheer trial it found success but once.

What made you decide to leave Tyrvine with the Fisalias?

After Fleurdelys's conception, Cantarella became my safeguard.

I trust this will serve to pave the way for you.

But that wasn't your original plan.
No... it was an unexpected variable.

Perhaps this is the influence humanity has wrought upon me... To change is to be free.

Cartethyia. Awaken.

I am Imperator, a being that owes you a great debt. I... have a question I wish to ask thee.
Dost thou rage at how life has unfolded? Dost thou renounce faith or hold resentment?
If thou wishes to forget, I can erase the past from thy memory.

Without the truth, I would not have had to strength to carry on.
The truth is a beacon in the maelstrom of my life.

dialogs.content: Let me take a good look at you, the sword-wielding hatless one, and the promising Niccolo. Hmm, you've grown out of that naive boy and into a reliable adult.
Ahem, I was young and full of myself back then, coming up with all kinds of silly names... Please don't make fun of me for it, Professor Novelli.
Those who look out to sea often dream of setting sail, but after seeing it all, they long to ride the waves back home, where life truly takes root.
Please accept this, Professor Novelli. I bought it just for you.
What a beautiful bundle of Sword Acorus... I didn't think you'd remember.
Of course, you once told me it was your favorite flower.
You used these flowers with their strong, straight stems to teach me how to fight opponents with a sword, long before I put my hands on a real one.
Yes. Traditionally, we used them in swordsmanship lessons for young nobles. But there was one child whom I recall was the exception.
You mean that Montelli girl who bested me? I heard she has become an important figure in her family now.
Losing to someone so much younger really got to me. Then I noticed the calluses on her hands... Unlike other nobles her age, she'd been training with a heavy, sharp metal sword from the start.
To her, fighting wasn't some noble virtue—it was a matter of life and death.
Perhaps that's the price of becoming a true Montelli.
A hefty price, indeed... Now, those calluses mark my own hands, and I finally understand the look she gave me when she saw me with that Sword Acorus.

You've come, warrior!
The mighty guardian, our Iudicis Arsinosa, is not the kind of Echo to warm to crowds.
The Lioness favors the strong, the unyielding, and the battle-hardened. Only those she deems worthy will find her arms welcoming.
But... she is still an Echo and can't talk.
(These sounds...)
What is it? Did you feel something just now?
I only heard strange sounds. Tell me, what direction did the Lioness just look toward?
The Vale of Glory.
It's where all heroes, blessed by the glory forged in iron and fire, find their rest.
But on the long path of hunting, many died with their bodies missing. Only their weapons returned.
Arsinosa's frequency is woven from the cries of souls in battle. The battered weapons still carry the will of their former masters, whispering the deeds left undone.
To touch such weapons is a rite of great importance for those who claim glory in the Great Agon and receive the Lioness's blessing.
Hearing the voices of our ancestors by Arsinosa's side is a great source of strength for Septimontians.
(Before meeting Buling, when I touched the Echo in that village, I felt... a layered, indistinct frequency.)
(It was like what Abby described on our journey to Septimont, but the source eluded me at the time.)
(But now... I've found it.)
(The source of that power lies in the Vale of Glory. The closer the Lioness gets to it, the clearer it becomes.)
She waits for us there. Shall we go together?
I'm not sure if Septimontian rituals will interest you, but you might uncover something useful, no?
Perfect! Let's head out.
Ugh...
What is it?
Nothing... just...

Anyway, it's no matter. Let's continue.

(If something cut her off, aside from the Fractsidus, it could've only been the Threnodian, which should be dead.)
(But Septimont holds no faith in the Sentinel, and the Threnodian was never able to establish influence here. Hmm... maybe it's not that simple.)
(The Threnodian controls the minds of Its followers through their faith. Mya is a Ragunnesi, and likely a follower of The Order of the Deep.)
(If the Vale of Glory is an important rite for champions, perhaps Mya went there... and it was there she vanished.)
(Her hysterics, hallucinations, and loss of control in the arena were signs of the Threnodian's corruption.)
(Phrolova once said, "The closer one stands to the <color=RedD>protagonist</color>, the greater their influence over the tale."
(In this Great Agon, Lupa is the <color=RedD>protagonist</color>. Years ago, it was Mya. Now, I'm seeing Mya's image flicker in and out throughout this journey.)
(If the Mya I see is under the Threnodian's control, does that mean securing the <color=RedD>protagonist</color> role is key to Its plan?)
(When I first met Lupa, I sensed what felt like Cartethyia's frequency on her. Later, I also felt the Threnodian's presence.)
(Did they cross paths? If Cartethyia is part of this story, the likelihood is high.)
(Could Lupa have forgotten? Did they meet without realizing it? Or is she lying and already under the Threnodian's influence?)
(Was Phrolova telling the truth by saying Lupa would bring forth the Dark Tide... or is she just another one of its victims?)

I don't know if it's the Threnodian's work, but... if something is wrong, and it's trying to twist my mind...

You'd protect my honor and my dignity.
There's more at stake than that, Lupa.
I've heard the Septimont saying, "All for glory, fear no death." But sometimes, living takes more courage than dying.

content.content: Who did this blade belong to?

dialogs.content: This is Tercules's sword. You remember the waters of the upper city, right? You were looking for Cartethyia. Tercules was the one that the statue was based on.
Ages ago, the Dark Tide bore down on Ragunnesi, and Septimont didn't escape.
Tercules was the son of the Ephor back then, and he led our warriors to face the Tacet Discords. He died in that cursed Tide, his strength worn down to nothing.
His sword was corrupted, but his followers still risked their lives to bring it back.
In this land, intense emotions easily blend with other forces. The Lioness of Glory was born from the fiery passions of heroes, so she holds sway over their weapons.
Back then, this sword was growing more sinister due to the corruption...
But all these years later, it has become a memento of a hero.
(I feel something strong and pulsing in the direction the blade is pointing.)
(It's coming from underground. Is it inside the mountain itself?)
...The frequency... it's the Sentinel Imperator...
Just like Ragunna, Septimont has its own Genesis Nexus... That's why It seeks...
...Power... needs more...

dialogs.content:
Subject: Welcome aboard the Echo Train of Averardo Vault!
 
To facilitate your business within the Averardo Vault, we are pleased to offer the Echo Train service. These unique Echoes will swiftly transport you to various areas within the Vault.
 
For your safety, please adhere to the following guidelines:
 
1. The Echo Train is gentle in nature, but please refrain from feeding or attacking it. Doing so may cause it to veer off course or even fall off the tracks if startled.
 
2. During the journey, you may enjoy the view through the train's window. Please do not extend any part of your body out the window. If you find that this rule has already been violated, promptly refer to Rule 6.
 
3. Averardo Vault only contains depositories, storage facilities, and small decorative sculptures. There are no statues or structures with a height of around ▇▇▇, resembling a ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇. If you encounter such a structure during your ride, remind yourself that it is merely an illusion caused by the Vault's enclosed environment and promptly avert your gaze. If you continue to perceive the structure, promptly refer to Rule 6.
 
4. You may call the Echo Train via your Terminal, and it will typically arrive within three minutes. If the train fails to arrive within this time frame, leave the station immediately and report the delay to the Vault staff at the front desk. Do not board any train arriving after the three-minute window.
 
5. The Echo Train within the vault is designed to resemble a fish. It has no limbs, legs, or tentacles. If you notice that the train's appearance deviates from this, do not board it. Instead, call for another Echo Train and wait until the abnormal train has left the platform.
 
6. If you violate any of the above rules, promptly leave the platform and inform the nearest Vault staff. If you have already boarded the train, immediately throw this flyer out the window. The train will proceed to the nearest station, where Vault staff will be waiting to escort you out. Please refrain from engaging in conversation or making eye contact with the staff.

For your safety, please adhere to the following guidelines:
 
1. The Echo Train is gentle in nature, but please refrain from feeding or attacking it. Doing so may cause it to veer off course or even fall off the tracks if startled.
 
2. During the journey, you may enjoy the view through the train's window. Please do not extend any part of your body out the window. If you find that this rule has already been violated, promptly refer to Rule 6.
 
3. Averardo Vault only contains depositories, storage facilities, and small decorative sculptures. There are no statues or structures with a height of around ▇▇▇, resembling a ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇. If you encounter such a structure during your ride, remind yourself that it is merely an illusion caused by the Vault's enclosed environment and promptly avert your gaze. If you continue to perceive the structure, promptly refer to Rule 6.
 
4. You may call the Echo Train via your Terminal, and it will typically arrive within three minutes. If the train fails to arrive within this time frame, leave the station immediately and report the delay to the Vault staff at the front desk. Do not board any train arriving after the three-minute window.
 
5. The Echo Train within the vault is designed to resemble a fish. It has no limbs, legs, or tentacles. If you notice that the train's appearance deviates from this, do not board it. Instead, call for another Echo Train and wait until the abnormal train has left the platform.
 
6. If you violate any of the above rules, promptly leave the platform and inform the nearest Vault staff. If you have already boarded the train, immediately throw this flyer out the window. The train will proceed to the nearest station, where Vault staff will be waiting to escort you out. Please refrain from engaging in conversation or making eye contact with the staff.

(A stack of papers rests here. They appear to be part of an unfinished novel or essay.)
 
...Ziegler was stranded on his private island, with only a coconut tree for company and the occasional Bell Crab scuttling across the beach.
 
Who was he? Ziegler Senior's son? Ragunna's most successful investor? The poor soul who lost everything in a gamble, with all his wealth and titles now gone? A mad artist? A hermit? The unfortunate fool who got caught in a shipwreck?
 
He gazed at the sea, the soft breeze lifting his graying hair while stirring the waves. In the golden glint of sunlight, he seemed to see countless versions of himself scattered through time, broken and incomplete. He felt a loneliness like never before, yet a strange sense of satisfaction.
 
He had no chance of leaving this island. Maybe tomorrow, or the day after, he would breathe his last breath under the scorching sun.
 
He had exhausted all of his miracles. The thought crossed his mind but quickly vanished without a trace. He decided to take some time to observe his island—to engrave all of its details deep into his mind, to fill his fragmented memories with them, and to hope that the coming darkness would not turn them to nothingness.
 
(The writing ends here.)

I've conducted over a hundred visits and interviews, traveling between Thessaleo Fells and Egla Town. Finally, I think I have a theory...
It seems that these regions are experiencing a phenomenon—mass hypochondria, if you will.
For example, many people claim to have seen an ancient knight they believe is still alive.
Others speak of an angel named Annis, said to answer the call of those with unbreakable wills. Annis appears in different forms, helping those in dire need.
From the records, she's often seen as a young girl, a flower, a bird… even a jellyfish.
Yet, after combing through records over the past few centuries, I have yet to find any concrete evidence for Annis's existence.
Medically speaking, it seems more likely that these are hallucinations brought on by intense mental strain.
When someone is under severe stress or endures deep trauma, the mind might create an external figure to ease the pain, like a survival mechanism.
Think of the pressures of strained family ties, the toll of years of competition, and hallucinations induced by toxins...
In extreme cases, one's own identity can fragment, conjuring up an imaginary figure.
So, when an entire community is facing intense pressure...
Hmm, but I'd say that angel or not, true salvation lies within ourselves. Don't you agree?

Is there anything else you want to know? I'll hold nothing back.
My "death"... Well, I'll start from the very beginning: My journey to win the championship.
I had failed to expose the family's match-fixing. After being deceived by Domina Julia and winning the title on my own, my memories became a blur... I was probably under some form of control.
The last thing I clearly remembered was standing in the Central Hub in the Vale of Glory, pressing my spear into something that resembled a control panel. Then the Dark Tide began to surge.

dialogs.content: What brings you here, Cantarella?

So you're saying... you're here to gather energy Imperator split from your Second Awakening?
Speaking of this, if you manage to recover that energy, does that mean you can become the Blessed Maiden again?
Theoretically, yes. However, that is not the purpose of my visit.
Energy from my Second Awakening is but one of many mixed in the fragments. There are also frequencies that belong to the daughters of the Fisalia family.
This energy is not mine alone.
Not to mention, I've already made my choice of rejecting fate's coronation.
We deserve the freedom to shape our own destinies. The Fisalia children are no exception.

Ah, how careless of me... I forget I'm speaking to someone who chose to wipe their own past...

dialogs.content: The melody has returned to its proper rhythm. This place is beginning to restore itself.
Soon, it will recover too.
I knew we'd make beautiful music together! Another perfect rehearsal!
Hold on, you played ahead of the beat. I heard it!
Ahem... Well, Phrolova, your playing and Triss's improvisation were completely in sync! No wonder you're our best violinist!
It's only because... I've played this piece countless times before.
Oi! Don't be changin' the subject now!
I've heard tell you've been asked to perform far from here? I'm sure you'll amaze them all, just like you always do.
That performance...
Are you alright, Phrolova? You look a bit pale...
Plans have changed, but it's nothing to worry about.
I see... When you can, come back and rest, will you? You've been workin' so hard!
I remember you said this is the only place you could truly rest. But you're always busy, and sometimes things here get a bit... messy.
I'm here with you.
Triss, do you want me to keep going with my plan?
Of course! I wanna sing and sing forever!
Even though this isn't the home we once knew?
I know it's not. I'm not the same as I was either. I died in an accident, hundreds of years ago.
But I still feel me inside, and I can still laugh and sing. It doesn't feel any different.
I know you can do it, Phrolova. You'll bring everyone back, and I'll be right here waitin' for ye. I'll wait for that day.
By then...
By then, you will stand on an even brighter stage.
(I'll be here. "Always.")

We should move.

Right! So, Peaks of Prestige is a game inspired by Echo Gladiating.
Unlike traditional gladiating, you don't fight yourself but command an Echo Squad using Action Cards through your Terminal.
No blood, no guts, just pure strategy and creativity. Every round's packed with surprises and possibility!
Bet you're a traveler, right? All you have to do is download the game on your Terminal, and you'll be ready to dive right in!
We might not have a huge player base yet, but trust me! You won't regret trying it.
Of course! In Peaks of Prestige, you earn Prestige Points by battling others. You can use them to unlock stronger Echoes and power up your team.
Oh, just a heads-up: all Echoes you use in-game are separate from the ones you actually own.
So even if you've got, say, two thousand Echoes stored in your Terminal... they won't help you here!
Haha, not that anyone has that many Echoes, right?
Ads? You mean those suspicious leaflets saying "Come play Peaks of Prestige"?
Nope, not me. No idea who made them either. We players believe that some hardcore fans just got too desperate to get new players, so they... went a bit too far.

He believes that the closer one stands to the protagonist, the greater their influence over the tale.
