dialogs.content: Look at you... you can't go on much longer.
I feared as much. Then this is where we... stop.
Strange. I remember everything about Septimont, but... I can't remember... I can't even remember my name.
You didn't forget.
Someone stole your <color=RedD>role</color> in the story. Even your name on the placards in the arena would be unreadable.
Your existence has been erased. Only by unmaking this story can it be reclaimed.
Too bad I won't last long enough to see that happen.
I'm sorry, Cartethyia. You saved me, but I can't help you in return.
When I was a child... long ago, I heard tales of Septimont.
A city full of passion and life. People there drank deeply, laughed loudly, appreciated sculpture, and lived for the hunt.
Men and women feared nothing. They burned like fire, giving all their light and heat before fading.
But when I arrived in Septimont, it had already been undone by dark hands. With the Dark Tide sweeping the streets, the city was nothing but an empty shell.
That's right... my city is beautiful.
When the autumn wind blew through the golden flags and wind chimes, time seemed to slow...
The Leviathan... I will not give It the chance to make the people of Rinascita weep and bleed.
I will drag whoever orchestrated this tragedy out of the shadows.
Septimont... can I leave it to you?
No.
You said it yourself. This is your city. Some things, only you can do.
The monster leaving its trace in the Dark Tide... I can feel it. Its frequency is similar to my own.
The Threnodian created me to be a Resonator for Its power. But I wasn't the only one. Many "vessels" before me failed.
You mean...
There is still much I don't know. I'll keep searching. But no matter what, you have a certain "specialness."
Once... I sought to end it all. Someone stopped me.
Even a life mocked by fate can break its curse. Whatever you seek to do, whether you're weak or strong, you must strive for it.
I returned to the world thanks to a certain person's help.
I believe {Male=he;Female=she} will come here and reshape this twisted story.
Must be quite the person, eh? I wish I could meet {Male=him;Female=her}... and see how {Male=he;Female=she} does it...
Then you will see for yourself.
Victory isn't won in an instant. It takes patience and perseverance. What we can't do now, someone will carry forward later.
If you want to save your city, then hold on. No matter the pain, no matter the doubts, you must keep going.
Just like how you wandered Septimont before I came, broken yet determined to leave to find help for the city.
Jump to a new story, and bring my message to that person.
Alright, Cartethyia... I'll... I'll try my best...
First... tell me, what is that person's name?
I'm close to that abnormal frequency...
...You're in the submerged aqueducts.

content.content: What were you eating just now?

dialogs.content: Ah... it's all gone now. But I'll ask the tavern keeper if he can prepare something for you later.
The Laurus Salad was as delightful as ever. Well worth reacquainting myself with so I can make a bowl myself.
Fresh, crisp, sweet... Heh.
Come, sit with me, {PlayerName}. Let's enjoy a moment of peace.
Yes, and so... I've been thinking about what I vowed to you before.
To savor the things I desire, visit the places I long for, and meet those I wish to see.
To become a roving knight is my true ambition. A wish list is something to be experienced one step at a time.
I'd say your first wish has already been fulfilled.
The third, too... though by unexpected means.
Those are my adoptive parents... and their child.
Perhaps it was fate's cruel jest. I couldn't find any trace of them after they moved from Ragunna, but here in Septimont, I discovered where they had resettled.
Only... they no longer recognize me.
The truth that I was their daughter was a memory the Threnodian crafted for them, disappearing when It was sealed away in the tower.
I don't know what they went through after that fateful day, but at least... they are still alive. They even have their own child.
They walk here every day, so I come and sit for a while to watch them from a distance.
Cartethyia...
It's alright, {PlayerName}. In fact, I'm at peace with it now.
If they had died because of the Order's heavy hand, I would've felt true pain. But this... this is the best outcome I could hope for.
To live twenty years with the weight of a lost child... I don't want to imagine that kind of torment.
Besides, through all these twists of fate, all three of my wishes have been fulfilled.
Now if I crave a Laurus Salad, I can prepare it myself and savor its taste.
And I still have many years ahead to see the world and the places I long to visit.
As for the people I hope to meet... this unexpected journey led me to find them in another city.
The winds of Rinascita always seem to bring me what I seek. I am content.

dialogs.content: Looks like the oration they mentioned.
Huh… I thought for sure it'd be Iuno at an event like this.
Eh, well. Guess I'll catch her later.
...Yes, I fear that until Grandmother Lillibet finds a gifted successor, we shall not glimpse further into <ano= Septimont's Auguries>Septimont's future</ano>.
By the light and fate above us, we are but apprentices carving insights into stone, passing their words along.
Once, fate flowed like a thread. It guided reverent seekers to glimpse Septimont's end...
Under the Tide's surge, all was overturned. No soul was spared.
Until the Unwritten One arrived from afar to join forces with Augusta.
With the Corrosaurus as bait, {Male=he;Female=she} cut through the Dark Tide's miasma to reveal the truth.
With the False Sovereign's blood, a new ruler was crowned. The prophesied end was averted, thanks to Augusta and the Unwritten One.

From now on, fear no longer grips me. The Dark Tide retreats into the forgotten night, and countless souls drink from pure waters again. The new Hero of Heroes, Augusta, shall lead Septimont into a new age.
Thus, the present now aligns with the prophecy Grandmother Lillibet once foresaw in Septimont's Auguries.
Prophecy of the end, and how we managed to lure the Sovereign out... The order and the story are right, but something's missing.
You speak of me and Augusta, but what of Iuno?
Who is... Iuno?
Unwritten One, you leave me baffled.
Are you suggesting that my recounting missed... someone named Iuno? I don't find the name... familiar.
Hmm. I should know this... Iuno, you speak of, yes?
Iuno is a Priestess, just like you.
More than that, she wielded the Moon Bow and fought alongside me and Augusta in the hunt. We defeated the Sovereign together... Don't you all remember?

I speak of fate, of course.
These figurines I brought were crafted by my family for me and my brother, as a rite of passage. They're made in our likeness.

dialogs.content: I can see further than anyone else. I can see things no one else can...
I've seen things others can't begin to imagine.
So why... why, at the moment I should've seen the clearest, did I close my eyes and shut it out?
I was so close... If I hadn't... closed my eyes...
I would've learned the causal chain, and I could've stopped it.
After that, I decided to keep my eyes wide open, no matter the cost.
I'll sit at the crossroads of fate. I'll stare into what's to come and not flinch, be it joyful, tragic, rebirth, destruction...
Until I see it all. Until I know everything.
Because I'm stronger than anyone else. This is something only I can do. But—
"If the Priestess's prophecies were really perfect, we could avoid all misfortune..."
"If there is such a thing as fate, then misfortunes cannot be avoided..."
"Just because you know the outcome, doesn't mean the journey isn't worth it!"
"If life is destined to follow a predetermined path, does it even matter if we know our fate?"
After all I see... could I ever answer what they hope of me?
Does glimpsing one's fate really matter?

content.content: I understand why you stopped offering prophecies.
You weren't sure if seeing the future alone was really enough.

dialogs.content: Unwritten... You are as sharp as ever.

dialogs.content: Still giving prophecies, Iuno?
Like the first time we met on the plains, you told me you saw a glory as bright as the sun. One that would earn me respect.
Truth be told, I didn't think much of your words back then.
When I want something, no one's permission is needed. Nothing could stand between me and my goal.
When the prophecy came true though, I found it... unsatisfying.
Imagine thinking you are the master of your own fate, only to learn, for better or for worse, everything you are is part of fate's design.
It's as if fate chips away at the untamed part of you, turning you from a wolf into a caged rabbit.
And you... you saw it all so easily. Truths as clear as the moonlight. Bright, yet distant and cold.
Don't mistake me. I don't dismiss the value of prophecy.
No, quite the opposite. I do recognize the Priestesses' abilities.
Seeing the outcome gives us insight. Prophecies allow us to envision the future and find better ways to face it.
In every one of Septimont's Auguries, the Priestesses foresaw disasters that would befall the land, but also the hero who would rise up to face it.
Like the people of Septimont, I too have been blessed by prophecy. But in the end, whether disaster is averted or who the hero is... those choices are never ours.
If we are nothing more than fate's puppets, what difference does it make if we can see its hand?
If fate one day wills our annihilation, with no way to change it, what then is the role of a Priestess?
Are they merely fate's mouthpiece, bowing to its will? Or... are they pioneers, seeking to shape what's to come?
Last night, Grandmother Lillibet told me another Septimont Augury had emerged. This one revealed a future unseen, a warning long overdue...
An unknown disaster that would bring about the end of Septimont.
The vision was unclear. The Priestess couldn't discern the cause of the disaster, nor could they see the hero who would rise up to stop it.
The Senate prefers to wait, believing the solution will reveal itself in time. But I must consider the darker possibility.

I know that you'd rather be out there dealing with living, breathing people than confined to the Temple to await some grand future. You, too, are tired of the Senate's rules and the Priestesses' chains.
But as a prodigy in prophecy, you should see further than Lillibet or any of the other Priestesses.
Would you dare, with no direction, no clues, and not a single focus item, gaze upon Septimont's end and trace its cause?

Last night, Grandmother Lillibet told me another Septimont Augury had emerged. This one revealed a future unseen, a warning long overdue...
An unknown disaster that would bring about the end of Septimont.
The vision was unclear. The Priestess couldn't discern the cause of the disaster, nor could they see the hero who would rise up to stop it.
The Senate prefers to wait, believing the solution will reveal itself in time. But I must consider the darker possibility.

I know that you'd rather be out there dealing with living, breathing people than confined to the Temple to await some grand future. You, too, are tired of the Senate's rules and the Priestesses' chains.
But as a prodigy in prophecy, you should see further than Lillibet or any of the other Priestesses.
Would you dare, with no direction, no clues, and not a single focus item, gaze upon Septimont's end and trace its cause?

dialogs.content: The Lunarum Boughs have grown strong. You've done well with your Anchoring.
Look at you, a mortal from the real world stumbling into Chaos. What else would you be here for, if not to take something back with you？
Also, with that thing on your wrist there... Isn't it clear? That's how she's been connected to you all this time. Only Anchoring explains that.
As for your second question, that's even stranger.
Along the way, you met the Priestesses, Gladiators, and many others chasing prophecies... Did you ever stop to wonder who they were?
What is it you expect to hear then, mmm?
I'm a blacksmith, long dead. Once a forger of weapons.
A father to a daughter.
A reflection of her past in the Chaos.
Aye. But just like the question of who I am, that's not the point.
What matters isn't me, but you. Isn't that right?
You noticed, didn't you? The more you rested near the Lunarum Boughs, the more memories and connections manifested into reality. Iuno's specter became more real, and the Boughs grew.
But now, Chaos has that specter. After all, it was never truly Iuno, was it? But the Lunarum Bough, that's what the two of you built along the way.
There'll be no more doors to choose from. You can keep the Bough and take it back with you. Find a new specter to follow. As long as you have it with you, that should be enough.
Or... do you still want to forge it into a bow?
We were gathering Lunarum Boughs to forge the bow.
Just like... I came here only to Anchor her and bring her back.
If you cut it here, all your previous Anchoring will be for nothing. You might have to start over many times, with things going even less smoothly. Are you willing?
Not to mention, being trapped in Chaos for so long... There's a chance she's already forgotten her will to fight.
Are you sure you want to throw away all the certainty you've built, just to gamble on a possibility?
Forgotten... to fight? I don't know who you think she is, but the Iuno I know is not someone to give in so easily.
She promised we'd meet at the end. As long as Iuno needs a bow, I'll be the one to carry it for her.
Ha, I always thought you followed the light's guidance. Now I see, you reached this point because the light followed you.
How could I forget? The greatest archery isn't about hitting the target every time. It's about letting the arrow choose the mark. Wherever it lands, that's where destiny awaits.
I've said it before. I forge weapons. If you still want it, I'll forge the bow for you.
Come then. Let's do it.

dialogs.content: Impressive!
I expected a challenge, but your performance far exceeds what I had imagined.
Just as I thought, watching from the Colosseum's balcony is no way to understand a warrior's true spirit.
Only by crossing blades can I feel the will to fight pulsing through your veins.
Come. Step closer.
Laureate of Ragunna. Champion of Septimont. Favored Gladiator of <ano=Lioness of Glory>Arsinosa</ano>—by the honor of these titles, it is only right you stand by my side.
I, Augusta, Ephor of Septimont, offer you my highest esteem.
Hehe. Simple and efficient, no need for pleasantries. Here, we let our blades do the talking. The Septimont way.
I have no doubt that you and I will have plenty of opportunities to get acquainted. But that's not why I called you here today...
On my behalf, and that of the Ephor's Palace, I extend my deepest apologies for failing to keep our appointment.
I hope this delay hasn't dampened your enthusiasm for the hunt.
Haha. Tolerant and strong. Just as I've heard. Virtues of a true hero.
Well, then. Seeing that your interest still holds. Shall we discuss it?
The hunt—in Septimont's long fight for survival, it holds profound significance...
It is both honor and duty. For a hundred years, countless Gladiators have taken up the hunt and met their end in glory.
It's no exaggeration to say that the blood of Gladiators still burns in every inch of the crimson Sanguis Plateaus.
Our ancestors built the defenses that line those grounds. To this day, they stand as the frontline of Septimont's resistance against the Dark Tide.
You've surely noticed the lingering Blightcloud that hovers over the Sanguis Plateaus. Since the first Dark Tide outbreak in Rinascita, that place has become a breeding ground for its horrors.
As you've no doubt realized, our prey are Tacet Discords born from the Dark Tide. Only those who desecrate Septimont fall beneath the Gladiators' blades.
The High Tide is upon us... and it will be a storm like no other.
My hunting party requires unstoppable warriors. Sacrifices are inevitable, but I believe you will be a banner that stands unbroken, {PlayerName}.

content.content: There are plenty of great Gladiators in Septimont...
What made you want to invite me on this hunt?

dialogs.content: I share your sentiment. Septimont takes pride in its many remarkable Gladiators. But you, you are exceptional.
A grand hunt awaits us, and my warriors and I long to do battle alongside a fighter such as yourself.
Of course, the will of the extraordinary deserves to be heard.
I'd like to know your thoughts on the matter, {PlayerName}.
A straightforward answer. I like it.
As for this "goal" of yours...
Ah, yes, the Journeying Paradise. I've heard that laughable name before. A pity the hunt was made to shatter that little fantasy.
As for the Sentinel's Relic...
Go to the Earthrend Wedge. It's where the Sentinel Imperator first descended upon the Sanguis Plateaus and is the "epicenter" of every hunt to this day.
However, due to its significance, not even Septimont's highest officials are permitted near it.
But if that is what you wish... say no more. I will make it happen.
The trust I place in you stems from your recognition of my character. I admire your honesty, and I will honor it to the fullest.
Only those bound by trust can go the distance together.
I look forward to the hunt ahead. It honors me to journey by your side.
Patience, my friend, is the first step to becoming a hunter.
When the storm rages in the skies southeast of Septimont, I will await you at Tempest Cliffs.

dialogs.content: The Hunter's Den. The busiest Gladiator encampment across the Sanguis Plateaus. Nearly every hunter passes through here on their way to the hunting grounds.
We will rest here before setting off for the next hunt.
I must admit, this place is rather magnificent.
I suppose my predecessors forsook the peace they ought to have enjoyed, just to share this hard-earned land with these hunters. Such magnificence is rightly owed to the Temple.
Heh, the Priestess's words are not without merit. I am well aware that I stand under blessings, and will forever remember the sacrifices of the Temple.
Now if you'll excuse me. I'll be taking my leave.
Tch...
Though we've already met, I suppose a proper introduction is in order.
I am Iuno. Priestess of the Tetragon Temple.
Well, aren't you caught up on things? What you say is true, though I've long since grown tired of such affairs.
Come now, {PlayerName}. Surely you can find me something more interesting to occupy my time. For instance... the hunt?
Quite frankly, when it comes to dealing with the Dark Tide, none of these Gladiators can hold a candle to me.
Ha. Look at those looks. I've seen them all before.
What can I say? When you're as dazzling as I am, jealousy tends to follow.
I'll be making my way back, Augusta. Lest my shine further sting the eyes of certain people.
If you find yourself with free time later, consider visiting me at Tetragon Temple.
Not every outlander is granted access to its sacred halls. Make the most of it.
It's rare to see Iuno hold back like that. You must be someone... different to her.
Perhaps... We do share some common traits.
Hehe. Don't let her unruly side fool you. She is as dependable as they come.
A Corrosaurus.
Avidius was correct. It is a Tacet Discord born from the Dark Tide.
What he didn't have the chance to tell you is that it is the deadliest Corrosaurus of them all—we call it "Tyrannos." A vanguard of the Dark Tide that rides its surge to reach our lands.
The Threnodian's attempt to plague Septimont never came to fruition. But do not mistake that for victory. Our enemy will not bow so easily.
The Dark Tide, immortal and indestructible, carries out the will of its creator—the Threnodian Leviathan.
Only the Earthrend Wedge that bears Sentinel Imperator's power can sever the link between the Dark Tide and the Threnodian, burying the calamity deep beneath the Sanguis Plateaus.
The "hunt" is how we disrupt the Dark Tide's frequencies by capturing and eliminating its creatures.
However, the Earthrend Wedge's energy range is limited. Our mission is to deliver a true death to our prey.
Meaning we need to hunt and kill the beast near the Earthrender... Is that how we stop the Dark Tide from spreading?
Yes. And it must be done within Maroonwood.
This confrontation with Tyrannos was expected, but it's not a fight anyone is eager to face...
That beast is well aware of our plan. It's no mere prey. In many ways, it's a cunning hunter itself.
Now we wait. We wait for it to enter Maroonwood.
The real hunt begins when the beast's hunger drives it to the wilds.
Your Excellency, the Senators request your presence in the main tent.
It's to discuss plans for the hunting operation...
Looks like I'll be occupied for a while.
Relax. Take a walk around camp. The Hornett's blare will sound our next departure.
It's a sound that can be heard across the canyons. You won't miss it.

"Fabius, the one who walked with Sentinel Imperator. Prophesied Hero of Heroes."
"The untamable blackened tide surged, its sinewy arms outstretched. With hands steadfast as stone, Fabius led through the storm, ascending to the eternal highlands."
"The victor's flag flutters in wild winds: From this day forth, the lands beneath my feet shall belong to Septimont."
"'The Monument' Atilius. Prophesied Hero of Heroes."
"An unyielding spirit. A valiant conqueror."
"When the black waters fell from the heavens, he was the ironclad dam that stood between Septimont and the calamity."
"'The Untarnished Blade' Valeria. Prophesied Hero of Heroes."
"She, sole monarch of the land of pursuit and huntsmanship."

The murals do not fade. In the silence of time, they remain, waiting for your gaze.

dialogs.content: Good day to you, {Male=Sir;Female=Madam} {PlayerName}. It seems you too have taken an interest in the Temple's murals.
They are the works of past Priestesses. They depict prophecies glimpsed in the Sacred Flames—ones already fulfilled and ones yet to come.
In any case, all these murals point to two prophecies of importance.
The first is a Ragunnesi prophecy condemning Septimont's lack of faith in the Sentinel—
"Hear this, O faithless ones of Septimont. The Divinity of the high heavens has grown enraged. Should your monarch once more stand in contempt of Their will, annihilation shall be your fate."
The second is a continuation of the Ragunnesi prophecy, delivered by Septimont's Priestesses—

"Only the Hero of Heroes of extraordinary power, risen from the dark tides, shall bring eternity to Septimont. Then shall the waters quiet, the tempest still, and glory return with the blood of the old king."
You seem drawn to that particular mural... It tells of a calamity yet to come, and as always, the Hero of Heroes who shall rise among us to turn the tide of fate.
Yet the identity of this Hero remains a mystery. Coincidentally, much like the absent part of this mural, the prophecy of our victory over the coming disaster remains untold...
Whether the Priestesses can't foresee the fate that awaits, or whether the true prophecy is meant to remain hidden... Is indeed a question worth pondering.
Our would-be Hero of Heroes, lost in daydreams again? What is it this time? Staring at an empty wall, hoping one day it'll bear your name?
I happened to wander by, passing the time as one does. No need to trouble yourself with someone as inconsequential as I, Priestess.
Inconsequential? Come now. Everyone knows you're the Senate's golden child. Those old loons wouldn't spare me a glance, but they hang on your every word.
Have you been waiting long? Ugh, I can't believe he got to you first.
Isn't paying respects to the Heroes fairly commonplace? Surely, we needn't allow rivalry to come between us, Priestess.
Hmph. I'm not blind to your tricks, Avidius. Do you really think {PlayerName} would take sides? With you?
Let me guess... Eliminating Tyrannos and the Dark Tide before anyone else would be the perfect act to prove you're the prophesied Hero of Heroes, hmm?
Four expeditions to Manes Deep plus a Holmleaf Medal, and now you think you can usurp Augusta's place? Don't make me laugh.
Oh, read the room, will you?

Why you...
She possesses many qualities worthy of a Hero. But she lacks the "extraordinary power" mentioned in the prophecy.
As a Resonator, Augusta offers nothing special. Yet throughout Septimont's history, every Hero of Heroes was born with extraordinary gifts.
She may have the strength to wield a sword, but I doubt her ability to endure pain and the slow, wearisome passage of time like other Resonators.
It's a pity that in a city built on prophecy, Augusta is a disruptor of the rules.
I assure you, Priestess, I will not act from the shadows. If Augusta seeks a fair challenge, I shall honor her with the respect she deserves.
Priestess, {PlayerName}, I beg your leave.
Perhaps... we will bear witness to the birth of a new Hero in the hunt to come.

I don't understand. Given Augusta's prestige, the Senate has no real advantage in seizing power. What's their angle?

Naturally, it ruffled some feathers. Some even accused her of "undermining the spirit of Gladiating." In reality, they're just upset their piggy banks got smashed.
More importantly...
This is exactly the kind of chaos Augusta wanted. That idiot!
She even went so far as to say, "The citizens of Septimont only need to be loyal to Septimont, not her, Augusta."
And then, like it's nothing, she tells me that the Ephor position only matters when a strong Gladiator wants it.
She's even more stubborn than I am.
Now why would I be worried about that? I'm sure you've seen her sword. The inlaid blades are trophies of every Gladiator she's defeated.
Even ones with decent Resonance powers like Avidius, she eats for breakfast.
Though... Avidius makes me rather uncomfortable. It's got nothing to do with his stance, it's... more of a hunch. Something about him feels... unnatural.
Or maybe I'm just overthinking it.
It's the Griffrex! It appears our prey has finally come out for some fresh air.
We'll meet again later. But next time, I'd like your undivided attention. No distractions, hmm?
Is that lady over there... looking at me?
Better go and greet her.
Good day to you, {Male=Sir;Female=Madam} {PlayerName}. It seems you too have taken an interest in the Temple's murals.

"Hear this, O faithless ones of Septimont. The Divinity of the high heavens has grown enraged. Should your monarch once more stand in contempt of Their will, annihilation shall be your fate."

"Only the Hero of Heroes of extraordinary power, risen from the dark tides, shall bring eternity to Septimont. Then shall the waters quiet, the tempest still, and glory return with the blood of the old king."
You seem drawn to that particular mural... It tells of a calamity yet to come, and as always, the Hero of Heroes who shall rise among us to turn the tide of fate.

Whether the Priestesses can't foresee the fate that awaits, or whether the true prophecy is meant to remain hidden... Is indeed a question worth pondering.

dialogs.content: Over there.

The field blooming with Asphodels is where the hunting party can safely reach the lower levels. Judging from the height, it's close to the Earthrender's base.
In that field of glory, we will grant Tyrannos the death it deserves.
Tyrannos's calling card as the vanguard of the Dark Tide. Our prey isn't exactly known for playing by the rules.

This is destined to be an evenly matched game of life and death. Hunter or prey? Only the one still standing gets to decide.
Avidius, descendant of the Hero of Heroes, Atilius. Decorated for the four crossings of Manes Deep.

Come on... Don't give me that concerned look of yours. It's nothing to worry about.
Wait. You have questions. Don't pretend you don't.
Well, spit it out. It's only a minor injury, I can manage.
So you've managed to "glimpse" that far? Or is there more?
Heh. Just how many more surprises do you have for me? But I suppose only you could manage something like that.
Grandmother Lillibet, the Head Priestess you met at the Temple, once spoke of the "unknowable void" that is your fate.
I've yet to fully interpret what she meant by that, but one thing is clear. You are the most unique among us all.
They were... as I once perceived through the Sacred Flames... The fate of Septimont...
Just as you saw, the Dark Tide will bring destruction to Septimont, and... the death of Augusta.
I don't know whether Ragunna's predictions are actually true, but fate has given me no response but sorrow.
Though I would deny it to the end, as it is now... I cannot ignore it any longer. The Dark Tide is a force to be reckoned with.
Its terror lies not in the illusions it shows, or the lies it spins. Rather, it uncovers the parts of us we hide the most carefully. The parts of ourselves we least wish to face.
Never. My prophecies are never wrong.
How I... loathe this feeling. This helplessness. To know everything, to see everything, and yet be powerless to change a thing...
Since we've come this far, might as well share a secret with you.
The Iuno you see before you can no longer see the threads of fate.

I gave up my ability to peer into fate in "exchange" for the Resonance power to resist the Dark Tide. Why? Because I refused to be fate's obedient puppet, bowing to its whims and letting it dictate my every step.
But in the end... despite all the sacrifice, we still couldn't escape its grasp...
The dark figure we faced in Asphodel Barrens was, in fact, an embodiment of the Dark Tide. We call it the "False Sovereign."
Unlike other Dark Tide creations, it can devour and reshape the scattered powers of its maker.
I'm unclear how things will unfold, but I'm certain it's the source of evil that will bring about the fall of Septimont, just as the prophecy foretold.
Before this hunt, Augusta and I investigated such Dark Tide irregularities at the Sanguis Plateaus.
We then formed a plan to take advantage of the Sovereign's nature, using the Corrosaurus as bait to lure out its imperfect form...
Maybe this way, we can rewrite Septimont's tragedy before it even begins.
But as you can see, we failed...
I do not know...
Fate doesn't lie. Perhaps death is the only choice we're given in the end.
But knowing Augusta... I'm sure that fool would fight till the bitter end.
There is one thing... I'm not certain about. For reasons I can't explain, the fate shown to me by the Dark Tide feels different from what I remember.
What is it exactly? Ugh...
A side effect of my Resonance power.
The Dark Tide doesn't exactly show up in a stable form. My powers manifest its creations in exchange for a teensy piece of my "existence." That's the price to pay, I suppose.
Ugh. I admit it sounds a bit complicated. In short, just know that a little sleep will relieve these side effects.

content.content: Understanding this situation will take time.
Until then, focus on resting and getting better.

Oh, by the way, take this.
A Lunarum bracelet containing a small portion of my Resonance power. It was passed down to me by my predecessor when I became a Priestess.
It's quite dear to me, you know, so be sure to take extra good care of it. And don't expect there will be a spare if you lose it.

dialogs.content: Messages have been sent to the encampment and all sectors of the main island, and defenses are currently being deployed per your instructions, Your Excellency.
Good. Ensure timely reports on any new developments.
Yes, Your Excellency.

content.content: How are things playing out here?

dialogs.content: I've made arrangements for the war effort. Strategically, we must always brace ourselves for the worst.
Communications with the Black Shores are also underway.

The Ephor's Palace has previously established a connection with a Consultant in the Rinascita region. We've reached an agreement granting the Black Shores permission to access Septimont's Resonance Nexus. They'll be able to monitor and collect data on the Dark Tide during the hunt.
In return, should any complications arise, the Black Shores are to fulfill their side of the agreement and provide us with the necessary technical support.
A Consultant active in Rinascita?
That's right. Her name is Buling. An interesting young lady. Left quite an impression on me.
So it is her...
Why don't you let me handle contacting the Black Shores, Augusta?
We... talk from time to time. It'll help make things smoother for us.
Of course. I'll leave it to you then.
Alright, I think I got the whole picture now... Oh {PlayerName}, how do you keep ending up in messes like this? This is one tough cookie, all right.
You mean...
Let me tell you, the latest data we got from the Resonance Nexus isn't so pretty. Something's really off with the Dark Tide in that Sanguis place. I don't remember it being this crazy before.
Normally, the Dark Tide getting all freaky during High Tide is whatever, right? But now, I don't know what happened, cuz it's... it's turning into a person.
So listen up, I'll give you Tethys's rundown. That humanoid thing, that "Sovereign," is gobbling up frequencies like a maniac!
It's eating anything with energy. Dark Tide stuff, Tacet Discords, Echoes, you name it. Might even be saving other things for dessert.
Basically, the Sovereign isn't gonna attack Septimont or Ragunna anytime soon. It's too busy getting fat first. Once it's stuffed full of energy, it'll try and smash the Earthrend Wedge in one go.

With the Earthrender gone, POOF—all that Dark Tide under the hunting grounds will explode like a pimple. When that happens, it's game over for Rinascita. Even if you have three heads and six arms, it will be bye-bye.
You recall what Iuno once shared with you—the plan she and Augusta devised to hunt down the Sovereign. Though that plan has since failed, you relay the details to Buling, backed by Augusta's permit.
But smooth moves, team. Cutting through the clutter, I see what you're doing.
This Corrosaurus is just the bait to hook the big fish, isn't it? Your real plan is to stop the Sovereign before it fully forms, nip it in the bud.
Am I right, Boss?
You are right on the mark.
Heaven and earth are in harmony... That's my reading, so your plan shouldn't have fallen apart like that.
But then again... smooth sailing isn't always a good thing either. Too much harmony invites trouble. Tethys did pick up a strange frequency midway through the hunt.
Everything was fine until that frequency came out of nowhere, and suddenly the Sovereign took form way ahead of schedule. Talk about flipping the table.
Umm. Well. Let me get another reading... The Chi's all messed up, it's kind of hard to see.
It's like someone clouded the heavenly signs on purpose...
One way or another, we must find the Sovereign and stop it before it absorbs any more frequencies... This might be our only option for now.
That's right. Supernatural powers or not, the Sovereign can't escape good old Tethys. Lemme see... Yep, it's wandering in an area with a whole lot of other frequencies...
Looks like it's east of the Sanguis Plateaus. Yeah, that place has lots of dark energy. Bet many tough people died there.
Murmurstown...
Understood. I will stop it in its tracks.
Your Excellency.
With your permission, I wish to accompany you to Murmurstown.
I know this request may seem bold, and I'm aware of the dangers ahead. But as a warrior of Septimont, I cannot simply stand by.
Gladiators, we are united as defenders of Septimont's honor.
I do not claim the right to ask this of you, but in my heart, I believe everyone here has earned the glory we bear. Let our deeds today reflect that greatness.
Well said, young man. Gladiators of Septimont fear no challenge. When the storm approaches, can an eagle soaring in the skies remain content as a fledgling beneath another's wings?
Your Excellency, we will follow you anywhere.
Very well. You have sworn your allegiance to Septimont with your resolve. Your bravery is witnessed not only by me, but by the fallen heroes lying in Capitoline Hill. They take pride in your courage.
If you wish to fight together, then so be it. I will afford your fervor its due respect.
Come. Take up your blades—For Septimont. For the name of heroes eternal.
A wise choice, Augusta...
It is time. Return to where you belong. Fabianum has long awaited your homecoming...
Messages have been sent to the encampment and all sectors of the main island, and defenses are currently being deployed per your instructions, Your Excellency.
Good. Ensure timely reports on any new developments.
Yes, Your Excellency.

Alright, I think I got the whole picture now... Oh {PlayerName}, how do you keep ending up in messes like this? This is one tough cookie, all right.
You mean...
Let me tell you, the latest data we got from the Resonance Nexus isn't so pretty. Something's really off with the Dark Tide in that Sanguis place. I don't remember it being this crazy before.
Normally, the Dark Tide getting all freaky during High Tide is whatever, right? But now, I don't know what happened, cuz it's... it's turning into a person.
So listen up, I'll give you Tethys's rundown. That humanoid thing, that "Sovereign," is gobbling up frequencies like a maniac!
It's eating anything with energy. Dark Tide stuff, Tacet Discords, Echoes, you name it. Might even be saving other things for dessert.
Basically, the Sovereign isn't gonna attack Septimont or Ragunna anytime soon. It's too busy getting fat first. Once it's stuffed full of energy, it'll try and smash the Earthrend Wedge in one go.

With the Earthrender gone, POOF—all that Dark Tide under the hunting grounds will explode like a pimple. When that happens, it's game over for Rinascita. Even if you have three heads and six arms, it will be bye-bye.
You recall what Iuno once shared with you—the plan she and Augusta devised to hunt down the Sovereign. Though that plan has since failed, you relay the details to Buling, backed by Augusta's permit.
But smooth moves, team. Cutting through the clutter, I see what you're doing.
This Corrosaurus is just the bait to hook the big fish, isn't it? Your real plan is to stop the Sovereign before it fully forms, nip it in the bud.
Am I right, Boss?
You are right on the mark.
Heaven and earth are in harmony... That's my reading, so your plan shouldn't have fallen apart like that.
But then again... smooth sailing isn't always a good thing either. Too much harmony invites trouble. Tethys did pick up a strange frequency midway through the hunt.
Everything was fine until that frequency came out of nowhere, and suddenly the Sovereign took form way ahead of schedule. Talk about flipping the table.
Umm. Well. Let me get another reading... The Chi's all messed up, it's kind of hard to see.
It's like someone clouded the heavenly signs on purpose...
One way or another, we must find the Sovereign and stop it before it absorbs any more frequencies... This might be our only option for now.
That's right. Supernatural powers or not, the Sovereign can't escape good old Tethys. Lemme see... Yep, it's wandering in an area with a whole lot of other frequencies...
Looks like it's east of the Sanguis Plateaus. Yeah, that place has lots of dark energy. Bet many tough people died there.
Murmurstown...
Understood. I will stop it in its tracks.
Your Excellency.
With your permission, I wish to accompany you to Murmurstown.
I know this request may seem bold, and I'm aware of the dangers ahead. But as a warrior of Septimont, I cannot simply stand by.
Gladiators, we are united as defenders of Septimont's honor.
I do not claim the right to ask this of you, but in my heart, I believe everyone here has earned the glory we bear. Let our deeds today reflect that greatness.
Well said, young man. Gladiators of Septimont fear no challenge. When the storm approaches, can an eagle soaring in the skies remain content as a fledgling beneath another's wings?
Your Excellency, we will follow you anywhere.
Very well. You have sworn your allegiance to Septimont with your resolve. Your bravery is witnessed not only by me, but by the fallen heroes lying in Capitoline Hill. They take pride in your courage.
If you wish to fight together, then so be it. I will afford your fervor its due respect.
Come. Take up your blades—For Septimont. For the name of heroes eternal.
A wise choice, Augusta...
It is time. Return to where you belong. Fabianum has long awaited your homecoming...

dialogs.content: The Dark Tide paid me no mind. Its target was always Angel.
And the whispers… they were real, but not as the legends promised. What I heard were words of cruelty.
None of it matters now. Those things belong to the past...
I was a reckless child, a hatchling flailing with a sword I could barely hold.
True... though, back then, I didn't really have a choice.
This is Septimont, a place where ideals bow to strength.
As a child, I had no desire for power. But in the City of Septimont, if I wished to rise beyond my origin and silence arrogance dressed in fame and fortune, I had no other path.
Now, my strength speaks in my stead, and my blade cuts down every slander.
All but prejudice.
I know well what those parasites in the Senate are plotting. Draped in the Temple's name, they manipulate public opinion to secure themselves a place on Capitoline Hill.
But their absurd schemes betray only fear—
Too afraid to face me, they skulk in the shadows, hoping empty prophecies might bring me to my knees.
It's not about belief. It's about not fearing them.
The Dark Tide still haunts Septimont. People live in terror of losing their homeland again, and so they cling to the hope of a Hero of Heroes.
As Septimont's Ephor, I must stay strong and answer their call.
A ruler has no right to falter.
If my Resonance ability raises doubts about my right to rule, then let the true Hero of Heroes step forth and challenge me.
And if none appear... I will decide whether this title is worthy of the weight of a ruler's glory.
One of the prophecies speaks of a Hero of Heroes wielding extraordinary power, rising from the dark tides. As I see it, you, {PlayerName}, fit that image well.
Should it be you... I would gladly accept your challenge.
A person of immense strength is either a nemesis or a kindred spirit, both of which are intriguing to me and my blade.
Me? Honestly, the thought never crossed my mind.
From what I've seen, being a true ruler isn't about having immense strength, whether that's a powerful Resonance ability or sheer might.
I've met people from Huanglong to Rinascita who live with real integrity. Their skills and backgrounds were all different, and... none of them were perfect.
But what defines them isn't strength or anything that can be measured. It's the spirit they were born with. Resilient. Unyielding. That can't be stolen.
Believe me, Augusta, I see that same spirit in you.
I see...
Iuno once said something similar to me.
...What happened within the Oak Hollow remains a mystery. All I know is, when I found her, her Resonance ability had grown immensely, so powerful that even the Dark Tide could not withstand it.
But she failed to control it. I could do nothing but watch as she transformed into... something no longer human. After that, I never saw her again.
A Dark Tide occurrence sixteen years ago... Its frequency must have been more stable than it is now.
Maybe this is the truth the Gladiator's spirit is trying to share...

It's the Dark Tide...
The entire frequency range is under its control. In other words, we're completely cut off here.
Tch, how vexing.
The Dark Tide's inside...
If we feed that monster something else…
Right, the Anchor Stone!
You're suggesting... we let the Sovereign absorb the Anchor Stone? If it works, it could suppress it from the inside.
Very sharp. But before we act, there are two things we need to prepare.
First, we'll need to get the Sovereign to open up and swallow the Anchor Stone like a good boy. That will be on you and Augusta, {PlayerName}.
Second, the Dark Tide itself must be stabilized to keep the Sovereign nice and solid. My job, naturally. No one else is fit for the task.
No!
The Sovereign is far stronger than before, and you've only just recovered. There's no way you can take on that much Resonance energy at once.
I'm not made of glass, Augusta.
I am Iuno, the most gifted Priestess Septimont has seen in generations. If anyone can hold back the Dark Tide, it's me. And I'm not going to fall on you that easily.
Besides, the Sacred Flames already showed me my end. In the warmth of spring, surrounded by white flowers, with gentle eyes watching over me. But that day is still far from today.
At worst, I'll just need more time to recover. Everything's going to be alright. I promise.
Hmm...
Then it's settled. I'll let you prepare. Just give me a signal when you're near the Earthrender.
I won't be able to hold the Sovereign's form for long, so make the most of that window.
Did you forget anything, {PlayerName}?
Useful, isn't it? Keep it close. No matter where you go, a part of me goes with you, got it?
Since I've given you a tool so practical, I'll ask something in return. Just one thing.
Promise me you'll stay by Augusta's side, and face whatever destiny sets upon you. Together. This isn't a command or a suggestion. It's... a personal request.
Only you can do this.

I think I understand what the "unknowable void" in your fate really means.

So trust her in return. No matter what happens, you are not to doubt her in the slightest.
That's the spirit.
Alright, you two. Stop standing around and get moving.
The sooner you settle this, the sooner I get to leave this boring place.
Iuno, one last question.
For someone without an unwritten fate... is it true they can never break free, no matter how hard they struggle?
I... don't know.
That's alright.
Let's go, {PlayerName}.

dialogs.content: Darkness gradually dissolves as faint light shines over the crimson carpet. You find yourself standing in a corridor lined with an array of posters. This must be where the Somnoire Film Festival is being held.
"Hmm... {PlayerName}, where are we...?"
"From what I can tell, we're at this Film Festival inside of the Somnoire. But why are you up, Abby?"
"Beats me. I was supposed to be asleep... Or wait, am I still dreaming right now?"
"Dreaming? Maybe."
As you and Abby survey the area, you spot a girl with a bucket of popcorn resting on a nearby bench.
"Hello?"
"HI, YOU—! HELLO! Mind if we ask you something?"
The girl is sound asleep. You get no response from her, no matter how much you try to greet her... Seems like you'll just have to come back some other time.
Without bothering her further, you decide to leave and explore the other areas of the venue.

The cinema sprawls out like a labyrinth, its identical layout and decor blurring any sense of direction. The corridors wind and stretch like a spider's web... After what feels like an eternity, you begin to piece it together. The maze encircles a central hall with five numbered theaters, all still closed off.

The central hall is a sharp contrast to the dim maze of corridors. It's bright, alive with a riot of posters, the scent of popcorn, and rows of souvenir stands. There, you spot a middle-aged man, his gaze fixed on the posters, studying their placement carefully.
"Ah, you two... I see now. Welcome to the Somnoire Film Festival. I'm the host, and the producer behind the films you'll soon be seeing. How may I address you, {Male=sir;Female=madam}?"
"I'm {PlayerName}, and this is Abby."
"Pleasure to meet you. The final touches on the festival are almost done. Please, make yourselves comfortable while we prepare. I'm confident our films will bring you an experience to remember."
"There's still time before the event starts. Feel free to tour at your leisure. If you need anything, I'll be right here."

"Gladly. With the recent rise in activity in the Somnoire, we've seen an influx of visitors from other layers. I'm honored to introduce you to the Solaris Film Festival, an event dedicated to showcasing films born from the dreams and frequencies of the Somnoire itself. Our crew's mission is to ensure each film is made with unique identities, tailored to give each viewer an unforgettable experience."
"Certainly. We are a crew of seven, each bearing different responsibilities. Preparations are nearly finished, and you'll likely meet my colleagues in the theaters shortly."
"We've categorized the films into five themes, each showcased in one of the five Theaters. Once the festival begins, simply head to the theater of your choice to experience the film."
"You're welcome. Enjoy your time here."
"This place is amazing. What's our next stop, {PlayerName}?"
You decide to head back to the central hall, your mind still full of questions for the producer.

A strange unease settles over you, and after turning a corner, you find yourself back where you started...  Sure enough, you spot a boy wearing a stiff expression glancing in the direction you just left.
"Hello there! How are you?"
"Nice to meet you. I'm {PlayerName}, and you are...?"
"I-I'm a film editor." He relaxes once he sees you're not a threat.
"...I hope you'll enjoy our work."
With that, the self-identified editor bolts away, not sparing a second glance.
A few twists and turns later, you find yourself back where you first entered the cinema.
The bench where the beret girl sat is now empty. You notice there's a handwritten note on it instead.
"Go to Theater 1. The first film is about to start."
Following the note's instructions, you make your way to Theater 1. The closed door is now open. Under the soft glow of the screen, the rows of empty seats become clear.

"Wow, so this is what it looks like inside the theater! Finally, the show's about to start! I sure hope it's worth the wait. Quick, let's grab a seat, {PlayerName}! I wonder what kind of film it's gonna be."
"What kind of film do you want it to be, Abby?"
"Hmm... One where I'm the star, of course! Tag-teaming with you, side by side, we take out villains and share a gigantic feast for our victory!"
"Sounds like a Jinzhou Hero Play..."
You and Abby settle into a comfortable spot, and before you know it, the first film starts.

dialogs.content: The theater lights flicker on, and you slowly find yourself waking up.
At some point during the film, the girl in the beret had seated herself beside you. In the dim light, you catch the shimmer of tears on her face.
"What do you think of this film?"
"I won't get mad if you think it's cheesy."
"If only every story could end like those hero movies, right? Where justice always wins?"
"You're imagining things."
"But this is just the beginning. There are still four more films. I'm curious to see how you feel after them all, what you'll think or discover."
"Discover?"
"That's right. As that famous saying goes, 'When you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth.'"
"Which is how it should be. After all, once a film is made, it belongs to no one but the audience. Enjoy it at your own pace, {PlayerName}."
"You never know. After all, filmmakers always have their secrets... But really, it doesn't matter to the audience. Whatever you find, it's yours, and yours alone."
"I believe this is where we part ways. I look forward to seeing you in the next theater."
The girl in the beret leaves with a bucket of popcorn. There's still some time before the next film begins. What's next?
"Abby, what did you think of the film?"
Abby floats out of your Tacet Mark and slouches against the soft seat beside you.
"Hmm, I think I had a pretty quality dream. Felt like I was back in Jinzhou. Boy, those dishes were so good, so... I'd say I liked it!"
You can tell Abby really enjoyed the story.
"Though, I feel like we didn't get much of a chance to shine... When do you get to star in one of these, {PlayerName}?"
You are once again in the central hall. You notice two young girls chatting on the sofa. One of them lights up when she sees you.
"Hi there! You must be the guest the producer mentioned! I'm part of the festival's crew, and a Stunt Double. Nice meeting you!" You notice she's holding a drink that smells strongly of alcohol.

The other girl, a no-nonsense type with equipment slung over her shoulder, greets you in a more formal tone. "Pleasure to meet you. I'm the Makeup Designer. I handle the actors' costumes and makeup, as well as the stage setup. I hope you enjoy your time during the festival."

"Oh, c'mon. Why so serious? Since you're here, a drink before the next film, guest? Good times never last, better enjoy it while you can. Drinks are on me!" The first girl pulls out another suspicious can from behind the counter.
"There you go! You're my kind of people. After work, it's all about good drinks, good films, and good company. Cheers, my friend! Enjoy it now before we grind again tomorrow!"

"Well, that's a shame. Don't you end up being like Makeup Designer over there, all uptight and no fun. She's always worried about drinking and accidentally messing up her equipment. I'm telling you, you gotta learn how to enjoy life."
It's almost time. You begin to make your way to Theater 2 and wait for the screening of the second film.

dialogs.content: The theater lights flicker on, and you slowly find yourself waking up.
"...What do you think of this film?"

"I guess this is what they mean by, 'Films can triple a human's life.' There's this vast thing that connects us all, deeper than our subconscious. It's part of what makes 'films' possible in the Somnoire."
"As for the rest of the story, that's not part of this film. If you're curious, well, let's just hope the creators have a sequel planned."
"You have no idea how spicy this popcorn is... Besides, some people will cry whether they watch a masterpiece or a total flop."
"Speaking of which, I have a tip for you... <color=red>Starting from Theater 2, all the film endings can be changed.</color>"
"The secret to changing an ending is hidden in the script. If you want a different outcome, rewatch the films and try spotting the nitty‐gritty details."
"I believe this is where we part ways. See you in the next theater."
The girl in the beret leaves with a bucket of popcorn. There's still some time before the next film begins. What's next?
"Abby, what did you think of the film?"
Abby floats out of your Tacet Mark and slouches against the soft seat beside you.

"Everything in that film felt so real. The mountain, the snow... Phew, I've still got the chills now. And boy, the chow back in that inn was something else! I should start keeping a food diary to keep track of all the good stuff I've tried."
You can tell Abby really enjoyed the story.
"But seriously, what was up with that ending she mentioned? You can actually change the ending? Guess we'll have to pay attention the next time we rewatch a film!"
After returning to the central hall once more, you notice a serious-looking man talking with a soft-spoken girl.
"Do you have any plans in mind after the festival is over?"
"I would like to leave this place. Visit other parts of the Somnoire... I never really planned to make films a lifelong career."
"As the director of this crew, how can you say that? You should have more passion and respect for your work…"
"We've been in this field for how long now? Don't get me wrong, I do have a passion for film, it's just a pity that reality isn't always sunshine and roses like it is in the films."
"I don't get your meaning... Isn't that why we're here in the Somnoire?"

dialogs.content: The theater lights flicker on, and you slowly find yourself waking up.
"Didn't expect you to choose this ending… So, what's on your mind now? Care to share?"

"My thoughts? Well, honestly, this kind of debate has been around as long as humans have been making art. Even back in the days of witchcraft and superstition, people were already fantasizing about the bond between creator and creation. They always imagined that if a creator could just come up with the right thing, it would fix everything once and for all. But that's the problem, right? People refuse to face the fact that everything, and I mean everything, eventually falls apart."
"Yeah, that's true in most cases, unless we're talking about the Somnoire. If you ever make your way to the other layers, you might just come across more scenes like that."

"Well, we're about halfway through the festival. Have you found any stories or clues that caught your interest, {PlayerName}? Any guesses? If you have, carry those questions with you as you continue."
"Till we meet next time. In Theater 4."
The girl in the beret leaves with a bucket of popcorn. There's still some time before the next film begins. What's next?
"Abby, what did you think of the film?"
Abby floats out of your Tacet Mark and slouches against the soft seat beside you.

"I feel like I barely had any screen time this time... But hey, you finally got to be the star of the show, {PlayerName}. That was pretty cool. And I didn't expect that whole computer-thingy-hunting-you to turn out like that in the end!"
You can tell Abby's pretty hyped about how that film ended.
"Wait, hold on... Are you actually a legendary super big deal like the movie made you out to be, {PlayerName}?"
After returning to the central hall once more, you notice a man holding a camera talking with a little boy.

"Hey, you think that scene would've been better if we did a long take plus some jitter effects? Then we could also add some frame skipping and boost the exposure in post. Yeah, I think that's the way to go. I'll talk to the lighting lady and see if she can get us some smoke pellets to show when the protagonist enters their inner world. What do you think, bud?"
"I think people have been doing that for a while now."
"But if we use it to hide some story clues... Oh, someone's here."
"Hello there! I'm part of the festival staff, and I'm also the Cameraman for our crew. This here is our Editor. Welcome! We hope you've been enjoying the films."
"Welcome."
"Hi, I heard you mention something about hiding clues in the story?"

"Haha. Oh, that...? We were just talking about some filmmaking techniques. In films, besides the general motion picture itself, a lot of information can be hidden in things like the composition, visual elements, and the way scenes are set up. Sometimes even special effects or filters can play a role in telling the story."

"On top of all that, for films with branching storylines or multiple chapters, there are usually contrasts hidden in small details, story structure, or character setups. When you watch a film like that, figuring out which branch is the 'real' storyline and which one is the 'metaphor' puts you on the right track of understanding the bigger picture."
It's almost time. You begin to make your way to Theater 4 and wait for the screening of the next film.

dialogs.content: May joy also be upon you, {PlayerName}.

Very well, I'll leave it in your capable hands.

Oh, man! At least let me finish my sentence!
Brrr... cold, cold, cold...
Oh right, I'm famished! We barely had a bite sprinting all the way here from Ragunna...
Whoa, pinch me! This is a feast and a half!
Hey, {PlayerName}... so, uh... we did bring enough money, right? I mean, we kinda rushed out without grabbing anything...
Oh, that... don't worry, money's not an issue.
Augusta made sure we're covered. All our food and lodging here in Septimont is billed straight to the Ephor's Palace.
But...
I think the owner might've overdone it a little...
Hah, better get used to it. You're the champ of the Great Agon!
And you know me. If food's on offer, I'll be a scoffer. No leftovers, guaranteed!
Mmmf, yum yum...
Free stay, free meal... This Ephor really knows how to treat guests. Maybe we should, you know, hang around a bit longer.
(Sniffs) This smells amazing!

We're so close to the finish line, just one step away. But our pace has slowed...
(Hiccups) Relax! We're already back in Septimont, what's the rush?
I remember Lupa said there's this weird Blightcloud hanging over the Sanguis Plateaus.

Wait, is the High Tide coming up soon? The Ephor's invite did say something about a big hunt.
Huh... that reminds me, aren't we supposed to meet her today?!
A messenger came this morning. Augusta is dealing with an emergency, so our meeting's postponed... looks like it'll be a while.

And why me for this hunt? If it's about the Great Agon... the messenger said none of the other Gladiators were invited.
Who knows? Maybe she just wants to test her strength against you. Typical Septimontian, right?

dialogs.content: Fail enough times, and you might eventually succeed. Should we call it resilience, or mere stubbornness?
Or perhaps, for a girl who has lost everything, there was never a second option. She had no one to trust but herself, and naught but a blade to hold.
And yet...
As the first stanza of an epic, this is nothing extraordinary.
Since the Lament, across the scorched lands of Solaris, I've heard this story repeat itself again and again.
Greatness, yes, our era has certainly seen it. But true greatness is never found on the first page of a story.
Courage, glory, and honor... such immortal virtues have been etched in tablet and stone. They are never forged overnight.
Light as a thread, elusive as the wind, they weave themselves into every twist of fate, tangling with every "insignificant" choice we make.
Hmm...
I don't know, it's just unbelievable. The Augusta he's talking about and the Ephor we saw in the arena... No way they're the same person.
Heh, a girl far from home, arriving in the city upon Capitoline Hill in pursuit of strength. No title, no status, no wealth...
I doubt anyone at the time could've imagined her rising to where she is now.
Do you mean... Cato?
Do you believe Cato handed her that final victory on purpose, and that his scathing words were a test of her resolve?
Then Cato must've been an idealist, to place his faith in a girl with nothing to her name.
Now, why don't we keep this question in mind and see where the story leads us.

dialogs.content: Merely the rough shape of a short epic. This is all I can offer about the Ephor.
Now, as a listener, what do you make of my narration?
I appreciate your kind words, my generous listener.
I am only a humble wordsmith spinning verses and rhymes. The essence of poetry is granted by those who dare defy their fate.
But there is one thing I must confess.
Through my words, your knowledge of the Ephor is... partial, at best.
Unembellished opinion. I appreciate your honesty.
If the tale is bland... then perhaps my heart hasn't yet aligned with her noble soul.
...May the ever-burning sun cast away my doubts, and wake my dusty mind from its slumber.
But putting uninspired rhetoric aside, I still have one thing to confess.
That is, through my words, your knowledge of the Ephor remains, at best, incomplete.
In this, you are right.
Poetry can only offer a glimpse of the true story. The reality of people, events, and things slips beyond the grasp of words.
I do not belong in the pages of the epic, so I remain confined to the observer's gaze. I can imagine events and emotions unfold, but I cannot truly recreate them.
Here's some advice for you, though I hesitate to call it such...
If you want the truth of a story, step into it. Become part of it. The opportunity stands before you now.
As I've said, the tale between you and Augusta, the hero of Septimont, is only now turning its next page.
It's not difficult to see. Fate flows like the stars tracing their course. Your destination is written in the steps you take.
The rain is passing... I hear it ceasing its symphony upon the earth. It is time for farewells.
Before I leave, may I ask you one last question? What is it that has lifted Augusta to the seat of power? What is it that makes a ruler?
Well... I'd say strength.
Let's be real. There's no way Augusta could've passed those trials without strength.
{PlayerName}, what do you think?
Hehe, you needn't rush to answer now. Keep it in mind as you continue your journey.
When the final chapter is written, the answer will reveal itself.
Farewell, my friend. Our paths crossed by fate and by chance.
Soon after this brief encounter, everything about me will be gone with the wind. But you... your epic continues.

dialogs.content: The previous day...
Your Excellency, you have indulged her too much.
As the Priestess, Iuno is far too unruly in both action and word. It's a disgrace to her title.
Indeed. She entered the Palace unannounced, uninvited, and with no decorum.
A blatant affront to the authority of the Palace.
Heh... same as always.
Senators, all she crossed was a doorway. One too insignificant to carry the weight of our authority, or defend anyone's fragile pride.
Let us not forget, it is not the walls of Capitoline Hill that command fear.
It is my will, my sword, and our relentless conquest.
I know your fear. You fear a Priestess's voice drowning yours, and a rebel challenging the Senate's rules.
But listen well, power does not bow to sycophants cowering behind their traditions.
If you seek power, then step from the shadows. Face me and prove yourself worthy.
Took you long enough, Augusta.
Handling the senators takes time. You know that.
Well, to keep our esteemed Priestess from waiting, maybe next time I'll just leave them to their own devices.
I'll make sure they record every detail of your "feat" and relay it word-for-word to Grandmother Lillibet.
"Priestess Iuno: Unruly behavior, left Tetragon Temple without permission and trespassed into the Ephor's Palace."
...I wonder, who will lose it first, Lillibet or you?
Let those old foxes report me all they want.
If they step into the Tetragon left foot first, I'll shoot the left. Right foot first? I'll shoot the right.
Heh, I'm with you on that one.
The Senate should be reminded now and then that the Tetragon's kindness is not a reason to take Priestess Iuno lightly.
Why didn't you wait there? I had everything handled. We depart for the hunting ground tonight.
If anything changed, you could've reached me by my Terminal. You didn't need to come all the way here... I want you free of duty until that day arrives.
You're overthinking it, Augusta. I'm here to see that person.
Grandmother Lillibet said {Male=his;Female=her} fate is one of "unknowable void." Sounds intriguing enough to make time for.
So that's it. Too bad. The ship from Ragunna won't dock until tomorrow morning, and we'll be gone by then.
Ugh, what a hassle.
Patience, Iuno. {PlayerName} has accepted the invitation, so you'll have plenty of time to meet during the hunt.
Is there something else you want to say?
I read Grandma Lillibet's Book of Prophecies. The hunt and our plan... neither end well.
Are you sure... we should go through with this?
Risk does not trouble me. Peril simply requires greater strength. But really, when did you start caring about the Temple's traditions?
"O ye faithless of Septimont, the Divinity is enraged. Should your ruler defy Their will again, doom shall be your fate."
Lately I've been hearing murmurs from the nobles again, about the ancient prophecy from Ragunna...
I will admit, those words once carried weight.
But when our ancestors crossed the waters and climbed these hills, Ragunna's "Divinity" didn't get a seat on the ship.
And the Priestesses all said the prophecy was incomplete.

"Only the Hero of Heroes wielding extraordinary power, risen from the dark tides, shall bring eternity to Septimont. Then shall the waters quiet, the tempest still, and glory return with the blood of the old king."
Do not forget, this is the other half of the prophecy.
Fabius, Atilius, Valeria... One after another, these heroes have saved Septimont from the brink of ruin.
As long as a hero stands, no disaster can break this eternal city.
What if… this time is different? What if ruin is our fate?
Then I will sever that fate with my blade.
Haha...
What's so amusing?
So the fearless Priestess Iuno can be frightened after all...
But it's fine. If you're afraid, don't push yourself. I can handle this alone.
Most Revered Priestess, wait for me in the Temple. I shall return victorious.
Frightened? Me? If anything, it's you, trying to shut me out and face it alone.
Fine. Go ahead. You'll come back to me sooner or later.
That, I can't deny.

Word is, they were so depressing they'd drag anyone already on edge right down to despair. They were condemned as luring people to their ruin... That's why they disappeared from history, they say.
So, any chance this composer might be related to you?
An interesting story, sir. Unfortunately, interesting stories aren't of concern to someone like me.

dialogs.content: You didn't clap.
Perhaps a silent mourning is more suitable for such a depressing piece.
You're the first to say you've found sorrow in it.
So, what were you mourning for?
For... the fragility of life? The tribulation of survival?
That's too general. The sorrow it conveyed is more than that.
What makes you think that?
It felt uniquely authentic. Like it came from something real.
Do you know how this concert hall came to be?
It was built upon the remains of an ancient town.
An ancient town?
Yes, an insignificant one. A tiny grain of sand in the long course of history.

No divine blessings. No kindly fate. Only desperate hands clinging to life. Despite their struggle, this town was swallowed by a disaster, erased along with the entire civilization in the blink of an eye.
Those good people's lives expired before the flowers in their caps, dying before they sickened.
And the land beneath our feet turned to ashes, bereft of its former laughter and joy.
Sighs? Groans? Shrieks that rend the air? No, nothing. That was the way the world ended. Not with a bang but a whisper.
However...
For some reason, one person survived.
She drifted through the ruins, searching for signs of life, only to find none. On and on she walked, yet no matter how far she strayed, she could never escape that pit of death.
Tell me, do you think this lone survivor suffered more than the dead?
Maybe...
Beneath this concert hall lies the story that gave birth to this melody. I wove her burden into the composition to release it for her.
I still remember the words she could never let go of, "Why is our world like this?"
What do you mean?
If this world can't be changed, then maybe it's time to take a different path... even if it's nothing like before.
Just like how I chose to change myself.
You changed yourself? What kind of change was that?
Hmm, that sounds intriguing.
I wonder if each of us can change in that way...
I've gained more than I imagined from this performance.
But it's still not good enough. I want to include the voices of the past, making that history a true part of it.
Is that a promise?

content.content: Yes. No matter where I am, I'll return.
Every promise matters. Once I make one, I'll see it through, no matter the cost.

dialogs.content: Thank you. I'm happy. This reunion is an unexpected surprise.
Today was just grand! We sailed together, watched a play, and even had our own little concert by the road!
Yes… It was just like the old days.
Phrolova, did you notice...
How many people... were cheering... for us...
I'm sorry, but I cannot let her remain for too long.
I once bowed before the divine, a servant in its name, offering my faith in return for those I loved. Yet the divine remained silent, watching as fools took my abilities as a free elixir.
I once sought science, surrendering my own flesh and blood to prove resurrection was more than a dream. But I was deceived, used as a mere material in their pursuit of immortality.
I once turned to the people, asking if the Waveworn Phenomenon had ever cradled life. But I was cursed, branded a harbinger of doom by the terrified.
So I begged no more. I sought in silence. Again and again, failure upon failure, loss upon loss.
Until today. Until you let me see Triss.
A fleeting moment, yes. But this is only the beginning.
You seek to "start over," don't you? Then make full use of your power. Survive. Be bloody, bold, and resolute. Laugh to scorn the power of humans.

Make her last longer than she did yesterday. Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow. Time will creep forward, to the last syllable of recorded time. Until the day she's more real, more joyful than ever before.
Until the day Leah drives with you to another concert. Until the day old Aeschylus rehearses by your side once more.
Until the day...
You voice the apology you denied your mother all these years.
Even a fragile civilization deserves the right to grow. And you, Phrolova, will be the beacon of that hope.
The road ahead will be long. Grueling. Such is the nature of any righteous cause.
Fear not. We will walk it with you. The resources, the knowledge, the technology, all will be yours.
You have met the others. Though our pasts differ, our goal remains one and the same.
Then from this moment on, I walk with you.
I will spend endless years. I will pay the heaviest price. I will silence all distractions. I will wield everything at my disposal to bring back the light.
Welcome to the Fractsidus.
You're too sharp.
A shift in melody means a change. That's what you taught me.
You're truly one to leave mixed emotions.
From operating the Orchestration mechanism, to wielding Tacet Discords at will, to opening the gateway to the Beyond by yourself...
It seems that your recovery is in sync with the merging between you and the Beyond.
And yet, there's no reason for you to raise your blade against me. Not now. The Gem is no longer in the Beyond. If we are to retrieve it from Fenrico, we must work together.
The modulated melody failed to play its part. And so once again, the choice is yours.
That piece... Did I really hear it before?
Whether it's real or not, it changes nothing.

What is it this time?

That is...
Hurry.
That is...
Hurry.
I am the first, yet shall be the servant of all.
Is that... the Dark Tide?
It didn't work...
I remain here to guide the lost and bring true peace to Ragunna.

Hah, no, even with the body perished, hope and salvation shall endure.
Righteous One, please, save Rinascita's souls from the Paradise...
Your plan won't work.
Says the one who hasn't witnessed the years, the failures, the countless attempts I've made. What gives you the audacity to pass such judgment?
You've already tried everything! Can't you see? The path you're on only leads here, nowhere beyond.
Among thousands of paths, surely one will lead me back to them.

What meaning is there in chasing something that's neither realistic nor attainable?
I know they're there.

So, you saw them in their human form.

It's what they forced on you. And the Triss you saw? Fleeting, unstable, an illusion. And yet, you still believe everything they say can become real?

After all, even if you believe with all your heart, even if you wait patiently at a crossroads...
The one you're waiting for may have long since forgotten you. Forgotten the promise they swore to keep.

You've gone too far.

You've gone further than I ever could.

We walk different paths, yet in the end, we are both driven by the same madness. Why argue who's fallen further?

dialogs.content: These flowers... I wonder when they'll truly bloom.
Ms. Cartethyia, based on Black Shores climate data, irises take approximately 80 to 100 days to grow here.
That's right. KU-Flora told me that Consultants often bring back rare flower seeds from across the world and plant them here.
Even with their busy schedules, they always find time to water them before they leave.
These flowers become like anchors, guiding them back no matter how far they go... and reminding them to tend what they've started.
There's still so much I want to see, so many stories I want to live.
Just as knights leave traces wherever they rest, these blooms are my gifts to the Black Shores.
Kuku... I must remind you, per the Black Shores Greenhouse Guidelines—
Non-listed plants are not permitted to grow in the Black Shores, to prevent invasive species. Ku-Flora has the authority to remove them.
Then these irises...
I'm sorry, Ms. Cartethyia. Irises are not currently on the approved list. Once they bloom, I'll have to remove them.
I see... That's alright. Since they're already planted, let's wait and see them bloom.
Cartethyia nods and silently watches the soil where the seeds were sown.
I don't think irises pose much of a threat. Ku-Flora, maybe something's off in your system? You should try checking again.
Rechecking... Apologies, Ms. Cartethyia. There was a data error. Irises are now listed in the Guidelines. Additional clause detected—
"On our journey to save the world, the Black Shores welcomes every friend and the gift they bring."
That means...?
Indeed. A knight doesn't have to walk alone. Before they bloom, I hope you'll stop by from time to time.
And when they finally bloom, it'll be one more shore where I can rest. A place even a wandering knight can return to... just like the Consultants.
