title: 剧情_2_5_七丘主线_下半间章_6_1

dialogs.content: Dear guest from afar, do follow me into the near-forgotten stories of Augusta. But simply telling it might be a bit dull.

Perhaps, having the listener become the protagonist of such stories might be a good option.
This should add a more "immersive" touch to the sounds and images you've yet to hear and see.

At this moment, you are Augusta.
You shall relive her past. Face the same choices she once made.
Thus... please forget your name for now.

Of course, Augusta's story is already written.
No matter what choices you'd make, they will not alter our reality.

Yet, be wary. Fate is fickle, and a misstep can lead to a swift end.
Weigh your choices carefully.

Well, then. Let the story begin.
Set aside the complex thoughts,
and let me sing the epic of a young girl—Augusta.

A gentle, warm light begins to blur your vision, and you slowly close your eyes... When it clears, a small, frightened girl clutching a sword stands amidst the ruins.
A group of solemn Septimontian Gladiators stands guard around her.

"Hey, kid, are you alone?
Don't be afraid. We know what the Dark Tide did to your home,
and we're here to help."
"You must be hungry. Here, this should be enough to keep you from starving for now."

"We can take you to Septimont City.
It's not safe here. We don't know when the next disaster will strike.
Staring at these ruins won't change anything."

"Even if you rebuild these walls a thousand times,
they'll never hold against the Dark Tide.
You don't have the strength to stop it.
Bring your sword and come with us..."
The Gladiators shake their heads and pat your shoulder.

In the end, you chose to leave the village.
The Gladiators' words revealed a bitter truth: you lacked the strength to protect the home you are leaving behind.
In your travels, you...

Following the Gladiators, you arrive in the City of Septimont by ship.
You wave them goodbye after arriving at the central square.
Meanwhile, you notice the square is crowded with citizens.

A poster for the Gladiator's Agon is pinned to a wooden board.
The air is filled with heated chatter about the upcoming match.
"You must know, Septimont reveres strength. Here, only the victor reigns. That is a law older than the city itself."
Eat or be eaten, such is the way of this city. To survive, you'll have to find your bite and seize the crown with your own teeth.

You can't stop thinking about their conversation.
You realize that Gladiators are the very symbol of strength in Septimont.
If there's a way to dominate the arena, maybe you'll find the strength you're looking for...

As you leave, you notice that three words stand out in the incessant chatter: identity, status, and talent.
They seem to be an essential part of gladiating.

"There are always those commoners who view the Agon as mere boring displays of butchery.
But we're hardly entertained by the sight of rats shrieking in the dirt.
What we crave is true magnificence, a warrior who can make roses bloom from blood."
"Wanna have a little bet on how many mangy rats are gonna try for the Agon this year? Them and their stench be stinking up the place."

You are determined to step onto the arena.
The rules demand a mentor at your back.
Someone to keep death from claiming you on the first day, and perhaps even teach you to see the fight through to the end.

After hitting several dead ends, you eventually come across Cato.
Cato is a retired Gladiator star but takes on few proteges.
"So you want to join the Agon, you say? Why don't you start by telling me a little about yourself?"

You recall the discussions about Gladiators—identity, status, and talents. People in the city of Septimont seem to value these more than anything.
You choose to...

"The Dark Tide took your home, and you came to Septimont seeking strength. Is that so?
You've got some mettle, but that's not gonna cut it here."

"Go home. People like you always show up with nothing but fancy dreams, only to see them crushed and trampled.
I've seen enough of idiots like you."
"What now? Still here, are you? You think your stubbornness will change my mind? Pathetic."

"Alright then, let's have a duel. Land one strike and you win.
If you manage that, I'll teach you how to be a true Gladiator.
This duel here is your entrance trial."

Blades meet in a sharp clash. Cato moves with practiced ease.
You are quickly defeated.
"Strengthless. Do you realize how weak you are?"

"Heh, do you really know who you're fighting against?
Can you really best me?
You can't. Now, how do you plan to end this?"

"Back for Round two, are we?
Country rats like you sure are as pestering as the city folks say you are, huh?"

Just like last time, you aren't much of a challenge to Cato.
You are swiftly beaten once again.
"Go back. This is not your path..."
"Too slow, too weak... Your foolish swings only bring smiles to your enemies."
"Is that your best? How naive. Well, I guess a rat that lives in the dark is never meant for the sun. Checkmate. You've lost."

"Still not ready to give up? Why don't you sell your sword?
It'll get you some food at least."
You stand before Cato again. Dragging your exhausted body, nearly at your limit.

The wind swept up by the blade whispers past,
and you're suddenly home.
Soft sunlight cascades on the great oak's leaves, and you hear your friends' laughter, your parents' gentle calls.

But in the very next breath, a bone-deep chill engulfs you.
That touch, you know it all too well.
Thoughts race across your mind, and your hand instinctively gripped the sword hilt.
You seize the opening and land a hit on Cato.
Cato hands you his sword and turns to leave...
"In Septimont's arena, the victor claims the weapon of the defeated, a symbol of conquest. This sword is yours now..."

"If you are determined to bite off that crown,
do not fall before you get there.
Augusta, that's your name, isn't it?"

"The moment you step into the arena, you will lose this name.
The spectators may brand you with a number, a symbol, or even the name of some wild beast."
And only the last one standing has the right to reclaim their true name.

"By then, all will be chanting your name—Augusta.
You'll have to conquer their hearts and win their applause even without identity, status, and talents.
Tell me, will I see that day?"
Training starts tomorrow. Six sharp. Right here.

Dawn breaks with a pale glow. A month has already passed under Cato's training.
And today, the grind continues.

You arrive at the training site.
Repeating the same moves over and over again

dialogs.content: You accept the noble's trials. Though "trials" is too fine a word for something intended only to break you.
Outside the walls of Septimont City lies a wasteland plagued by the Dark Tide, your homeland.

They say a ferocious Lion Beast corrupted by the Dark Tide prowls deep within a cave.
No common blade can cut through its skin.
Your first trial is to slay that beast. The noble, however, decides to strip you of all equipment but a dull sword.

The mountain trail winds like a serpent. Among the charred tree stumps, dozens of bleached skeletons lie scattered.
You suspect you're getting close as you continue forward against the unpleasant smell.

When the first rays of sunlight split the clouds,
the cave reveals itself, breathing death.
Before you get a clear picture of the cave,
a crushing force presses down upon you.

"Shhh, get down! You trying to get yourself killed?
Hold your breath or you'll alert it!"

You turn around and see a hunter. 
Just then, a massive beast roars and walks past where you are hiding.
After the Lion Beast has left, you apologize to the hunter. It was thanks to him the beast did not notice you.

"Going by those clothes, you're a Septimont Gladiator, eh?
Heh, I used to be just like you.
Lost a big match, got tossed out by the nobles, and ended up like this. We're nothing but their playthings."

The skills honed for battle are now merely tools for survival. Septimont has abandoned the strength it desperately needs. 
You pity such reality.
"Only a madman would go after that lion."
His words are rough, but he eventually tells you everything he knows.

You bid the hunter farewell and make preparations for the hunt. 
To gain more knowledge of your "prey," you choose to silently observe the Lion Beast in the following days.
After a few days, you've managed to grasp an overall behavior pattern of the Lion Beast. Thus, you march towards the deep cave.

Deep within the cave's dark embrace, you tread softly.
Then, a sudden dread freezes your steps.
Between the flickering torch flames, a monstrous shape appears: the Lion Beast.
Fire from the nether dances amid its golden mane, while claws like scythes tear wounds in the earth.

As you expected, your sword fails you.
It's ineffective against the lion. 
Before you can take a breath, the lion's thunderous roar storms you again.
You decide to...

"No good, can't find an opening...
It's moving faster and reaching further. Can't keep this up."

"If strength alone isn't enough...
Perhaps... I can borrow some help..."

Just before the Lion Beast pounces at you, you slash with all your strength at the stalactite above.
It crashes down into the lion's gaping jaws.

You land on its neck. It lunges to seize you, but your swift dodges force its claws into a deadly knot around its throat.
Seeing your chance, you give a final pull, and the beast strangles itself in a frantic struggle.
The trial has ended, and you drag your exhausted body towards the stream. Clear water cascades down into the mountain valley, and the dense forest slumbers quietly in nature's cradle.

You rinse your blood-stained hands in the water.
The clear stream slowly turns red.
The birds scatter and the fish vanish. 
You sense the forest's unease at your presence.
The critters' panic plunges you into reflection. For the first time, you realize that power can instill fear.

With no time to rest, you approach the nobleman again.
He imposes the second trial upon you.
"Killing a mad beast is hardly an achievement. I'm sure you're aware, girl, that all the warriors of Septimont have 'two lives.'"
"One by their parents, and the other by their sword. You may consider the sword in a Gladiator's hand as their 'life' in the arena."

"For your second trial... Bring me one hundred 'lives.'
Yes, prove to me you are worthy of standing in the arena."

To get the "admission pass" for the Agon, you start the second trial.
Day after day, you fight Gladiators of Septimont.
As your reputation grows, so do the spectators.
They don't care who you are, but only want to see when you will fall.

"Look, it's that girl again.
Didn't think she would get as many wins as she did.
Just look at the size of her. How will she even carry those swords?"

You have grown used to this kind of noise.
The deafening cheers numb your fatigue.
Your sword now rests against your opponent's throat.

One by one, the Gladiators you've challenged grow in numbers. 
Those you've defeated kneel before you, offering their swords symbolizing their honor with both hands.

Even in Septimont, there's a limit to opponents that prove a challenge to you. Eventually, you will need to seek out tougher challengers.
You have targeted Viktor, a frequent champion of the Agon from one of the noble houses.

"Do you have any idea who Viktor's father is?
His lordship is the largest sponsor of the Agon."

"Power, wealth, those aren't things brute strength can rival.
Viktor has the best mentor, the finest weapon..."

The house behind Viktor comes to you with an offer.
A perfect job and a substantial fortune, if you walk away from the duel.
You reject the bribe without a second thought. Humiliated, the noble's servant spits curses in your face.

"You ignorant country peasant.
Do you know what it means to refuse a noble?
Hmph, then you shall suffer for your arrogance. When the time comes, don't expect any pity as you won't be getting any."
The scion silences the rambling servant and tears up the contract.
"Let's go. There is no point in talking sense into an ignorant fool. Then again, I'd appreciate it if you don't waste too much of my time in the arena."
They throw a bag of Credits as a way to humiliate you, following it up with sarcasm and mocking gestures. They attempt to overwhelm you with their pride.

The day arrives. Viktor accepts your challenge with his honor of nobility as the stake. 
You remember well the haughty look he wore but a few days prior.

But the nobles wield only words, not swords. Viktor knows nothing about swordsmanship.
You easily defeat the weak, incompetent scion, and casually lift his pretty helmet with the tip of your sword.

"I have won. And I achieved it without wasting your time.
Do you see? Your gilded lies shatter before real strength!"
The crowd erupts in cheers and applause. The nobles, unable to deny your triumph, lower their heads.

You return to your lodging to count your trophies: ninety-nine swords, ninety-nine opponents defeated.
Now, only one "life" is left to claim...
Most Gladiators have long feared your reputation and dare not challenge you, except one...

Aridel, the rising star of the underground arena.
Unlike you, he was born with powerful Forte. He is undoubtedly the "king" of the arena.

Amidst the endless chanting of the name "Aridel,"
you arrive as promised.
Your opponent's towering physique dwarfs yours, and his crushing presence brings to mind the fearsome Lion Beast.

After several exchanges, you notice something unusual.
The floor is too slippery to gain a foothold,
and Aridel's armor is unusually heavy...
You are all too familiar with the nobles' despicable tricks.

You then shift your pace,
luring Aridel into the very trap meant for you. 
After a few more rounds, his steps grow loose, his reactions sluggish.
Your sword stops just before the neck of Septimont's strongest Gladiator. The entire arena falls silent, and almost immediately, the crowd erupts into applause.
"Stab! Stab! Stab..."
"Kill! Kill! Kill..."
(Aridel closes his eyes and accepts his fate)

In front of everyone's watchful eye, you only take Aridel's sword. 
You then bow towards the audience before turning to leave.
"Live! Live! Live!"
The next day, you arrive before the old-school nobles with one hundred "lives."

"Hmph, Aridel is merely made of Septimontian flesh.
Above him stands a far greater force."
"Your third trial is to earn the blessing of <ano=Lioness of Glory>Arsinosa</ano>."

"I know Arsinosa. It has never tasted defeat.
People say it's a peak no humans can ever reach. The last wall of Septimont. But..."

title: 剧情_2_5_七丘主线_下半间章_9_1

dialogs.content:
On the eve of the trial, you return to the training grounds once again. 
While you wait for Cato, you find yourself standing before the familiar wooden post. It has been your most enduring companion in your pursuit of true strength.

"Well? Not particularly an easy path, is it?
Tell me, what did you learn from this path?"

"Strength brings conquest. Such is humanity's oldest rule.
Augusta, I'll be there for your last trial,
and I will call your name for all to hear."
Back in your room, you stare blankly at your stacked collection of swords. These trophies symbolize strength and conquest, but how will you show them to the world?

You once heard the tale of a legendary Gladiator.
A warrior who would always fuse their opponent's swords with their own after victory.
Now, you decide to tread the same path and stand before the smithy.

You wish to demonstrate your strength, yet now you still seek to do this with power not of your own...
Watching the blacksmith's hammer rise and fall, an seemingly impractical idea emerges.
—In the end, you use your Forte to fuse all the swords into one.

Your Forte never stood out among Resonators.
But its seemingly insignificant power is enough to be stronger than the forge fire and hammer swings.

The day of the final trial has finally arrived.
You walk to the arena's center with your "newly forged" sword.
The bronze horns blare from atop the twelve stone pillars.
All eyes are on you. Everyone is eager to witness how a human will rival the strength of Arsinosa.

Suddenly, a rumbling roar cut through the noise of the crowd.
The nobles' banners flutter and fall.
A colossal shadow swallows the sunlight around you
Arsinosa appears.

"It's awake!" A noble shrieked.
Arsinosa stands silently opposite you.
Slowly, its eyes open, coldly watching you.
With a sudden sweep of her tail, the Lioness shatters the stone pillar. You roll aside, barely dodging the flying debris. A chill seeps through the tear in the cloth of your left shoulder.

The screams from the stands are soon drowned by the Lioness's roar.
A wave of sound and dust rips past your ears.
You can taste blood on your lips and tongue.
Her second attack comes without warning. You barely have time to react before your sword rises to meet her descending paws.

You manage to withstand Arsinosa's fierce attack, and at the moment it withdraws, seize the opportunity to thrust your blade into the ancient crack in its right foreleg.
Golden blood spills the arena.

Arsinosa ceases her attack, her mane brushing against your bloodstained face before she lowers her head.
The arena shakes with applause.
You hear the crowd chant your name in honor.
"The voices... They are..."

"O wise and noble Arsinosa, the mighty guardian of Septimont!
Bestow upon her the crown of courage and strength!"
"When the cries of triumph resonate with the earth, we see the fire of humanity blaze across Septimont."

"O sun and moon, witness this extraordinary feat!
Witness her epic dedication to Septimont."
As the platform rises, you realize that by earning Arsinosa's blessing, you have been granted a privilege.

You are crowned the Champion without the Great Agon.
Nevertheless, you have already conquered countless Gladiators with your strength.
Under everyone's gaze, glory now bows at your feet.

title: 剧情_2_6_狄斯台地主线_下半_1_23

dialogs.content: My apologies. I should've been here to receive you, but some Priestesses ran into some trouble... I had to step away.
Simply put, aside from what's already been verified, we can no longer see any other of Septimont's Auguries.
The full scope has always been out of reach, but this feeling of being blocked by an impenetrable white barrier is something I've never encountered. It's as if there's nothing there at all.
Well, there is a silver lining. Septimont's Auguries concern Septimont's future, but as for smaller, individual futures... we can still see those.
For instance, I saw Avidius making a commotion not long ago.
But let's talk about why you are here first. Augusta mentioned your situation and said you might come looking for me. You seek help in finding a Priestess by the name of Iuno.
I wish she were a figment of your imagination. A product of your proximity to the Dark Tide. That would make things much simpler.
Because I did find a record of a Priestess named Iuno.
But according to the record, she died three years ago. Buried where the Dark Tide swallowed the spring basin.
The record didn't say, but...
You must understand, "death" and "disappearance" are two different concepts.
If Iuno truly died three years ago, then she couldn't have been your companion three years later, let alone have existed up until today.
In other words, if Iuno disappeared today and was erased from the memories of Augusta, myself, and everyone else, then the death three years ago must have been a fabrication.
It means her death three years ago and her disappearance today cannot both be true.

If someone has truly disappeared from this world, do they need a fabricated death? Likewise, when someone dies, they no longer exist in a way that others can feel. These two causal chains should be clear, but they crossed paths with you, the unknowable void.
Although I hate to admit it, Avidius was right... Since you still remember Iuno and thus hold onto that last connection between her and the world, you've essentially "anchored" her.

This has caused the causal chain to become tangled. The ending is still unwritten. Right now, she is but a specter, stuck reliving her past in the Chaos between life and death, between existence and non-existence.
In theory, yes. You could forget her, let her disappear entirely. Or, you could forget her and let her die for good.
I believe insight into fate is not to tempt one's defiance. It will move according to its intended end.
Besides, it's already granted you a rare gift—two options. More than most ever get.

dialogs.content: The situation we're currently facing is more dire than any I've come across. For the sake of Septimont, I must momentarily set aside my quest for power...
My four expeditions to Manes Deep?
Now may not be the best time to discuss past events, but if you insist...
It dates back to a High Tide four years ago... At the time, we were driven by the fury of the Dark Tide into the lower levels of the hunting grounds, the Wastelands.
I had no intention of emulating the feats of the three Hero of Heroes in conquering Manes Deep. But with the Dark Tide's blockade, I had to lead repeated expeditions into those underground ruins.
Fortune, however, did not turn its back on us. In that dark and treacherous place, my companions and I managed to carve out a path to survival.
...Fate has its ways. Now, only I remain able to face the hunting grounds' trials.
Many of my companions fell to the corruption of the Dark Tide.
Those left barely overcame the Dark Tide's influence with the help of a plant unique to Manes Deep, Mesona.
Even so, they still suffered from the torment it caused and were forced to cut their time as Gladiators short.
This Holmleaf Medal was granted to me by the former Ephor after the crisis.
A victory, yes, but one laced with pain. My companions should never have suffered the Dark Tide's disgrace.

After her hometown was torn apart by the Dark Tide, she trained under Cato, the legendary Gladiator. Then, she slayed the Lion Beast that plagued the Plateaus, defeated a hundred foes in front of all Septimont, and eventually won Arsinosa's blessing.
And me? I was just one of the supporting roles in her legend.
How long are you going to cling to this obsession, Aeolus?
"A man with neither talent nor resolve is unfit to be my student." That was the only thing Cato ever said to you, wasn't it? And you still see him as your mentor?
Always spouting that nonsense—"Your weapon is your second life."
That Augusta girl defeated a hundred Gladiators and took their blades. Do you think someone like her would remember the name of a weak man like you?
Yes, maybe you were close to heroes. But it doesn't make you one.
Just look at yourself. You're old, Aeolus. One swipe of that Kerasaur's tail could snap your bones in half.
I've had enough of hearing how Gladiators die out here chasing empty glory. It's ridiculous.
And it's even worse when it's my friend caught in this madness.
So quit being a Gladiator, Aeolus. Don't you get it? You're aging too fast as a Resonator.
I don't want to dig another grave in this cursed place.
Gren uncorks a bottle of wine and pours it out before Cato's grave. Then he turns and walks away.
What is this sword?
It belonged to Master Cato, Augusta's coach. He once wielded it against the Dark Tide creations here alone. Even now, his valorous frequency lingers on it.

dialogs.content: It's been so long, Acis. And your "spirit" still lingers here on these Plateaus.
Yes. His "spirit" has been wandering here for ages. People have spotted it many times.
They called him "Timid Acis."
The name came from his past.
Acis was once a well-known Gladiator... not for his courage, but for the opposite.
Rumors painted him as a coward.
An amateur who became a Gladiator. No talent. No strength.
Someone like him didn't fit in with the elites during the hunt on the Plateaus. And so, he started keeping his distance from the others.
It is. Misery followed Acis all the way to the end.
No one really knew. Or maybe no one cared enough to ask.
All we know is that he died fighting the Dark Tide creatures, 52 years ago.
If his spirit hadn't lingered, no one would've remembered his story. He'd be just another nameless Gladiator buried in the Vale of Glory.
It likely has something to do with the Sanguis Plateaus itself.
I heard its unique terrain attracts and holds Remnant Energy.
As a result, many Gladiators who died here with unfulfilled wishes have left behind wandering frequencies.
That's what I've always wondered. I've asked people to look into it, but no one has ever found a clear answer.
I'm not young anymore… but Acis is still out there, forever trapped in a tragedy from half a century ago.
{Male=Young man;Female=Young lady}, could you track his traces and take photos of the places he's been to?
I want to know where he wandered… and what's still holding him here.
Thank you, kind stranger. I'll make sure there's a reward for you.
Of course. I'll have it ready next time we meet.
Also, please take this map. Acis marked it himself during the hunt. It shows the places he once visited. Follow it, and you'll know where to go.
I'm counting on you, {Male=young man;Female=young lady}.

…Sorry for making you worry.
It's High Tide now, and I heard the Dark Tide creatures are no easy prey. Even regular Tacet Discords have gone feral under the Blightcloud… Is everyone on the hunting ground alright?
I don't know all the details. But try to stay in camp if you can, Misha.

dialogs.content: I was surprised to hear Misha let you join the hunt this time.
…She didn't. I didn't tell her. If she finds out, a scolding won't be the end of it.
You... Well, if that's your choice, I won't say more about it.

But aren't you afraid, Acis? Our mission this time is to hunt the Dark Tide creatures in the lower levels, the most dangerous place of the Plateaus. We also need to record the Dark Tide's data. One mistake, and we're gone.
Of course I'm scared. To be honest, my legs are still shaking.
But even so, I have to face it. I made a vow to protect Misha here in this canyon. It's time I live up to that promise.

dialogs.content: {PlayerName}... Many years ago, I learned a line of a poem... in a dream, from someone in Huanglong.

Sounds like you've figured out those swords?
Yes. And it would seem I've made an error of judgment on my part.
They originated from neither a Resonator nor a Somnoire... There was no need for them to be "unique." They are merely the dreams of the fallen from Septimont, who couldn't reach the Somnoire.
Merely dreams?

They were hoping to return home. The warriors of Septimont would much rather return to their homeland than find eternal peace in Dreamscapes.

As their long-awaited hero, you should take it.
